summary: Q-54 independent verification of CR-E05 against day1.txt, plus Q-52 / Q-11 / Q-06 transcript reads and DOCKET-WATCH Run 2
logs: Q-54: 6 completeness readers over day1.txt + 8 proposition testers over CR-E05
229 candidate findings, 186 confirmations logged, from 14/14 agents
deduped 229 -> 229 (125 material). Adversarially verifying 16; 213 NOT verified and will be reported as unverified candidates, not as findings.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The exclusionary rule was invoked by the defence. On defence stipulation 'for purposes of this hearing only,' Agents Hull and Davis were permitted to remain throughout."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Accurate as far as it goes, but the court exempted two further categories in the same breath (16:06): "Of course, victim representative is excluded from that rule as is the case manager pursuant to the rules." The court had already formally recognised Erika Kirk's presence at 08:39 and stated it was "mindful of the duty to protect and uphold the constitutional rights of both Mr. Robinson and Ms. Kirk."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §6A correctly records that Erika Kirk was present throughout and never spoke; the victim-representative exemption is the mechanism that made that lawful once the exclusionary rule was invoked, and it belongs with the rule rather than sixty sections away. Small, but it closes the loop between two things the file states separately.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent. The header states the probable-cause standard as the library's own framing; the transcript's own statement of it is not recorded.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Immediately before the recess to place the monitor, and before any witness, the court admonished counsel (26:43): "I do wish to remind the parties that this is a preliminary hearing. It is a probable cause standard and if you could keep that in mind as you're presenting your evidence, this is not intended to chill what you present, but keep in mind that the standard is probable cause and that is what the court as a magistrate will be looking to."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05 correctly frames the whole file around probable cause. That the court itself set that frame on the record, unprompted, before evidence began is the primary-source anchor for the framing — and it is the same posture the court invoked again at 02:36:05 when it received the dispatch account not for its truth "sitting as a magistrate, not before a jury" (§3.4). The two are one continuous judicial stance, and the file has only the second half.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent on the hearing's announced schedule.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: At 14:59–15:21 the court set the week: "I anticipate that we will begin each morning at 9:00 AM with the exception of Wednesday and we will begin at 1:00 PM. We will take a 15-minute morning break and a 15-minute afternoon break… We will recess for lunch at noon for one hour each day with the exception of Wednesday and court will resume at 1:00 PM and continue until 5:00 PM each day."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: It is a structural fact about all five hearing days, not just Day 1, and the library's other transcript files cover the rest. Day 3 (Wednesday 2026-07-08) was scheduled as an afternoon-only sitting — which bears on any comparison of day lengths or of how much testimony each day carried, and on CR-E03, which covers Days 2, 3 and 5.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §2.1 records the portable-electronic-devices ruling. §1.3 records that Exhibit 6.1 "had already been displayed on the courtroom screen and captured by the media camera." The media camera itself is never identified, and "Wilson" and "KSL" appear zero times in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The court voir-dired the single camera operator on the record (10:16–10:54): "John Wilson, KSL News," whose stated duty was "Shooting the proceeding according to the decorum order," who confirmed he had fully reviewed the court's standing decorum order, understood its requirements, needed no further time, and anticipated no difficulty complying. The court also noted "there is no still photographer for today's proceedings pursuant to the court's ruling from last week." The subsequent monitor-placement ruling was addressed directly to him: "this is going to the camera operator, do not want them to be displayed on TV."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The "media camera" is a load-bearing entity across CR-E05 — level 3 of the three-level framework, the Exhibit 6 revision, the Exhibit 8 publication denial, and the §1.3 note that unredacted PII was captured by it. Knowing it was one pool camera, operated by a named KSL operator examined on the record under a standing decorum order, with still photography separately excluded by a prior ruling, is what lets a reader judge the actual exposure. A prior ruling from the week before Day 1 is also an acquisition target the file does not name.

not_verified_items.target_section: NEW — not in the file at all (bears on §2.1, §3.3, §7, §8 item 5)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — CR-E05 contains no reference to State v. Purcell, State v. Wager, or the prima facie foundation standard (grep of the .md: 0 hits for each). §8 item 5 records only that Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 35 were "all admitted Day 1, none held."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every scene photograph in this block was admitted over a live, argued objection, on a stated legal standard. For State's Exhibit 3 the prosecutor cited "State v. Purcell, which is a Supreme Court case here in the State of Utah, 1985… if a competent witness with personal knowledge of the facts represented in a photograph can testify that that photograph accurately represents those facts, the exhibit's admissible," giving the citation "711 Pacific 2nd 243… page number 245," and argued the burden expressly: "The showing that's required here, it's essentially a prima facie showing. We're not required to show proof beyond a reasonable doubt, for example, that it was accurate that day or even a preponderance of the evidence." For State's Exhibit 35 he added "State v. Wager… W-A-G-E-R… Utah Court of Appeals case from 2016… 372 Pacific 3rd 91," describing its facts (the foundation witness was not present when the photo was taken and could not date it, but knew the room and the defendant, and that was held sufficient). The court overruled both objections, expressly finding for Ex 3 that "the witness is familiar with the scene… the necessary foundation has been laid," and for Ex 35 that he "mentioned the roundabout and identified the buildings." These three strings occur nowhere else in day1.txt (Purcell 2, Wager 2, "prima facie" 1 — all inside this block).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05 §3.5 presents "Exhibit provenance was outside his knowledge — he does not know who took Exhibit 35, where it came from, or how old it is" as a defence-favourable cross point, without recording that the court had already ruled, on cited authority, that provenance was legally unnecessary for admission at this hearing. A careful reader of CR-E05 alone would not know what "admitted" means for the scene photographs, nor that the State litigated and won the exact point the file later frames as a defence gain. This is also the file's §0 standing rule ("a forensic report is silent about the provenance of what it examined") playing out live on the record, unrecorded.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 ("Three defence attacks") and §3.5 ("Exhibit provenance was outside his knowledge")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "A standing constitutional objection ran against every exhibit — the same Rule 1102 / Art. I §12 challenge recorded at CR-E03 §5A.2a… Day 1 is inside its scope." §3.5 records the provenance point only as cross-examination material.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: For each of the four exhibits in this block the defence made a TWO-part objection: renewal of the standing objection PLUS a fresh, exhibit-specific authentication ground, none of which is a Rule 1102 or confrontation ground. Ex 3: "we renew the standing objection. We also object again that this individual can't identify when the picture was made or how it was made or by whom." Ex 35: "renew the standing objection and object on the grounds that there's no indication on this photograph of when it was taken in terms of relation to the actual incident at issue here." Ex 3.1: "We renew our standing objection, and object on the grounds that there's no foundation laid as to when the photo was taken or by whom." Ex 3.2 adds a different ground again: "There is an evidence tag here, which begs the question that it's not a fair and accurate representation of how he saw it. And we also don't have any indication about when this picture was taken or by whom." The State answered these with photograph-authentication case law, not with Rule 1102.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file collapses a distinct, four-times-repeated authentication objection into "the same Rule 1102 / Art. I §12 challenge." That mis-scopes what the defence preserved on Day 1 as to the scene photographs, and it moves a litigated-and-ruled-on issue into the cross-examination column where it reads as unanswered. It also matters for CR-ACQ purposes: if these photographs are ever sought, the appellate posture attached to them is authentication, not confrontation.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "…immediately saw an out-of-place object about 10–15 feet in from the guardrail: a red and black screwdriver (State's Exhibit 3.1, evidence tag 5)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness testified that the evidence tag was NOT there when he found the item, i.e. the exhibit photograph postdates evidence-technician processing: "on this exhibit, Exhibit 3.1, there's an evidence tag, yellow number five. Was that present when you found the screwdriver?" — "No." The same concession was made for Exhibit 3.2: "Was that present when you were on top of the Losee Center and observed this?" — "That was not." Critically, the follow-up "So, that was left there by an evidence tech?" — "Yes" was a leading question supplying a fact the witness had no personal knowledge of; he had left the roof before the technicians worked it and never testified to seeing anyone place it.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's parenthetical "(evidence tag 5)" reads as a neutral descriptor of the exhibit. The record shows it is the opposite: it is the sworn admission that these rooftop photographs do not depict the scene as the first officer found it, and it is the express ground of the defence's Exhibit 3.2 objection. Any later use of Ex 3.1/3.2 as an image of the untouched scene would be wrong, and the file gives a reader no way to know that. The witness's "yes" to "an evidence tech" is an adopted inference, not personal knowledge — exactly the anchor/connection distinction CLAUDE.md requires be graded separately.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.3 and §7 ("The court repeatedly ruled against the State… which is itself evidence that the rulings admitting exhibits were considered rather than reflexive")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — CR-E05 records no admission colloquy for Exhibit 3.1 at all beyond the parenthetical citation in §3.3.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The court, not the defence, spotted a gap in the State's foundation and prompted the cure. After the objection the judge interjected: "And did you state that this was a fair and accurate representation as of September 10th, 2024?" The prosecutor: "I had said that day. I'll ask it again… to the officer," then re-asked with the date; the witness said yes; the court then admitted 3.1 "based off the firsthand knowledge of what this image purports to be, and is a fair and accurate representation as this item on that date of September 10th, 2025." Note also that the year is rendered as "2024" in the court's own question — a date error inside the ruling colloquy.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §7 offers "the court repeatedly ruled against the State" as the file's principal for-the-prosecution evidence that admission rulings were considered. The fuller record cuts the other way on this exhibit: the court actively assisted the State in repairing a foundation the defence had just attacked. Both facts belong in a both-directions section; recording only the first is the bias signal CLAUDE.md warns about. The "2024" rendering also belongs in §1.3 as a further instance that dates in this Rev text cannot be taken at face value.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He could see only the right side of Kirk's body under the tent; **simultaneous with the shot** Kirk leaned to the left and went down."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness never described Kirk going down, and expressly disclaimed being able to see him. His own words, twice: "I saw him lean to the left"; "I saw him go to the left because I could no longer see the right side of his body. He went further underneath the tent to the north side of the tent, so left." The word "fell" enters only through counsel's leading question — "When he fell to the left?" — answered with a bare "Yes." Immediately before, he had said: "I could see the right side of Charlie's shoulder. Not his whole body because he was underneath the tent."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the only eyewitness-to-the-victim testimony in the block, and the file states as observation something the witness described as a loss of line of sight. "Went down" implies an observation he affirmatively said he could not make. The distinction between the witness's own words and a term supplied by the examiner and adopted with a monosyllable is precisely the recording-layer fidelity CLAUDE.md's prime directive protects.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "…the Losee building 'was right in my' line of sight" (§3.2); "On the southwest side he found a disturbance in the gravel" and the impression is "in the direct line of sight" (§3.3, §3.4).
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The line of sight from the roof to the tent was testified to as PARTIAL and vantage-limited, and the file records neither qualification. Q: "Is there a clear line of sight between the tent and the top of the Losee Center?" A: "Yes, there is." Q: "Is some of it obstructed?" A: "Yes." Q: "Obstructed by what?" A: "The Sorenson building that's right here, this white roof this kind of obstructs a little bit of the view of the courtyard." Then: "Where would you have to be standing or perhaps lying down on the Losee Center to see into the courtyard where that tent was?" A: "On the far south side of the Losee building, you could have a line of sight towards the courtyard." The tent itself is not visible in State's Exhibit 3 at all — "You cannot. In this picture, you can't." Note also that "or perhaps lying down" was supplied by the prosecutor, not the witness.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: It cuts both ways and the file records neither direction. It narrows the possible vantage to the far south edge of the top roof — which tends to support the State — while simultaneously establishing that the sight line is obstructed in part by the Sorenson building, which is an evidentiary limit a reader would want. And the prone framing entered the record from counsel roughly an hour of stream time before the witness offered "it looks like a sniper pad" — context the file's own careful flagging of that phrase (§3.3, §6) is incomplete without.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The rooftop was restricted**, reachable by an outside public stairway and a low guardrail (§3.3)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The compression runs toward the State on the access question. The stairway is affirmatively public — Q: "Is that open to the public?" A: "It is." The barrier is "a little handrail, like a little guardrail, probably about a couple feet high that somebody could jump over." And the "restriction" is not a lock, sign, fence or posted prohibition: Q: "Is that area restricted? Is it off limits?" A: "Yes, it is. **There's a natural barrier with the guardrail. And from there on, there's no path. It's gravel roof, so it's not paved like everything else.**" Q: "But someone could hop over that railway?" A: "Yes."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Stated flatly as "the rooftop was restricted" in a section headed "Confirms," a careful reader takes it as a formal restriction that someone breached. The witness's own account is that the restriction consisted of a two-foot rail, the absence of a paved path, and gravel underfoot, at the top of a stairway open to the public. Given the Losee building is a named physical/forensic question for this library, the character and height of the barrier is load-bearing, and the file's compression is an unwarranted assertion in the State's direction — hazard 4 in the other polarity.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.4 ("The camera system, **the route**, and the northeast drop") — NEW subsection needed
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — 0 hits in the .md for horseshoe, 800 South, 850 South, 600 West, 720, 925.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On State's Exhibit 35 the State laid a full street framework for the neighbourhood north and east of campus: 800 South ("the long straight road… at the top of the photo"), 850 South (running east–west, "the middle of that horseshoe"), 600 West ("the far right side of the horseshoe," north–south), 720 West ("to the left side of the horseshoe… runs north and south") and 925 South ("on the bottom of the horseshoe that connects those other two Wests"). ⚠ The witness's own summary then names a different street: "On the left side is **725 West** of the horseshoe." Both strings occur exactly once each in the whole of day1.txt, both inside this block, so the record contains an unreconciled 720/725 West discrepancy.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the State's geographic foundation for the area the person on the roof was seen to run toward — §3.4 itself records the "drop off the northeast side." A reader of CR-E05 has the escape direction but none of the street framework the State put in evidence to support it. And the 720/725 inconsistency is exactly the kind of number a later reader mapping the route would carry forward wrongly; whether it is the witness's slip or a Rev mis-rendering is not resolvable from this text and should be flagged as unresolved.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — 0 hits for "parking structure," "tunnel," "Heat Plant," "Campus Drive."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State elicited a detailed pedestrian and vehicle route from the parking structure to the Losee Center. Vehicles "enter and exit right here on the north side of the parking structure… into level one." On foot: "If they were to park into this LDS Institute parking lot… there's a tunnel that goes underneath the road that still comes out into the parking structure itself. And then they can exit out here on the second level onto Heat Plant Road… They can exit there and go back towards Campus Drive. So you could walk out either up here on the northeast side of the parking structure and cross over to the LDS Institute. Or you can come out here to the southeast side and you can exit there and walk down to the courtyard or **behind the LDS Institute building towards the Losee Center**." Campus Drive was separately described as running from the top-left "almost like a T," past the Institute building and structure, "all the way around campus" back to the roundabout.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §3.4's heading promises "the route" but records only the escape side (the northeast drop). This is the approach side — the State building, through a foundation witness, a walkable path from a public parking structure to the Losee Center, including an underground tunnel. A careful reader of CR-E05 alone would not know the State put an approach route in evidence on Day 1, nor that the physical connectivity of the parking structure to the Losee is on the record.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.3 ("Other rendering hazards") — and it bears on all of §3.1–§3.4
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — §1.3 lists label breakage, timestamps, garbled names and two missing conferences, but not this.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The court stopped the examination to put on the record that the proceeding is audio-only and that pointing does not survive: "Mr. Grunander, let me stop you just for the benefit of the record because the record is picking up the audio. When you're pointing it to… as you're identifying, indicate the general location on it, the left side, right side, middle, upper, lower, just so the record knows to some degree where you're pointing. In that way, **because the video isn't being captured.**" The prosecutor: "Understood. That's fair." Everything that follows — the whole of the Ex 2, 3 and 35 identification testimony, and the screwdriver's location on Ex 2 — is the witness's verbal gloss on a gesture no record preserves.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is a first-order access-path caveat and the court itself stated it. Roughly an hour of the block consists of "right here," "just over that," "about right there" tethered to a photograph the library does not hold (§8 item 5, §9.1). It is the reason none of the pointing testimony can be independently checked without the exhibits, and it should sit in §1.3 alongside the label breakage rather than being absent.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The rifle is never recovered, described forensically, or photographed** in this record. The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged '**long black object**' (§3.4)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The second sentence is false on this block alone, and on CR-E05's own content. This block contains sustained testimony distinguishing firearm types by sound — "a handgun is more of a short bang pop sound. With a rifle, you have more of a longer violent bang or crackle sound" — a direct assertion "That was a rifle shot" (agreed to by Chief Long), and an **empty pistol holster** observed on the courtyard grass. The file itself elsewhere records the holster (§3.2), Kirk's armed private security and Utah's open-carry status (§3.5).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §6A is the file's scoped-nulls section, where precision is the entire product, and a false absolute there discredits the nulls that are correct (I confirmed all eight zero-occurrence terms whole-file with a validated positive control). If the intended claim is "the only reference to *the rifle*," it needs saying; as written it contradicts §3.2 and §3.5 of the same file.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §7: "Bagley's account is first-hand and internally consistent — he heard the shot, inferred a rifle from its sound and the holster's presence, **reasoned to the Losee building before any camera evidence**." §3.1 records only the radio call and "Oh, that was kind of fast."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The chain of inference had a wrong first link that the file omits. On being told a shooter was in custody, the witness reasoned to a close-range handgun: "I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody. I thought at that moment I was like, 'Oh, that was kind of fast.' **Obviously it was close range probably because we had an individual in custody.**" He held that reading through the injury canvass and only abandoned it on seeing the empty holster: "I realized that the shot I heard was more of a rifle shot and not a pistol shot." (The cross confirms this at line 5527: "I thought we had a suspect in custody, so to me it would be a close encounter.")
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §7 presents a clean, unbroken inferential chain as the strongest for-the-prosecution feature of this witness. The record shows the officer's first operating theory — driven by the wrong-person detention the file itself lists as defence-favourable — was close-range handgun fire, and that it was wrong. That is the concrete mechanism by which the erroneous custody report shaped the initial reading of the scene, and it belongs in the both-directions section as a qualification on the file's own headline.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Route: into the Sorenson Center, up four flights to the Losee fourth level…" — no other description of the building's vertical geometry appears in the file (0 hits for "stories" or "atrium").
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The Losee building's geometry was established in detail, with an internal inconsistency. Q: "How many stories does the Losee building have?" A: "There's four." Later, on Ex 3, he said it has "the four or five floors that are sitting right there," then enumerated: level one at courtyard/ground level with an elevator; "Level two would be the second one where these red ATVs are sitting on the grass"; the third; "and your fourth level, which is the actual top level of the building is that very top one with the windows." On top there is "an atrium… it's got a little sphere on the top of it. It looks like a little square right on top of the Losee building." The two gravel shades were also specified: lighter gray where the atrium is; "on the west side, there's two ventilations for the Losee building, two vents on top of that. It's in the darker gray gravel."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The Losee building's physical configuration is a named forensic question for this library, and the file carries only "four flights." The roof furniture (atrium structure, two vents on the west side), the two gravel zones, and the witness's own "four" / "four or five" wobble are all things a careful reader would want before reasoning about sight lines, cover, or the position of the gravel impression the file discusses in the same section.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 35 — the scene photographs, all admitted Day 1, none held." No description of what any of them depicts (0 hits for "Exhibit 3.2" in the .md body).
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: State's Exhibit 3.2 is the line-of-sight exhibit and the file does not say so: "that's a picture of the top of the Losee building, looking west… We're looking west towards Utah Lake." From it the witness could see the courtyard ("Yes, a little bit"), the tent Kirk was under, and the Hall of Flags. He authenticated it by landmark — "The Fugal building's on the top left… on the right, is a white roof, which is the Sorensen building… There's also the gravel area on top of the Losee building." By contrast State's Exhibit 3 is "a drone picture of the campus, more of the courtyard looking eastward" in which the tent is NOT visible, and State's Exhibit 35 is "an aerial view of the campus and the northeast area, just north of the campus neighborhoods."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §8 lists these as acquisition targets with no indication of which one answers which question. Ex 3.2 is the only photograph in evidence taken from the rooftop toward the courtyard — it is the artifact that would test the partial-obstruction testimony directly. Without a one-line content note per exhibit, a later acquisition run cannot prioritise, and the file's own line-of-sight discussion has no named artifact behind it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "A three-level framework for every exhibit… **(1) admission into evidence; (2) publication to the courtroom; (3) publication capturable by the media camera.** Absent a specific objection to level 3, **the court treated level 2 as carrying it.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The three tiers are stated correctly, but the default rule is not what the court announced. The court's words: "There's basically three levels of objections that could be objected to. First, the admittance of the exhibit itself, second is the publication of the exhibit **to the gallery**, and third is the publication which is electronically captured by the media… **If no objection to the publication media capture of the exhibit is specifically raised, the court will presume there's no objection.**" That is a waiver-by-silence presumption placed on counsel, not a rule that granting level 2 carries level 3. Delivered in the same passage, and absent from CR-E05, is the court's Article I §28 clarification that victims and victims' representatives "are entitled to be treated with dignity and respect, that if they choose to leave the courtroom, they can come back whenever they wish. They're not prohibited to coming back solely at the break."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file says this framework "governs the whole hearing" and that CR-E04's "admitted but not published" finding "sits inside" it, so its exact terms matter downstream. A presumption of no objection allocates the burden to counsel and is what a reader must know to interpret any silent record; "level 2 carries level 3" is a different rule with the same practical effect only where counsel says nothing.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: He ran down the outside stairs "**jumping over people lying on the steps**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: That string does not appear in the transcript; it is a composite of two separate clauses presented inside quotation marks. The actual testimony: "As I was trying to get down to the bottom of the stairs, people were running up, **people were laying down on the steps. I'm trying to jump over people** to get to the bottom of the stairs so I can help stop an individual that's probably shooting."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The substance is faithful, so the picture is not wrong — but the quotation marks are. CLAUDE.md's recording layer is defined by fidelity to the words, and a composite inside quotation marks is the failure mode that standing hazard 7 names. Also lost is the clause stating his purpose in descending: "so I can help stop an individual that's probably shooting."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Timestamps are recording-stream time, not time of day**, and the clock jumps across each recess… They are **identifiers**. Day 1's stream begins at 06:57 with the call to order."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Three things this block supplies that §1.3 does not. (1) An on-record wall-clock anchor stated by the judge: "So, 10:43. Let's go ahead and come back… Around 10:44. Let's come back at 11 o'clock and then we'll resume direct examination" — spoken at stream 01:45:47. (2) The timestamps are non-monotonic and repeated WITHIN the recess, not merely jumped across it: a block labelled 01:49:21 contains inline "[inaudible 01:46:00]"; 01:52:00 heads four consecutive turns; 01:57:23 heads three; "All rise, court is back in session" carries 01:59:16 and the judge's "Please be seated" carries 02:08:08. (3) Two part-seams with words duplicated on both sides: at 01:41:58/01:42:00 the phrase "the empty holster. I turned to my chief and I said, 'That was a" appears twice under the same label; at 02:15:52/02:16:00 "which begs the question that it's not a fair and accurate representation" is repeated across a seam in defence counsel's objection.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The clock anchor is a genuinely checkable datum the file lacks — stated by the court, not derived by conversion, so it does not breach the no-conversion rule. The non-monotonic timestamps and the duplicated part-seams are concrete evidence for a hazard the file currently asserts abstractly; a later verifier quoting across a seam would otherwise double a phrase and not know why.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.5 records only that they "'had an idea' thousands would attend"; the file states no observed crowd figure, and says nothing about the injury canvass.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two facts about the immediate aftermath. Crowd size, with the basis stated: "I'd say there was several thousand people because you had it on the grass that was jam packed. In the amphitheater sitting on the grass you had people standing on the back up along the cement. You had people that were on the second level, the Sorenson and over by the Woodbury Building." And the injury canvass: he found one youth on the grass near a wheelchair "almost convulsing," thought he had been shot, was told by the accompanying parent it was a seizure and that he was uninjured, "and then at that moment I observed that there was no other injuries that I could see at that moment." (No identifying detail about either private individual appears in the transcript or need be recorded.)
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Numbers are on the materiality list, and expectation ("had an idea thousands would attend," a planning point on cross) is a different claim from observation ("several thousand" present). The canvass is the only first-responder testimony in this block about whether anyone besides Kirk was hurt, and it is a negative finding by the officer who looked — the kind of scoped observation this project treats as evidence.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §1.3 records that Exhibit 6.1 "had already been displayed on the courtroom screen and captured by the media camera before the publication framework was clarified," and §2.1 records the 01:04:49 lectern live-stream failure.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: There is a third instance in this block, and this time the court caught it prospectively. After the State asked "if we can publish that on the witness's screen" for the unadmitted Exhibit 35, the judge interjected: "Thank you, Mr. Grunander. I was just going to mention that **we shouldn't display it until it's been admitted in.**" The exhibit was then shown to the witness's monitor only.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file develops display-before-admission as a Day 1 theme across two incidents; this is the third and the only one where the court stated the rule prospectively rather than reacting to a breach. It also shows the sequence the court expected (witness monitor only, then admission, then publication), which is the practical content of level 1 in the three-level framework.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The garble list names "David Sterk"/Sturgill, Falmina/Faumuina, Elschultz, Cam Nelson/Ken Nielsen, "Erica Kirk," "Mr. Cook's presentation," "Bayliff." Defence counsel is written "Kathy Nestor" in the §1.2 table without comment.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Rev's speaker label reads "Kathy Nestor" (12 occurrences in this block) while the court addresses her from the bench as "Ms. Nester" five times — e.g. "Thank you, Ms. Nester. Mr. Grunander"; "Ms. Nester, anything else you wish to add?"; "Ms. Nester?" The transcript also renders the same building "Sorenson" and "Sorensen" within two hours of stream.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.3's rule is that "no name in this file should be treated as verified orthography," and the file maintains an explicit list. The label/bench divergence for the defence attorney who makes every objection in this block is exactly the kind of item that list exists to hold, and the file currently uses the label spelling in its most-cited table without flagging it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**No briefing, no debrief, no meeting** that morning; he does not know whether any security meeting occurred; **no operational or tactical plan, no written materials.**" The file gives no reason, and §3.1 says only that he was "posted at the south end of the Hall of Flags."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Bagley explained WHY there was no briefing: a pre-event disturbance on top of the Hall of Flags. "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags… The Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area. I got dressed and then came back and then went to the Hall of Flags to secure that area." And again: "I don't know because when I got there, it was starting to… People were throwing stuff down on the tent." (An earlier, weaker version at 01:02:54 — "people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area" — is why he was posted there at all.) A whole-file search for /throw/ returns exactly two Bagley hits, both in this block.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05 presents "no briefing" as a bare security-posture failure. The record supplies both a cause and an independently significant security fact the file never mentions: hours before a rooftop shooting, people were on top of a building overlooking Kirk's tent throwing objects down onto it, the chief was notified, and the two on-duty officers were diverted to it. It cuts in both directions — it partially answers the defence's no-briefing point, and it establishes an elevated-position incident above the victim before the event. A reader of CR-E05 alone would not know it happened, and would not know that §3.1's own fact (his Hall of Flags posting) was a response to it.

not_verified_items.target_section: §6A ("The only reference to a weapon…") — and §3.3
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §6A: "**The rifle is never recovered, described forensically, or photographed** in this record. The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged '**long black object**' (§3.4)." §3.3 describes the gravel disturbance without mentioning any gun marker or measurement.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Describing State's Exhibit 5 (the nighttime side-profile of the prone position), Bagley testified: "You can see more of the length of an individual. So you can see that more of there's two elbows, two knee areas, plus also towards the far right of the photo is also a marker where somebody laid a gun down." — "It's like a prone position." He also identified in the same exhibit "a measuring tape, it looks like" on the roof. A whole-file search for /laid a gun|gun down/ returns exactly one hit, this one.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The §6A null is falsified inside this block. An admitted exhibit carries a crime-scene evidence marker that the witness described as marking where a gun was laid down at the prone position, with the position measured by a tape. That is directly load-bearing on two of the file's own headline items: the purposive casing search that found nothing (§3.3, §6) and the "sniper pad" characterisation the file warns readers to handle carefully. A reader of CR-E05 alone would believe Day 1 contains no photographic or forensic indication of a weapon at the perch.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 ("The nighttime rooftop photographs rest on hearsay")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Admitted over preserved objection under URE 1102 and Utah Const. Art. I §12.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State's argument was broader and cited named authority: "Under rule 1102, hearsay is admissible to establish the foundation for, or the authenticity of, any exhibit. That's found in 1102 sub B sub 3. I would also point out… under rule 1101… in subsection C1, the determination of questions of fact preliminary to admissibility of evidence when it's determined under rule 104… the rules of evidence do not apply… so even at trial, hearsay is admissible to establish the foundation of an exhibit. I would also just point the court to State v. Griffin. This is a 2016 Utah Supreme Court case. The citation is 384 Pacific Third 186…" The court then overruled, noting the standing objection, Rule 1102, and quoting Art. I §12 at length ("nothing in this constitution shall preclude the use of reliable hearsay evidence as defined by statute or rule… at any preliminary examination to determine probable cause…"), ruling "as it relates to reliable hearsay in this instance."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the legal architecture by which every hearsay-founded exhibit entered on Day 1, and CR-E05 compresses it to a two-rule citation. Two things are lost: (a) URE 1101(c)(1)/Rule 104 — the argument that the rules of evidence do not apply AT ALL to foundation questions, which is broader than 1102 and, on the State's telling, would apply at trial too; (b) State v. Griffin, 384 P.3d 186 (Utah 2016) — a named, checkable Tier 1 authority that belongs in §8 as an acquisition target and appears nowhere in the file. This also frames the Rule 1102 discussion at §4.4 and the confrontation objection at §4.4 item 1.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Asked why the mismatch with the shot's direction did not register: "**During [the chaos]…**"" — and the bullet's flat header, "**The wrong person was detained.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The full answer: "During the chaos moment, no. They said they had a person in custody. I figured those guys saw something I didn't see. They took that person in custody and I thought that was him." Nothing in this block has any speaker state that the detainee was the wrong person; the defence implies it, and Bagley's own evidence is that he deferred to the arresting officers' vantage. He did volunteer that the detention surprised him ("Yes. And that's why I was quite surprised") and that the detainee was not near the holster.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two defects in one bullet. The ellipsis truncates a complete, reasoned answer into a non-answer, on the file's most defence-favourable page — hazard 7, and hazard 4 in the direction the file elsewhere guards against. And "The wrong person was detained," stated flatly in a recording-layer bullet, is an analyst-layer characterisation no witness makes; the recorded facts are a detention within ~30 seconds near the tent, the witness's surprise, and his deference. Rewriting to quote him in full and attribute the "wrong person" framing to the defence costs the file nothing and fixes both.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.1 (The shooting, as he saw and heard it)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "A little after noon: '**A kid asked him a question, and then I heard a shot fired.**' He puts it at **12:23**." The file never says how many shots he heard.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On cross: "So you heard the shot and you only heard one shot, correct?" — "Yes." A whole-file search for /one shot/ returns exactly one hit, this one.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Single-shot testimony from the officer closest to the courtyard is a basic evidentiary fact of Day 1, and it interlocks with two findings CR-E05 does make: the purposive search that produced no spent casing (§3.3) and his rifle-versus-handgun inference from the sound (§3.2). It is also the only place in Day 1 where the shot count is established at all. A reader of CR-E05 alone cannot say whether one shot or several were heard.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 ("His report omits the direction of the shot")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**His report omits the direction of the shot** — 'I don't see a direction' — and he wrote no supplement."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Accurate as to compass direction, but the very next question drew a qualification the file drops. Asked whether the report says anything about thinking the shot came from the Losee building, he answered: "Later on when I saw the empty holsters, when I … I think I actually said that in there, where I see the empty holster that I realized the line of sight." The defence did not press it and moved to the holster.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05's version leaves the reader with a report wholly silent on where Bagley thought the shot came from. His sworn testimony is that the report does record the holster-to-line-of-sight realisation — i.e. the report is silent on compass direction but (he believes) not on the reasoning that took him to the Losee roof. Under the both-directions rule this qualification belongs in the same bullet; leaving it out overstates the defence's point in exactly the direction hazard 4 warns about. (It also bears on §8 item 4, which names the report as an acquisition target — this is what to check it against.)

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Describing the nighttime photograph: '**to me, it looks like a sniper pad, a person that has been [lying there]**.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The sentence continues, and the continuation is the evidentiary content: "to me, it looks like a sniper pad, a person that has been laying in a prone position and you've got markings of elbows, knees, and feet to where somebody was in the line of sight of where Charlie's tent was." On State's Exhibit 5 he itemised further: "two elbows, two knee areas." A whole-file search for /sniper pad/ returns one hit, this one.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file flags "sniper pad" as the witness's own characterisation and tells later readers to carry his qualification — correct — but the bracketed "[lying there]" elides what he actually said he saw: discrete impressions of elbows, knees and feet, oriented to the tent's line of sight. That is the difference between a vague "disturbance" and a described body-position impression, and it is the fact any later analysis of the rooftop photographs turns on. Hazard 7: reliable as to the words, misleading as to the testimony.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.3 ("left at about 1:01–1:03 p.m., and handed off")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He secured the roof with tape around the southwest portion, left at about **1:01–1:03 p.m.**, and handed off."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two details are omitted. (1) He set a SECOND barrier at the roof access: "where that natural guardrail is, that was the other barrier where they were advised not to go any further from there, other than police officers." (2) He released the roof scene to "a county deputy, a female," instructing her "not to let anybody inside the crime scene without being a police officer or an investigator." The defence returned to it on cross — "you turned over the scene on the roof to a woman who was a deputy sheriff, right?" — and established that she, like the Payson officers, "weren't there until after the shooting… part of just a response of everybody in the area."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05 names the two Payson officers who took the northeast scene (§3.4) but leaves the roof handoff anonymous. Given the file's own emphasis on scene integrity — the unreviewed video window, others on the roof during it, the dead body camera — who held the perch scene after 1:03 p.m., and that she was an unassigned responder from another agency, is part of the same chain.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 ("and he wrote no supplement") vs §8 item 4
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.5: "…and he wrote no supplement." §8 item 4: "Bagley's police report (used on cross as 'Bagley 1'; **a supplement within a larger agency-assist report**)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: In this block he testified the opposite of §3.5's wording: "I did a supplement on it. I didn't prepare the report because the incident was a big agency assist, so obviously it says it has all the responding officers to that effect." The basis for "no supplement" is a different question, outside this block, at 04:20:01 — whether he wrote "any kind of supplement… other than what we've gone through today, that one report you wrote… Have you ever written another one?" — "I have not."
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 5047–5050 (02:49:30); the later exchange at 04:19:51–04:20:01
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: As written, §3.5 contradicts §8 item 4 and the sworn testimony in this block. The document at issue IS his supplement. The fix is one word — "he wrote no FURTHER supplement" — but uncorrected it invites a later reader to record that Bagley never supplemented an agency report he in fact supplemented.

not_verified_items.target_section: §2.1 / §7 ("the rulings admitting exhibits were considered rather than reflexive")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §7 supports this with three examples: 12.1, the "murder" misstatement, and publication. §2.1 and §3.3 do not record the court policing foundation on its own initiative.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On State's Exhibit 4 the judge raised a foundation problem sua sponte, before ruling: "…it also appears to be other artifacts on this image that I haven't heard any testimony about. And so—" — prompting "I will follow up, Judge," and a further foundation sequence on the orange/red triangular markers. He did the same on 3.2, admitting only with an express finding: "Given that follow-up question noting that the evidence tag, it appears to be number two on State's Exhibit 3.2 was not present, but otherwise it is a fair and accurate representation…"
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions material the file's own §7 argument wants: the court twice made the State cure foundation it had not laid, and admitted only on findings that itemised what was and was not present when the witness observed the scene. It also matters technically — the admitted exhibits carry court findings about post-hoc alterations (markers, tags), which is the same defect that later sank Exhibit 12.1 (§5).

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 ("The nighttime rooftop photographs rest on hearsay")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The file records the hearsay objection to Exhibits 4 and 5 but not the separate objection ground to the daytime rooftop photograph, State's Exhibit 3.2.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "Your Honor, I think that we renew our standing objection. There is an evidence tag here, which begs the question that it's not a fair and accurate representation… And we also don't have any indication about when this picture was taken or by whom. So we object to its admission." Separately, the court's basis for admitting Exhibit 5 was NOT purely hearsay: Bagley independently adopted it — "With respect to what you observed that day, apart from the evidence tag, the yellow tag as well as the orange or red markers, is this a fair and accurate depiction of what you observed?" — "Yes"; the court admitted "[g]iven the foundation that has been laid and that the witness has testified that this is a fair and accurate representation of the scene."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two corrections in one. (a) The defence's provenance objection — no evidence of when a scene photograph was taken or by whom — is a distinct ground from the Richards hearsay objection and applied to the daytime photographs too. (b) §3.5 leaves the impression that Exhibits 4 and 5 rest on Richards' hearsay alone; Exhibit 5 has a dual foundation, one leg of which is Bagley's own eyewitness adoption, and that is the leg the court's admission ruling actually named. That cuts for the State and the both-directions rule requires it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Defence counsel put on the record that the State was '**clearly offering it for the truth**.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Her objection had a stated reason and a proposed cure, both omitted: "he's clearly offering it for the truth because he's asking him to describe the route of the individual and it's based on what other people told him. So if he wants to circle back to it after he's put the video in, I mean, we could do that, but right now I still think it's inappropriate hearsay, Your Honor." The objection was framed as "a continuing objection to all the hearsay that's being testified to here."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The defence conceded a curable path — put the video in first, then ask about the route — which is precisely the sequencing problem that recurs with Exhibit 12.1 on Day 1 and Day 2 (§5, D-52). Quoting only the four-word accusation makes the objection look reflexive when it was specific and offered a remedy.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Exhibits 4 and 5 were taken by **Melissa Richards**, a state forensic-lab employee **who did not testify**"; §8: "**Melissa Richards**, state forensic lab."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Asked who she is, Bagley answered: "She's the lead senior forensic for the State of Utah Examiner." That is on its face a garbled rendering — most plausibly "lead senior forensic examiner for the State of Utah" — and it is the only description of her role in this block.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "State forensic-lab employee" understates the seniority the witness attributed to her, and the phrase as rendered is a garble that belongs in §1.3's list alongside Faumuina/Elschultz/Nielsen. Since §8 item 8 makes her an acquisition target, the file should carry her role exactly as spoken plus the flag that the orthography and title are unverified.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §1.2 tabulates six label failures, all of them MISattributions. §1.3's garble list does not include defence counsel's surname, and the file itself uses both spellings — "Kathy Nestor" in §1.2, "Nester" in §2 and §3.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two additional, distinct rendering failures in this block. (1) The name: Rev labels her "Kathy Nestor" throughout, but she states "my name is Kathy Nester," and the court addresses "Ms. Nester" (02:15:50) and "Ms. Nestor" (04:04:55) — the court, rendered two ways. (2) A different failure mode from misattribution — anonymisation: the prosecutor's reply to the court before the lunch recess carries "Speaker 7" ("Not the state, no"), the bailiff's "All rise" carries "Speaker 8," and a silent stretch carries "Speaker 9."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.2 is the file's flagship caveat and the basis of QUEUE.md standing hazard 9. It currently describes only labels that name the wrong person; it should also record that Rev drops named counsel into anonymous "Speaker N" labels mid-proceeding, since a reader searching by counsel's name will silently miss those turns. And the file's own inconsistent Nester/Nestor usage needs a stated basis — which exists, at 02:43:01, in her own words.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Timestamps are recording-stream time, not time of day**, and the clock jumps across each recess… They are **identifiers**. Day 1's stream begins at 06:57 with the call to order."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The rule is right, and this block contains a worked example plus the only wall-clock anchors spoken on the record here. Before cross began the court asked counsel to break "roughly in that 12:00, 12:10 range"; counsel stopped "five minutes early for lunch"; the court said "We'll come back at one o'clock." The stream then runs 02:56:54 → (silence 03:24:00) → 04:04:41 for a recess the court had fixed at about 55 minutes.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest available demonstration of hazard 2 — an ~68-minute stream gap across a ~55-minute recess — and it gives the library on-record clock statements (break ~12:05 p.m., resume 1:00 p.m.) that can anchor later-day work without ever converting a stream timestamp. Recording the anchors is not the same as converting them, and §1.3 currently has neither.

not_verified_items.target_section: §6A ("Bagley's entire testimony contains no reference to Tyler Robinson")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Bagley's entire testimony contains no reference to Tyler Robinson.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: True of the witness's own answers in this block, but not of his examination: defence counsel introduced herself to him with "my name is Kathy Nester. I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Robinson today." A name search across the Bagley portion returns that hit.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §6A explicitly frames each null as "a claim about a full-text search of this Rev rendering." As phrased, this one is falsifiable by that very search, which is how scoped nulls lose their value. Re-scoping it — "Bagley never refers to Robinson; the only mention during his testimony is defence counsel identifying herself as Robinson's attorney" — keeps the substantive point (nothing Bagley saw is tied to the defendant) and survives the search.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §2's shape table records only "Officer Chris Bagley — direct (Grunander), cross (Nester), brief redirect; excused." The word "redirect" appears exactly once in the whole file (grep-verified), and no redirect content appears anywhere.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Redirect was short but substantive and was the State's single rehabilitative act after the cross. Grunander had Bagley approach the monitor and pin the holster's location on State's Exhibit 1: "this is the picture of the courtyard area facing north... On this top tier back here... the waterfalls on the left side... On the south side by the Fugal building, that top tier of grass is about where it was at." Grunander then confirmed "Neck [sic — near] by the Fugal building," and Bagley closed with the point of the whole exercise: "And that's where I could see straight up where the line of sight was." The Fugal building is a landmark that appears nowhere in CR-E05 (grep: 0 hits).
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 6208–6271; stream 04:20:10–04:22:03 (the pin-down at 04:21:27 and 04:21:52)
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Headline 2 calls the cross "one of the most defence-favourable stretches in the whole hearing." That is defensible, but a reader of CR-E05 alone would believe the State did nothing to answer it. In fact the State closed by having the witness geographically tie the abandoned holster's position to the direct sightline to the Losee building — which is precisely the inferential chain §3.2 and §7 credit him with. It is a both-directions gap in the file's own strongest section, and it supplies a courtyard landmark (Fugal building) the file's geography lacks.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.4: "He **saw 'a long black object in the left hand'** as the person crossed the roof; asked what it was, he said '**It looks like a rifle or something to that effect, a long object… like skinny and long**.'" §6A: "The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged '**long black object**'."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The file stops one exchange short of the witness's flattest concession. Nestor: "So you can see a towel, but you can't see an actual gun." Bagley: "I don't know if it was a towel or a blanket. I don't know what it was." Nestor: "But you can't see an actual gun in the video?" Bagley: "No. Like an object, like a form of a gun, like a long object." He also testified the object appeared wrapped — "You can see it's almost like it's covered over something" — and the word "towel" was supplied by counsel, not the witness, who then declined to adopt it.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the single most defence-favourable answer in the block and it strengthens the file's own §6A null ("the rifle is never recovered, described forensically, or photographed"). CR-E05 reports the hedge but not the express denial, so a careful reader gets a weaker version of the file's own finding. It also matters that the object was described as covered/wrapped and that the witness refused counsel's "towel" — a reader of CR-E05 would not know a covering was in issue at all (grep: "towel" and "blanket" both 0 in CR-E05).

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.4 renders the exchange as: "**asked what it was**, he said '**It looks like a rifle or something to that effect, a long object… like skinny and long**.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: He was not asked what it was. Nestor asked: "And **knowing what you know about the case today**, do you have an idea about what that object was?" — and the "looks like a rifle" answer responds to that. Immediately before it, asked what he could tell the last time he watched, he said: "Well, not tell what it is. I can see there's an object in that left hand."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's phrasing converts a hindsight opinion, expressly invited by counsel's framing, into a perceptual description of what the witness saw on the video. That is exactly the anchor/connection separation CLAUDE.md requires, applied to a single answer. Since §6A leans on this passage as the record's only weapon reference, the framing carries weight beyond §3.4.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §6A asserts of Day 1: "**No ballistics, no bullet recovery, no fingerprints, no DNA** of any kind." §6 confirms "**No spent casing and no unfired bullet on the Losee roof**." The file is otherwise silent on any bullet found elsewhere.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Immediately after establishing that Bagley found no casing and no unshot bullets on the Losee roof, defence counsel put two propositions to him that presuppose a bullet was recovered somewhere: "Are you aware of there being a bullet found on another roof—" ("I'm not aware") "...in the vicinity? Were you aware of another bullet being found on the scene not on the roof of the Losee building?" ("No").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A question by counsel is not evidence of the fact assumed and must stay in the recording layer — but its presence is a fact about the record, and CR-E05 records other counsel-supplied facts (the 27:35 bodycam length, the ~30-second detention). This one bears directly on a headline finding and on D-48: the file treats the rooftop null as clean corroboration of CR-E04 §5.1, while the defence was on the record floating a bullet recovered elsewhere on scene. It is an open lead the acquisition roadmap should carry, and it makes §6A's flat "no bullet recovery" imprecise as a statement about the transcript.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.5 and §7 record the scene-integrity problems — "His body camera died on the roof, before the tape went up"; "He never reviewed the video for the window between the individual leaving the roof and his own arrival." The file records no corresponding concession by the defence.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Defence counsel expressly conceded the other half on the record. Nestor: "Okay. But once you put the tape up, then we're confident from that point on the scene was preserved, right?" Bagley: "Yeah." She then established that he never left the roof to obtain the tape: officers "responded on the scene that he was down on the bottom and threw it up to me"; "So you didn't have it on you?" — "No." "And you didn't leave the scene to go get it?" — "No."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The task's own standard names concessions as material, and CLAUDE.md's both-directions rule makes an audit trail that only weakens one side a bias signal. §7 lists the bodycam death and the unreviewed window under "Against the prosecution" without recording that the defence itself bounded the problem at the moment the tape went up, and that the witness's continuous presence on the roof (tape thrown up rather than fetched) was established on cross. A reader of CR-E05 alone would over-read the scene-integrity attack.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.4: "**Unaccounted alterations.** Hull conceded '**some edits were made by your office**' — **the prosecutor's own office** — to Wright's video (04:39:43)." §7 and the revision log carry it as "alterations conceded to have been made by **the prosecutor's own office**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two elements are dropped. (1) The answer is hedged and second-hand: "**My understanding is** that some edits were made by your office **in order to protect some of the participants in the video**." (2) The identity of those participants is stated in the block: defence counsel argued the exhibit should be protected "particularly because **the video contains images of minor children**, which I know the state has made an effort to redact." CR-E05 never mentions minors in Exhibit 6 (grep: "minor child" 0 hits) and characterises the non-publication reason only as "not all alleged victims' faces were obscured."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Three problems at once. The "my understanding is" hedge means the lead case agent had no first-hand knowledge of who altered the exhibit — which strengthens the defence point but also means the file states as a concession something the witness could only relay. Omitting the stated protective purpose, and the fact that the protected persons were minor children, makes a redaction-of-minors look like unexplained tampering when listed under "Against the prosecution" in §7. And the minors point is living-persons-relevant material that §1.4 would want.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.4's table gives the Wright collection chain and §4.4's preamble states the Rule 1102 architecture — "not one of the five source witnesses testified." The file is silent on Hull's own distance from the verification act.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The pre-hearing verification of Exhibit 6 was performed entirely outside Hull's presence. "And who had that follow-up visit with Ms. Wright?" — "That was **Agent Davis. I was not able to attend**." "And you know that happened because you spoke to Agent Davis?" — "I spoke to Agent Davis, and **he provided me with a written statement** that Ms. Wright had completed." Hull's testimony about the 1102 form's contents likewise rests on having read the document afterwards ("I have seen that written statement... I have" read it).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: CR-E05's headline 4 is that every civilian video entered as Rule 1102 written hearsay with no source witness present. The record adds a second layer the file misses: the sponsoring agent was not present when the statement was taken either, so the foundation for Exhibit 6/6.1 is agent-hearsay about witness-hearsay. That is the strongest form of the file's own architecture finding and it is what the defence's reliability argument in the same block was aimed at.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.4 attack 1 records only: "**Confrontation.** A standing constitutional objection ran against every exhibit — the same **Rule 1102 / Art. I §12** challenge recorded at CR-E03 §5A.2a." The single "UCJA" mention in the whole file (line 214) attributes the UCJA argument to **counsel for the news media** at 05:09:43. The rule number 4-202.02 appears nowhere (grep: 0 hits).
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The UCJA issue originated as a defence objection to Exhibit 6.1, an hour earlier and by subsection: "this does fall under the type of document that should be safeguarded under **Rule 4-202.02(8)(f)**, as in 'Frank,' and/or should be classified as protected under **subsection (5)(O)**, as in 'orange,' because the disclosure could jeopardize the life safety or property of the witness." She also argued Wright "technically could be classified as **a victim** of the event" and therefore protected on that ground; that the statement "would not be admissible at trial in the current format... due to its hearsay nature"; and that publication would harm the client's fair-trial right. The court made her restate the rule ("the Utah Code of Judicial Administration for Rule 4-202.02(8)(f), as in 'Frank,' and/or (5)(O)") and read it before ruling. The State's answer drew the distinction the file's §2.1 framework depends on: "that judicial rule, **it has nothing to do with admissibility. It's simply publishing it**."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §2.1 presents the three-level exhibit framework (admission / courtroom publication / media capture) as a judicial construct. The transcript shows it was litigated by rule number, with the defence supplying the publication-side authority and the State supplying the admissibility/publication split. A reader of CR-E05 would think the UCJA thread began with the press an hour later, and would have no rule citation to pull. It also records the defence, unusually, arguing victim status for a State witness.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.4 attack 3: "Hull made **three self-corrections after consulting his notes**." The file identifies the notes no further, and §8's acquisition list does not include them. "refresh" appears 0 times in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The refreshing document is identified on the record as a specific, already-disclosed artifact: "I have **some notes and a timeline from my investigation that was part of discovery**." The court then made an evidentiary ruling on it — Nestor: "Your Honor, when he's done, may I take a look at the materials as well, please?" Court: "**You may**." "Ms. Nester, if you'd like to come forward." She approached and inspected; Hull confirmed "That is my times and dates."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two things are lost. First, a ruling — the court permitting defence inspection of the writing used to refresh, which is the procedural counterweight to the "recall is unreliable" attack the file builds in §4.4. Second, and more usefully, a named primary artifact: the lead case agent's investigative timeline, produced in discovery, containing the dates and times underlying the whole collection-chain table in §4.4. That belongs in §8 as an acquisition target and is absent.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.3: "he **specifically looked for a spent shell casing** — at the prone position, over the edge, 'all over' — and '**As a matter of fact, no**,' he could not find one." The analyst-layer paragraph then treats this as corroborating that "no bullets or casings were found on or immediately around the Losee building."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness attached his own temporal limit, which the file drops: "I was looking over the edge, looking all over the place, making sure the gravel wasn't disturbed, and I couldn't find a shell casing **at that moment**."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "At that moment" bounds the negative search to his own time on the roof (~12:44 to the 1:01–1:03 handoff the file records at §3.3), before the crime lab processed the scene. The file's confidence statement is properly scoped ("High as to the testimony"), so this is a precision point rather than a reversal — but the qualifier is the witness's own, it belongs in a section the file headlines, and standing hazard 7 (selective quotation reliable as to the words, not the document) is the reason to restore it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §1.3 records only the garble: "the drone operator is 'Sergeant **Cam Nelson**' at 02:54:06 and 'Sergeant **Ken Nielsen**' at 04:18:21 — **the same person, named two ways by the same witness**." §8 item 5 lists Exhibits 1, 2, 3 among "the scene photographs, all admitted Day 1, none held." "Provo Police" appears 0 times in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The same passage establishes the provenance of the aerial exhibits and the agency: "the pictures you were shown, exhibits 1, 2, and 3... do you have any knowledge about where those pictures came from or who took them?" — "**I guess they were drone footage. Just taken from a drone**." "Do you know who was operating the drone?" — "**Sergeant Ken Nielsen from Provo Police Department**." Note the witness's own hedge, "I guess."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file mines this passage for a name-garble caveat but not for the two facts that matter operationally: State's Exhibits 1–3 are drone imagery, and the operator was Provo PD — a different agency from UVU PD, which is where a records request would go. It also drops the "I guess," which is a live provenance hedge in a section (§3.5) whose whole point is that "exhibit provenance was outside his knowledge."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.1: "He was later directed to Utah Valley, understanding he was going only to assist... **SBI was then designated the lead investigative agency, with Hull and Agent Davis as lead case agents.**" No name is given for who directed either step. "Jensen" appears 0 times in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "And do you recall who directed you to come down to Utah Valley?" — "I believe it was **Lieutenant Jensen**." And on the lead designation: "I was informed by **my lieutenant** that myself and Agent Davis would be taking lead on the investigation on behalf of the State Bureau of Investigations."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §4.1 builds an SBI personnel-and-assignment map; the officer who ordered the response and made the lead-agent designation is missing from it. It also matters that the lead designation came from inside DPS rather than from an inter-agency decision, which the file's passive "SBI was then designated" obscures.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The file is silent on Hull's prior familiarity with the UVU campus. §4.5 records that "the four-campus-visits timeline rests **solely** on UVU surveillance review."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "Prior to September 10th, 2025, how familiar were you with the Utah Valley University campus?" — "**Not very. I think I maybe had been there once before.**" His familiarity was acquired afterwards, and he said how: "both in walking the campus and looking at the incident scene, in viewing surveillance video of the campus and the surrounding areas, and just my general involvement in the investigation."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hull is the narrator for most of Day 1's campus geography and for the movement timeline the file flags in §4.5 as resting solely on surveillance review. That his entire geographic knowledge post-dates the shooting and derives from the same surveillance material is a qualification on the narrator, recorded in his own words, and it is the kind of both-directions calibration §4.5's hedging paragraph is already reaching for.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.5 records the video volume — "Hundreds of hours of video were available, predominantly UVU's; Hull personally watched perhaps **10–20 hours** that day." The file records no attendance figure and no public-submission stream. "3000"/"3,000" appear 0 times in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull described a second, distinct intake channel: "We were getting a large volume of information from the general public, **phone tips, people sending videos**. **Analysts were scrolling through social media** and social sites as people were posting information onto the internet." And on scale, framed hypothetically: "If you imagine there's **3000 people** at an event and everybody has a cell phone, there was a lot of information that people were willing to share with us."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Numbers are material by the task's own test, and this is the only attendance figure in the block — worth recording, with the caveat that Hull phrased it as a hypothetical ("if you imagine") rather than as a headcount, so it should not be hardened into an established attendance. The public-tip and social-media intake is also a sourcing channel entirely absent from §4.4/§4.5, which describe only agency-collected and UVU video.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.3 cites the ME report's basis precisely as "**URE 1102(b)(5)**"; §4.4 describes the 1102 architecture without recording which subsection the State invoked for the witness statements.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State's citation for Exhibit 6.1 was given inconsistently within a single argument: "it was gathered in compliance with the Utah Rules of Evidence 1102, **specifically subsection B8**" and then, a paragraph later, "it has been collected in compliance with rule 1102. As I stated, **B3 or B8**."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's Rule 1102 architecture is headline 4 and the subsection is the operative authority. Recording it as the State actually stated it — imprecisely, twice — is both a completeness point and a small addition to the §4.4 "recall/precision" thread, which the file currently attributes only to the witness.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.5: "He does not know who took **Exhibit 35**, where it came from, or how old it is. He first saw **Exhibits 1, 2 and 3** 'a couple of weeks ago'." §8 item 5: "**Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 35**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: These are all State's exhibits. The block itself shows the parties using the qualified form where it counts — Grunander on redirect: "if we could pull up **State's Exhibit 1**" — and the file uses "State's Exhibit" correctly ten times elsewhere, including for 12.1, 11 and 6.1.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Standing hazard 3: exhibit numbers are not unique across parties, and Day 1 has both State's and defence exhibits in play. The inconsistency is confined to Bagley's scene photographs, but §8 is an acquisition list — the exact form a later reader will quote into a records request.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4: "*(CR-E04 records that he **left SBI in March 2026** and is now an investigative sergeant at POST.)*" — both facts attributed to CR-E04.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull established the current assignment himself on Day 1, in the block's opening qualification sequence: "What is your current assignment with the Department of Public Safety?" — "I'm currently positioned as an **investigative sergeant at Peace Officer Standards and Training**." "Was that your assignment in September of 2025?" — "No, it was not." Only the March 2026 departure date is unique to CR-E04.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: It is a small sourcing point but it runs the right way: Day 1 independently corroborates half of what the file attributes to a companion file. Under the both-directions rule confirmations are supposed to be logged explicitly, and a cross-file corroboration recorded as a borrowing is a confirmation the library loses.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Contacted by **Agent Mortensen** 10-08; video provided electronically 10-11. Hull contacted her **2026-04-06** *(corrected on the stand from April 7)*" — i.e. the table's collection-chain cell makes Hull the person who went back to Wright.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull testified he was NOT there. Inside my block the prosecutor himself corrects mid-question: "that statement that was prepared by Ms. Wright, what does it state with regards to the video that you showed her that day? Or I guess Agent Davis showed her that day." And on the handwriting: Q "was it you or SBI Agent Davis that prepared that?" A "Based on the writing, it appears to be Agent Davis's writing, but it's not my writing." (Boundary context immediately before the block confirms it flatly: "who had that follow-up visit with Ms. Wright?" / "That was Agent Davis. I was not able to attend... I spoke to Agent Davis, and he provided me with a written statement that Ms. Wright had completed.")
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Wright's Exhibit 6.1 is the one 1102 in this tranche where the sponsoring witness never met the declarant and never watched her verify the file. The foundation is therefore hearsay resting on hearsay — Hull relaying what Davis handed him — which is precisely the reliability point the defence was pressing. CR-E05's table erases that gap and makes Hull the through-line for all four statements. This is the file's own §4.4 headline architecture, described wrongly.
