not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 ("The SBI 1102 form" paragraph and defence-attack list)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent. §4.4 describes the 1102 form as containing only "an advisory that the statement will be used at a preliminary hearing in lieu of live testimony, and a warning that a false statement is a class A misdemeanour," and lists three defence attacks, none of them authenticity of the form itself.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every 1102 form in this tranche is a TWO-HAND document, and the defence made it a live authenticity objection that the court took seriously enough to reopen foundation. Nestor: "there's clearly two different authors in the body of the document. One wrote something on the very top line, and then it looks like Ms. Wright wrote the rest of it. Which we don't have any indication of who wrote that top line and when they filled that in, if it was before or after she signed the document. So I have some concerns about authenticity." The court agreed on its face: "as I'm determining it, it does appear that the writing is different. Did you want to lay additional foundation, Mr. Sturgill?" Hull then explained the practice: "Because we were asking Ms. Wright to verify a specific video. The file name for that video was written on the statement in her presence... because we were specifically asking them to verify a specific digital file that had a specific digital name, and we didn't want there to be any errors in how that name was presented. We wrote the file name on the document for the individuals." On Wright's form the hand was Agent Davis's; on Phillips's, Hull's own ("I believe, in this instance, it was myself that wrote the file name on the form").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The identifier that ties each 1102 statement to a specific digital file was written by a law-enforcement officer, not by the declarant. That is the mechanical joint of the entire Rule 1102 video architecture CR-E05 calls Day 1's "documentary architecture" — and it is the same joint D-52 turns on (whether Exhibit 12.3's wording did or did not account for the alterations). A reader of CR-E05 alone would picture a witness-written form.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Ex. 6** — admitted; **initially not published at all** because not all alleged victims' faces were obscured." The reason is given; the dispute that produced it is not.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The prosecutor represented to the court that the faces were blurred: "to protect who we believe is victims in this video, I believe their faces have been blurred out," and when challenged, "My recollection is they've all been blurred out." Defence counsel contradicted him: "I think it's only the minor children whose faces are blurred out, not Ms. Wright, if I'm not mistaken." The judge then had the video played on the monitors and made a finding against the prosecutor's representation: "Based off what I've watched, there was some blurring of faces, but not of all the faces."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the second time in the same hour that the State's representation about its own redaction work was shown to be wrong on the record (the first being the unredacted 6.1 at §1.4). CR-E05 records the first and not the second, so a reader sees an isolated "glitch" rather than a pattern in the State's exhibit handling — and the defence's factual correctness is not credited. It also connects directly to §4.4's own defence-attack 2 ("alterations by the prosecutor's own office"), which is where the blurring came from.

not_verified_items.target_section: §7 ("For the prosecution, and logged as squarely")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The court repeatedly ruled against the State** — on 12.1, on the \"murder\" misstatement, **on publication** — which is itself evidence that the rulings admitting exhibits were considered rather than reflexive."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Across the eight exhibit rulings in my block, the court gave the State exactly what the State asked for in seven, and partially reversed toward the State in the eighth. 6.1: State asked admission + courtroom + public — granted. 7.1: all three requested — granted. 8.1: all three requested — granted. 12.3: all three requested — granted. Ex. 7: State asked admission only, no publication — granted as requested. Ex. 8: State asked admission, no publication — granted as requested. Ex. 9: State asked admission, no publication — granted as requested. Ex. 6 is the only divergence: the State asked for all three, the court first denied courtroom publication, then after counsel for the news media (not the defence) intervened, moved BACK toward the State and allowed courtroom publication, withholding only media capture.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The proposition that the court "repeatedly ruled against the State … on publication" is contradicted by this block, and the one apparent instance was a third party's win that the court then narrowed in the State's favour. CR-E05 offers the claim as evidence that admission rulings were considered rather than reflexive; that inference does not survive contact with this stretch. Standing hazard 4 applies in the mirror: a correction running toward the State's disadvantage is as reportable as one running the other way.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Ex. 8** — admitted; **publication DENIED**, citing Art. I §28(1)(a)… **Ex. 9** — admitted; **not published, not broadcast**; the court watched it in open court on monitors." Both are written as the court's own doing. The file records the State's self-restraint only for Ex. 7.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State volunteered non-publication for all three graphic videos, and on Exhibit 9 the defence expressly agreed. Ex. 8: "With regards to publication, Judge, it's our position that it not be published here in the courtroom, and that it not be published so that the cameras can display it." Ex. 9: "we'd ask that it not be published here in the courtroom, nor published in any way that the media camera could capture it. And following your reasoning, Judge, out of deference to the victims and the victim's rights." Nestor on Ex. 9: "We agree it should not be published. We object to its admissibility."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The pattern — the State, not the defence, driving non-publication of every video showing the shooting, with the defence agreeing outright on one — is a real feature of Day 1 and cuts directly against §7's framing. It also shows the parties converging on victim-dignity grounds while continuing to fight about admissibility, which is a different picture of the hearing than "three defence attacks, all preserved."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Flash drive to **Lt. O'Brien** on 2025-09-10, then downloadable versions to Agent Mortenson" — the row gives no 1102 date and no collector, while every other row gives one.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull: "Mr. Farnsworth originally provided, I believe, a flash drive to Lieutenant O'Brien with one of the local agencies, and a short time after that on September 10th, he provided downloadable versions, electronic versions to Agent Mortenson, **and an 1102 was collected from him on May 6th of 2026**." And on who collected it: Q "who collected that 1102 statement from Mr. Farnsworth?" A "It was Agent Mortenson who collected it." Hull's only personal contact was afterwards: "He provided it to me, and then as I mentioned, I subsequently spoke to Terryl Farnsworth personally regarding his statement." Hull also could not name O'Brien's agency ("one of the local agencies").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two of the four 1102 statements in this tranche (Wright's, Farnsworth's) were collected outside Hull's presence, by Davis and Mortenson respectively. That is the single most important structural fact about the Day 1 hearsay architecture and CR-E05's table does not show it. The 2026-05-06 date also completes the timeline the other three rows carry — nearly eight months post-event, two months pre-hearing.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 (Rule 1102 table, Olsen/Ex. 9 row — "Collection chain, as testified")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The chain cell for Exhibit 9 reads only "Hull met Olsen **2026-06-24** *(corrected from July 2)*" — presented as a chain.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull conceded he does not know the front end of that chain. Q: "do you recall who provided that video to you initially and who collected it?" A: "**Initially, I don't know specifically for that video**, but I know that whole process was overseen by Mr. Olsen who's responsible for that system." Olsen's role was described as oversight of the UVU camera system ("He has a long title, but I think it's director of infrastructure, but he is responsible for that system"), not as the person who pulled or handed over this file.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Exhibit 9 is the video CR-E05 itself relies on at §4.2 for Kirk being carried out under the breezeway, and it is from the same UVU surveillance family as Exhibit 12.1 — the exhibit that anchors D-52. An unknown initial collector, admitted by the sponsoring witness, is a chain-of-custody gap a reader of the table would never suspect. It also supplies context for why the defence's 12.3 objection ("verified the recordings but doesn't say how") had force.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Every civilian video came in through a **Rule 1102 written statement** … and not one of the five source witnesses testified." The file does not state what Hull's own contribution to authentication was held to be.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State expressly limited Hull's authentication role. Arguing Rule 901 on Exhibit 6: "Judge, you have an 1102 statement prepared by the person who actually caught these images on her camera or on her phone. And so, Judge, I think that alone sufficiently authenticates the document. And then even further than that, you have Agent Hull, who has reviewed the video himself and authenticates it, **at least with regards to location**." The court's Exhibit 7 ruling made the dependency explicit: "I will admit Exhibit Seven into evidence based off the foundation that's laid. **The 1102 is tied directly to this**, and so for admission purposes, it is admitted." Hull's own recognition testimony was uniformly locational — "It's the amphitheater at the Utah Valley University where Mr. Kirk was doing his event"; "consistent with the event that Mr. Kirk was presenting at UVU on September 10th, 2025."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is an evidentiary limit, and the task treats limits as material. Every one of these videos stands or falls on the absent declarant's written statement; the testifying agent verified nothing but the venue. A reader of CR-E05 could reasonably think the case agent's review added independent authentication of content.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 ("Three defence attacks on this architecture, all preserved")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Three attacks are listed: confrontation, unaccounted alterations, recall. The UCJA classification argument appears only once, as a clause inside the description of the media counsel's rebuttal, and never as a defence position.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: A fourth, separately-briefed defence line ran through every exhibit in this block: Utah Code of Judicial Administration Rule 4-202.02, cited by subsection. Nestor opened with "(8)(f), as in 'Frank,' and/or … (5)(O), as in 'orange,' because the disclosure could jeopardize the life safety or property of the witness," adding that Wright "technically could be classified as a victim of the event." She later added "(4)(R), as in 'Richard,' photograph, film, or video of a crime victim are designated as private court records. And I do think that based on what the state has previously referenced… they are perceiving that everyone in the audience is a potential victim, and so we think it shouldn't be published under that rule." For Phillips she argued "private means it shouldn't be played to court, and it shouldn't be played to the public through the media." The State then challenged the defence's standing to make it at all: "with regards to this video, and this video only, the State doesn't believe that the defense really has standing to make an argument on behalf of the victims in this case."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This was the defence's principal publication argument and the one the court's whole publication practice was built against. It also surfaces a notable feature of the State's posture — that everyone in the audience is treated as a potential victim — which the State declined to disown ("we don't necessarily disagree") while simultaneously denying the defence standing to invoke it. None of this is recoverable from CR-E05.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Ex. 7** — admitted; **the State itself asked that it not be published.** Viewed on the judge's and counsel's monitors only, with sound, **counsel ordered to guard their screens.**" No objection ground is given.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence objected to Exhibit 7 on Rule 403 as well as authentication: "And also under Rule 403, we think it's more prejudicial than probative, and we would raise it for that reason as well." She had separately described the video's content on the record: "this video does in fact show a closeup view of the shooting of Mr. Kirk, and grievous injuries in very stark relief." The court admitted it without addressing 403 in terms, resting on "the foundation that's laid. The 1102 is tied directly to this."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the only Rule 403 objection in the block and a distinct evidentiary ground from the confrontation and authentication attacks CR-E05 catalogues. It also matters that the court did not engage it expressly — CR-E04 records Judge Graf invoking Rule 403 on Day 2 for Exhibit 12.1, so the Day 1 non-engagement is the earlier half of a sequence the library is already tracking.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.4 ("Twice, private individuals' details entered the proceeding") and §1.3
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Twice**, private individuals' details entered the proceeding" — the unredacted Exhibit 6.1 handed to the court, and a street address spoken aloud at ~06:57:20.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: There was a third redaction-handling failure on the same day, and the defence argued an objection without the operative document. On Exhibit 8.1 Nestor stated mid-argument: "I don't have a redacted version of 8.1, but I assume there is one. **There is personal information on this one.** Do you have the… Okay, I don't have that one." The judge stopped to check: "Ms. Nestor, I just wanted to check, did you get a copy of the redacted—" / "I was just handed it." The court's eventual publication ruling turned on redaction: "being that the person's identifying information is redacted and not viewable, I'm going to overrule the standing objection."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.4 makes a counted scope claim ("twice"), and a counted claim that undercounts is a defect in exactly the section where this library is most careful. Substantively it shows the 6.1 incident was not a one-off "glitch": the State was still handing the defence redacted versions of exhibits during argument on them. (No detail is reproduced here, per the standing rule.)

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.2 (Kirk's evacuation) — the file has no section for scene geometry at all
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent. §4.2 mentions Exhibit 9 only as "*(Exhibit 9 partially shows Kirk being carried out under the breezeway.)*"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: After Exhibit 9 played, the prosecutor took Hull through the geometry of Kirk's position, producing the only distance figure in the block. The banner in the middle of the frame is "the rear of the gazebo" — "like a pop-up tent that Mr. Kirk was sat underneath while he was addressing the crowd." Kirk's position relative to it: "Approximately dead center. He's on a stage, so he's slightly raised in relation to the bottom of that banner and then he's seated in the middle of the stage, so approximately in the center." Distance from banner to Kirk: "I don't know specifically. **If I had to estimate, I would say three to five feet.**" And the camera's own orientation: "It's a view kind of looking what would be east under the breezeway towards the back of the stage where Mr. Kirk was situated." Kirk being carried out is "on the left side, the back of the pop-up tent… carried down the left side of the video under that breezeway."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Numbers are named material by the review standard, and this project has live physical/forensic questions about the Losee line of sight. This is the only stand-off/position testimony in the block, it is expressly an estimate (which must be preserved as such), and the breezeway camera's stated eastward orientation toward the back of the stage is a geometry anchor that CR-E05 §3.2 (Bagley placing the shot to the east) has nothing to sit beside. Recording the anchor is not the same as asserting any connection between them.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 (Rule 1102 table, Ex. 6 description) and §4.4 publication bullets
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Ex. 6** — her position in the amphitheatre; the beginning of the presentation; **no act of violence depicted**" — and the Ex. 6 bullet explains non-publication as "not all alleged victims' faces were obscured."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull testified that Wright's 1102 statement identifies who is in the video: "Herself and **her two young children**." The defence's objection had rested on this from the outset: "the video contains images of minor children, which I know the state has made an effort to redact, but nevertheless, the reference to the minors, I think, would still fall under the protection." Hull also gave the substance of Exhibit 6.1 — the only recording-layer content of any admitted 1102 in the block: "It states that she's confirmed that she did review the video and that it was a true reflection of the video that she took on September 10th, 2025."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Minor children in the frame is the whole reason the blurring and classification fight happened, and without it the "faces not all obscured" ruling reads as a generic victim-privacy call. The 6.1 wording matters separately: it is a bare "true reflection" verification with no mention of any alteration — which is the exact contrast D-52 rests on, since CR-E04's quotation of Exhibit 12.3 has language expressly addressing zooms and highlights.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.2 (the speaker-label table — the file's self-declared most important caveat)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "| **Ryan McBride** | **The examining prosecutor, whom the court repeatedly addresses as \"Mr. Sturgill.\"** There is **no \"Sturgill\" label anywhere in the file** |" — the reader is left to assume "McBride" is a mis-rendering or a phantom.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "Mr. McBride" is a real person present at the State's table, distinct from Sturgill. When the court polled the parties before playing Exhibit 9, it addressed the State's side and observed: "And to the state, are your screens secure so they're not viewable? All right. Thank you. **Seeing Mr. McBride nod his head**, we can go ahead to the state representative." Within the same minutes the court addresses the examining attorney by a different name — "Mr. Sturgill, you may continue," "Anything further, Mr. Sturgill?" — so both are State counsel and the label is co-counsel's name attached to lead counsel's turns.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.2 is billed as the file's most important caveat and is now QUEUE.md standing hazard 9, so its precision matters more than any other passage's. The failure is not invention — it is a real attorney's name misapplied — which means a future reader must not mechanically rewrite every "McBride" label to "Sturgill" without checking content, and must keep open that some turns elsewhere in the day could genuinely be McBride.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "⚠ **Exhibit 6.1 — the statement whose unredacted version carried personal identifiers — had already been displayed on the courtroom screen and captured by the media camera before the publication framework was clarified.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The record is more favourable to the court than this reads, in two respects. First, the judge affirmatively kept the unredacted version off the public screen: "I want to make sure that's not coming on screen. It's just coming on my screen to review it." What was displayed and filmed was the redacted version, after the judge had already ruled it "admitted into evidence and may be published." Second, the framework was not unclarified — the court said so: "What my ruling **when we came back from break** was if you are objecting specifically to the exhibit and then to the exhibit being published in the courtroom and then the exhibit being published, which can be captured by media. If that's not specifically addressed, I am going to allow it." What happened at 04:56:54 was the court restating an existing default and holding the defence to it, not filling a gap. CR-E05's own §2.1 dates the framework's first articulation to 02:08:53.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: As written the sentence invites the inference that unredacted personal identifiers reached the public feed. They did not, and this is a legal-care section where a sentence liable to be quoted onward should be exact. Standing hazard 4: an unwarranted characterisation running against a party is as reportable as one running for it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent. §2.1 records the three-level framework and the lectern-monitor incident but not this.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: After discovering the unredacted 6.1, the court imposed a standing procedural requirement on the State for the remainder of the hearing: "just for clarity moving forward, if there is a particular exhibit, I'll ask that you provide it instead of me relying upon here, just so there's no misunderstanding and I can see exactly what is being moved into evidence. I don't want to assume… and I want to do the proper analysis." The court also stated its allocation posture on publication: "I would prefer argument on this issue from both sides. **This is the burden of the state**, so I don't want to exceed my lane by just assuming."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both are rulings of general application in the same family as the three-level framework §2.1 preserves, and the second is the court expressly placing the publication burden on the State — useful context for every subsequent publication ruling on Days 1–5.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 (the Rule 1102 architecture paragraph); cf. §4.3 which does cite a subsection
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.3 cites "**URE 1102(b)(5)**" for the ME report, but §4.4 names no subsection for any of the four video 1102s.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State relied on Rule 1102(b)(8) four times, and once wobbled on the record: "it was gathered in compliance with the Utah Rules of Evidence 1102, specifically subsection B8… As I stated, **B3 or B8**." Thereafter consistently "(b)(8)" (Phillips, Farnsworth, Olsen). The State also formulated the reliability basis carefully on 8.1: "it's under oath… **Or not under oath**, but pursuant to a notification to the declarant that a false statement made is punishable."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file cites the subsection where it knows it and leaves a hole where it does not; a reader cannot tell whether (b)(8) was the basis or whether the record is silent. The "not under oath" concession is also the State's own characterisation of the weight these statements carry, and is worth having verbatim.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.3 (the ME report) — boundary-adjacent to this block
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**ADMITTED over defence hearsay and confrontation objection**" — the objection is recorded as an objection to the exhibit.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence objected first to Hull's TESTIMONY about the autopsy, independent of any exhibit, and the court expressly declined to rule at that point. Nestor: "if this is not personal knowledge, we object to the hearsay if someone told him all of this. I don't believe this individual was present at the autopsy, so we object to any testimony about the autopsy or what he was told about it." The State: "I'll just simply lay foundation for the report itself." The court: "as it hasn't been moved into evidence just yet, I'm not making a ruling… If you wish to lay more foundation, that's certainly your choice." Hull then confirmed he and Davis met the doctor at the ME's Office "within a few days of the incident" but could not recall the date or time.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 9002–9025 (06:00:38–06:01:10), continuing to 9089 — one line past this block's end at 06:00:35, flagged as boundary-adjacent
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The objection to the oral autopsy testimony preceded and is distinct from the objection to Exhibit 11, and the court's non-ruling is why the State pivoted to laying foundation for the document. Whether Hull's autopsy testimony was ever received over objection, or only the exhibit was, is a real distinction CR-E05 currently collapses. Flagged for whoever holds the adjacent block.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**every civilian video came in as Rule 1102 written hearsay through Hull, with not one of the five source witnesses present**" — with Olsen (UVU) listed in the same table as Wright and Phillips.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The four sources in this block are not one category. Wright and Phillips are bystanders who shot the video themselves. Farnsworth is a commercial contractor — "TPUSA had a videographer, Visual Impulse" — whose company's fixed cameras recorded it. Olsen recorded nothing at all: he is the UVU official "responsible for that system" who verified institutional CCTV as a custodian, and the defence's objection to his 1102 was correspondingly a custodian-competence objection — "the individual basically states they verified the recordings but doesn't say how, doesn't say whether they viewed it, doesn't say whether someone else viewed it and told them."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Civilian video" is doing real work in the file's headline. Institutional CCTV verified by a records custodian raises a different reliability question from bystander phone video verified by the person who shot it, and the defence attacked them on different grounds. Flattening them makes the Rule 1102 architecture look more uniform than it was.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The garble list covers SBI personnel, the drone operator, "Erica Kirk," "Mr. Cook's presentation" and "Bayliff," and concludes "**No name in this file should be treated as verified orthography.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two further hazards in this block. (1) The witness's own name and rank are unstable in the same passage: the prosecutor says "You've seen this video, **Agent Hall**?" and later "From what we've heard from **Sergeant Hull**" — against "Agent Hull" everywhere else. (2) The court twice calls a State exhibit a plaintiff's exhibit — "What I have in front of me, **plaintiff's exhibit 6.1**" and "I'm going to go ahead and grant the publishing of **Plaintiff's Exhibit 7.1**" — interchangeably with "State's Exhibit." Rev also emits bare "Speaker 11" and "Speaker 12" for unidentified voices at 05:30:05 and 05:43:49.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Standing hazard 3 requires writing "State's Exhibit N" precisely because numbers are not unique across parties — and the Day 1 record itself uses "plaintiff's" for the State's, which is a trap for anyone searching or cross-referencing exhibit numbers by party. The Hall/Hull/Sergeant variance is a garble class the list does not currently warn about: the principal witness's own name.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Counsel for the news media then intervened** (05:09:43), arguing that the UCJA classification rule governs court-file records rather than in-court exhibits and that the public has a qualified right of access. **The court revised its ruling**…" — the rule/right framing is captured; the operative reasoning and one acquisition lead are not.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The argument the court actually adopted was about the magistrate's reliance: "when we are in a public proceeding and the State is presenting an exhibit that you are relying on, and the public is being denied the chance to see it. That is a fundamental violation of the right of access… **the public is entitled to see what you're seeing so that they can understand what your decision-making process is.**" He also conceded the exhibit-by-exhibit approach for material "so prejudicial that they cannot be shown in public, **that is not this**… This sounds pretty anodyne to me. **It's not even depicting the shooting**" — a characterisation the court effectively accepted. And he referred to a filing: EMC "should be allowed too, **for reasons that we briefed**." The court's own reasoning tracked him: "in recognizing the argument from the media, I see the differentiation, and how they are differentiating the rule that was cited versus what was presented."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The reliance rationale — the public may see what the magistrate relies on — is the reasoning that governed publication for the rest of the hearing, and it is more portable than the rule-vs-exhibit distinction alone. "For reasons that we briefed" also points at a media brief on electronic media coverage; §2.1 knows of an amended media motion on portable devices, but whether that is the same filing is not established here and is worth naming as an acquisition item.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: D-52 cell: the foundation change overnight was "most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement, since the 12.3 language CR-E04 quotes expressly addresses the alterations ('the only changes are some zooms and red highlights') while the 12.3 admitted on Day 1 at 05:46:10 evidently did not, or the objection could not have succeeded."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Day 1's Exhibit 12.3 ALREADY contained the alteration language. Arguing for 12.1 on Day 1 the prosecutor told the court: "if you refer to Mr. Olson's written statement, it's plaintiff's exhibit 12.3. He, too, has reviewed this video, and he has also identified this video as being accurate with the exception of those additions. In his words, it's the zooms and the red highlights. They weren't part of the original recording, according to Mr. Olson." That is materially the same sentence CR-E04 quotes. The court's ruling confirms it: "what I have is the original video, and Mr. Olson saying, 'This is the video, minus the alterations.' And we have Agent Hull saying, 'This is the video and there are alterations,' but I'm missing a link." The missing link was a declarant for the alterations, not a description of them.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's own headline register entry rests its only hypothesis on an inference the transcript it cites refutes. It also misdirects Q-52: the resolving question on Day 2 is not "was 12.3 amended" but "what new artifact or declarant did the State supply." Resolving D-52 against the wrong hypothesis would produce a false finding.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The State announced it would prepare and offer an unaltered version the next day, and the day ended early." File is silent on the rest of the plan.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State's plan was to offer BOTH: "our intent is to prepare an original version of the video that has been in dispute today without the circles, without the blur and without the zooming in… introduce that tomorrow as a different exhibit," and then "if that is admitted, we do intend to introduce that exhibit 12.1 as well." The State invited the judge to review 12.1 overnight expressly so "you could compare that to the version that doesn't have the circle, the blur and the zooming in."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is a stated mechanism for how 12.1 got admitted on Day 2 — a clean comparator exhibit, not a rewritten 1102 — and it sits in the same passage the file cites for D-52. Omitting it is why the file's hypothesis went the wrong way.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The exclusion is framed entirely as the court sustaining the defence's authenticity objection: "The defence objected on authenticity… The court SUSTAINED the objection."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The dispositive point was raised by the COURT, unprompted, after argument closed: "Do you have a version of this video that does not have alterations, such as zooming or circling?… that seems to fall outside the 1102, because you don't have a person testifying 1102 saying, 'I made the alterations.'" The judge expressly disclaimed any sinister reading — "I say manipulate to, not saying it in a nefarious way." The State then CONCEDED: "We don't, not right now, not today," and offered "I know who that person is. We could actually call that person as a witness if that would cure that, and we're prepared to do that if necessary."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: It changes who drove the exclusion and records that the State knew the identity of the person who made the alterations, could have called them, and did not — a fact bearing directly on D-52 and on any assessment of the compilation's chain of custody. It is also a both-directions point: the judge's non-nefarious framing is favourable to the State and the file drops it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "State's Exhibit 12.1 — the UVU surveillance compilation prepared by the Utah County Attorney's Office." No individual named.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull named the producer: "Utah County Attorney's Office. I believe Ms. Derfler is the one that produced the video," first name "Kimberlie." Note the careful distinction the transcript supports: Derfler is identified as producing the compilation; the record does NOT establish who made the zooms, circles and blurring — the State later said only "I know who that person is" without naming them.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The missing Rule 1102 declarant is the whole of D-52, and the file has no name for anyone in that chain. This is a concrete acquisition target the file lacks, and the produced-vs-altered distinction is exactly the anchor/connection separation the project requires.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Only "the four-campus-visits timeline rests solely on UVU surveillance review." The content of the timeline is never stated.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull testified: "We were able to establish that Mr. Robinson had been on campus approximately four times throughout the day, twice before the shooting, the time of the shooting, and then after the shooting later in the evening into the early hours of the 11th." He confirmed all four visits were captured by UVU surveillance video, and that the video he personally reviewed covers the 10th plus "a very small portion, I think about 0:30, of the 11th."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the State's Day-1 account of the accused's movements — the substantive core of the video evidence — and a reader of CR-E05 alone learns only that a count of four exists. The file hedges the timeline without ever recording it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hull repeatedly said 'the vehicle we believe to belong to Mr. Robinson'; the wheels are 'fairly unique'." The vehicle is never identified and the route from name to vehicle is never described.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The name went to "our SIAC or our State Information and Analysis Group," which produced a "workup" — driver's licence records, DMV records, addresses, photographs, associated vehicles. Robinson's produced a photograph, an address, a date of birth, and a DMV-associated vehicle: a Dodge Challenger, "silver in color," with "two registered owners… Mr. Robinson and then his mother." Hull testified the workup is what allowed the video search to be re-run for a specific person and a specific car.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The vehicle is the sole link between the doorbell footage and Robinson, and the file's own hedging paragraph turns on it while never saying what it is or how it was tied to him. The co-registration is a documented limit on the attribution (the car is not solely his) and belongs in the record, attributed.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The defence objected that it was unduly suggestive (14th Amendment due process)." Only the suggestiveness ground is recorded.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The renewed objection at 07:39:28 carried a second, distinct ground the file drops entirely: "Also, we believe there's a lack of foundation establishing his ability to interpret the surveillance video." The first objection (06:37:44) was made on "constitutional grounds" generally and elaborated as the single-defendant-at-counsel-table problem, with Nester deferring to "Mr. Burt" — a defence lawyer the file never names.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Whether a case agent who watched surveillance footage can competently interpret it goes to the reliability of the entire identification, not just the courtroom staging of it. Preserved objection grounds are exactly what a later reader needs; and the file's 14th-Amendment tag actually attaches to the second objection, not the first.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The 12.1 objection is recorded only as an authenticity objection to unaccounted alterations.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence made a second, separate application: that the video "be classified as protected under UCJA 4-202.02" subsection five, "J as in jelly bean," sub-parts (i) and (ii), because publication would "interfere with the defense's ongoing investigation" and Robinson's "ability to get a fair trial." Its substantive prejudice argument was: "This is basically putting together photos that are clear with photos that aren't clear, putting them all together in such a format that it makes the case that it's all one person," and it would be "extremely prejudicial for people that may ultimately serve on this jury." The court never reached it, having excluded the exhibit.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A rule-cited protective-classification request is a distinct legal event, and the "makes the case that it's all one person" argument — that the compilation itself performs the identification — is the sharpest defence attack on the surveillance evidence anywhere in the block. §7's against-the-prosecution list omits it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "…admitted over objection, with Ex. 13 (Ms. Noble's 1102) as foundation." No objection ground, no foundation contest, no date recorded.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Exhibit 13 was contested on a ground unique in the block: "Agent Hull amended this himself, and there's no foundation as to when he filled that in, if it was before or after she signed it." Hull had testified the file names on the form were "my handwriting on the 1102." The court then expressly invited more foundation — "Do you wish to lay more foundation about when the statement was written, whether it was before it was signed or not?" — and the State supplied it: collected April 6, at the residence, Hull present while she prepared it and witnessing her signature. The court's admission ruling turned on the sequence: it noted the confirming sentence and "right before that statement is the notations that were allegedly made by Agent Hull."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the only point in the block where the investigating agent's own handwriting inside a witness's sworn substitute-for-testimony is litigated, and the only 1102 where the court demanded supplementary foundation before admitting. It bears on the reliability of the whole Rule 1102 architecture §4.4 headlines. The April 6 date also matches the Wright/Phillips collection dates in the §4.4 table, indicating a single 1102 sweep the file does not surface.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.4 records publication outcomes for Exhibits 6, 7, 8 and 9. §4.5 records no publication outcome for Exhibits 13 or 12.2.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Both were published at the highest level. Ex. 13: "I will authorize publication in the courtroom and by the media if they so wish to capture it," with a prescribed display protocol — first portion on screen ~10 seconds, scroll to the written portion ~15 seconds, then scroll to the very bottom. Ex. 12.2: "admitted over the objection, and may be published in the courtroom and by the media if so chosen," and it was then PLAYED in open court with sound (the judge asked; the State: "it's night sounds. It's crickets chirping").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The three-level framework is a §2.1 headline of this file. Exhibits 13 and 12.2 are the only exhibits in this block to clear all three levels, and the court's specific display protocol is a concrete instance of the framework in operation. Omitting them leaves the file's publication record incomplete for the day it claims to cover end to end.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Ex. 12.2 — a sequence of short doorbell videos of a vehicle at about 00:38 on 2025-09-11."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull described and then narrated the content under oath: the vehicle "arriving in front of the residence, an individual exiting the vehicle and moving away from it, followed by an individual returning to the vehicle and unlocking it. And then it shows the vehicle a short time later starting and leaving the area." On playback: "There's an individual who gets out of the vehicle. You can hear the door close… There's actually two reflective panels on a dumpster, and you can see the individual pass those reflective panels," then "the individual comes back across those reflective panels to the vehicle, unlocks the vehicle, and gets into it."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The evidentiary point of 12.2 is a person leaving a car, going out of frame, and returning — not merely "a vehicle." The file's one-line treatment gives a reader no idea what the State said this exhibit shows. Note also what Hull did NOT say: he made no facial identification and described nothing carried to or from the vehicle.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent on any unresolved foundational gap in Exhibit 12.2.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence objected that it could not tell "if this is a compilation, or if this is just one of the one, two, three, four, five, at least six videos they took from the Nobles… is this just a portion, or is this the whole thing?" The State conceded "That's a good point" and laid more foundation, but Hull's answer left the gap open: 12.2 "does" consist of "either some or all of those videos that you showed Ms. Noble," and is "a number of short videos sequenced" — he had earlier said it was "four separate short videos" and that "the one shown on the statement was shown to Ms. Noble." The court admitted it by applying "the same analysis" as its previous rulings without resolving the subset question.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Whether the admitted exhibit is co-extensive with what the 1102 declarant actually verified is the same defect that killed 12.1 an hour earlier — and here it was not cured, merely not pressed. That asymmetry is a finding about how the Rule 1102 architecture actually held up.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "An off-record conference at 07:15–07:37 — announced as a ten-minute break for counsel to confer, running some twenty-two minutes — is not in the transcript. The State's next act was to end the day; whether the two are connected is not established."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The recess is announced at stream 07:15:47 and the court returns at stream 07:37:54. Per the file's own §1.3 and the project's standing hazard, "timestamps are recording-stream time, not time of day, and the clock jumps across each recess" — so no duration may be computed across a recess. The record itself gives the only clock anchors: the court says to return "at, well, roughly 4:30," and later "We have about 19 minutes until 5:00."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file performs, in an open-items list, precisely the operation its own caveat section forbids, and then builds a soft insinuation on the derived number ("the State's next act was to end the day"). Left standing it will be quoted forward as a fact about the length of an off-record conference, which the Rev rendering cannot support.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hull and Agent Davis personally visited Dr. Guajardo within a few days and had 'a fairly in-depth conversation' about the autopsy." Nothing on how the report reached him or on his distance from the examination.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The provenance chain is thinner than the file implies. The defence's stated basis for its first objection — "I don't believe this individual was present at the autopsy" — went uncontradicted; Hull never claimed attendance. He could not recall the date he received the report, could not recall the date of the meeting with the doctor, and described receipt as "provided to us electronically… Sometimes via email, also on disc, compact disc." His authentication was format familiarity only: reports "are in a standard format that the medical examiner uses," and nothing was "peculiar" about this one — "it appeared to be a standard form." He needed to consult a document to pronounce the doctor's name.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file calls Exhibit 11 "the most operationally valuable single fact in Day 1" and the decisive artifact for Q-15/D-49. Standing hazard 8 — provenance is a separate verification act from content — means the acquisition target's chain matters, and the entire chain here is one agent's format recognition of a document he received by unspecified means on a date he could not name.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "ADMITTED over defence hearsay and confrontation objection."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two further grounds are dropped. (1) An express request to voir dire: "If they're presenting him as an expert in this field based on the limited questions about his experience and seeing previous medical exam records, I'd like to voir dire him on his qualifications to opine about it." The court never ruled on it. (2) A reliability argument that survives the rule's enumeration: "even though 1102 has a provision about exams… the court still has the overarching mission under 1102 to make this reliability finding, right? And it's just completely in a vacuum being offered by someone who's a police officer." The court's ruling cited Art. I §12 and Rule 1102(b)(5)'s enumeration and made no express reliability finding on the record. There was also an earlier, separate hearsay objection at 06:00:38 on which the court declined to rule — "as it hasn't been moved into evidence just yet, I'm not making a ruling."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: An unruled voir dire request and an unanswered reliability argument are preserved appellate points, and they are the strongest reading of the defence's position — which the project's steelman rule requires be shown before the admission is recorded as routine.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "07:46:07 — Hull admonished and left on the stand overnight — 'you are still on the stand for all intents and purposes.'" File does not say who sought the admonition or why.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence asked for it, on a stated conflict: "I recognize that Agent Hull is the case agent and is working with the state in preparing for this, but he is still on the stand and I would ask that he be instructed that he can't discuss his testimony. Even though he's the case agent, I don't think it's proper for him to discuss his testimony while he's excused for the night." The State did not oppose: "It's not a problem, Judge." The witness was then excused only "For now, Your Honor."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the same tension §2.1 records at the start of the day — Hull and Davis exempted from the exclusionary rule as case agents — resurfacing at its end, now with the exemption cutting against the integrity of an unfinished examination. It is a defence-favourable evidentiary-integrity point and belongs in §7's against-the-prosecution list.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Exhibit 13 (Ms. Noble's Rule 1102 statement…) carries a Nest-versus-Ring inconsistency in how the camera is described. Recorded as an internal inconsistency in an admitted document."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The inconsistency is between the witness's spoken testimony and the document, not internal to the document. Hull consistently said "Ring": "We collected Ring doorbell footage," "It was a Ring doorbell video that was provided," "his vehicle on that Ring doorbell camera." The court, reading from Exhibit 13, quoted: "I confirmed that the above files were taken from our Nest doorbell videos and are accurate." Only one brand appears in the document as read into the record.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file frames it twice as internal to the exhibit, which would send a later reader looking for two brands inside one document. The real discrepancy — the officer's oral testimony versus the declarant's own words — is the more useful form of the flag, since it bears on how closely Hull's narration tracked the underlying documents.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §4.5 gives only "Hull personally watched perhaps 10–20 hours that day." §1.3 treats stream timestamps as identifiers with no clock mapping available.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two further quantities and three clock anchors are on the record. Hull put the UVU footage containing Robinson or his vehicle at "probably about 16 hours," and his own viewing as covering the 10th plus "about 0:30" of the 11th; the defence estimated the disputed 12.1 compilation at "just about five minutes." The court spoke three real-clock references: return "at 3:25" after the afternoon break (stream 06:29:03 on resumption), return "at, well, roughly 4:30" (stream 07:37:54 on resumption), and "We have about 19 minutes until 5:00" (stream ~07:42:51).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The 16-hour figure is the State's own measure of how much footage the identification rests on. The spoken clock references are the only real-time anchors in the block and would let a later reader place the Day-1 afternoon and independently observe the recess jump — a small correction to the file's blanket treatment of time as unmappable (over-hedging is a defect too).

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §1.4 records the State's PII handling only in its failure mode — the unredacted Exhibit 6.1 the judge caught. §7's for-the-prosecution paragraph does not mention exhibit handling.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Exhibit 13 was offered in redacted form and the redaction was put on the record before admission: "the personal identifying information appears to be redacted. Is that right?" — "It has been redacted, yes" — "It wasn't redacted when you collected it, right?" — "No, no the original form was not redacted." A residential street address was nonetheless spoken aloud in open court during the same foundation sequence (this report does not reproduce it, consistent with §1.4).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The both-directions rule requires logging the counterweight: by the later exhibits the State was redacting and saying so on the record. An audit trail that records only the failure is itself a bias signal — the project's own stated test.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.2, table row 1 ("Richard Novak → Officer Chris Bagley")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Rev merged the witness and his cross-examiner into one label" — offered as the mechanism behind the Novak/Bagley collision.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Bagley's cross-examiner is NOT Novak. Cross runs under the "Kathy Nestor" label, and the court names her in the adjacent turn: 04:20:05 (Nestor label) "Okay. That's all I have. Thank you, Your Honor. I tender the witness." → 04:20:06 (Judge) "Thank you, Ms. Nestor." Direct ran under the "Chad Grunander" label ("Mr. Grunander, your witness," 44:40). I parsed all 1,410 turn headers between the oath (line 641) and the excusal (line 6283): Richard Novak 589, Chad Grunander 476, Kathy Nestor 211, Judge 96. Of the 589 Novak-labelled turns, only 7 end in a question mark and all 7 are the witness's own clarifications ("Can you hear me?" 01:09:43; "Of the video?" 04:15:47; "Exhibit 35, I think?" 04:17:49). No examiner's question anywhere carries the Novak label. Rev merged the witness with a defence lawyer who did not examine him at all on Day 1.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.2 is flagged as "THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT IN THIS FILE" and states the rule every later reader must apply. The stated mechanism is wrong, and it contradicts CR-E05's own §2 ("cross (Nester)") and §3.5. A reader told the collision is witness+cross-examiner would distrust the Nestor-labelled cross — the very stretch §3.5 calls "the most defence-favourable stretch of Day 1" — and could reassign Bagley's answers to it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Timestamps are recording-stream time, not time of day, and the clock jumps across each recess (CR-E03 §1). They are identifiers."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On Day 1 the clock does not jump across any recess. (a) Direct evidence: the recorder ran through the mid-morning recess — "Speaker 6 (01:45:56): All rise" … nine "Court Attendees" turns timestamped 01:49:21 through 01:58:55 … "Speaker 6 (01:59:16): All rise, court is back in session." (b) Anchor test: the court's own spoken wall-clock references all fit ONE constant offset of ≈ +8h56m — 01:45:47 "So, 10:43 … Around 10:44. Let's come back at 11 o'clock" (offset 8:57:43); resumption 06:29:03 after "come back at 3:25" (8:55:57); lunch "at noon for one hour" taken 02:56:54 and resumed 04:04:41 (8:59:06 / 8:55:19); 07:42:51 "We have about 19 minutes until 5:00" (8:58:09); call to order 06:57 at a 9:00 a.m. setting (8:55:03). Anchors on BOTH sides of the ~1-hour lunch recess agree within ~3 minutes; had the media stopped for lunch the post-lunch offset would differ by ~60 minutes.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: An unqualified factual claim about the primary artifact, imported from CR-E03 §1 (a claim about other days) and never tested on Day 1. It is an over-hedge in the direction the project's hazard 4 warns about: it tells later readers Day 1's timestamps carry no temporal information when they in fact convert with a single stated offset. It also makes CR-E05 internally inconsistent — §8 item 11 measures "some twenty-two minutes" across exactly the recess §1.3 says the clock jumps. NOTE: I am asserting this for Day 1 only; I did not test Days 2–5, and my wall-clock anchors are the court's own approximations.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §1.3 lists the garble as "Sergeant **Falmina** (**Faumuina**)" with no in-transcript source; §4.1 then states "⚠ **probably Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina, but UNCONFIRMED** … **the transcript does not make it, and this file does not either**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: day1.txt contains the correct spelling itself. At 24:19 the State's lead prosecutor lists the anticipated witnesses: "And lastly, Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina, also of the Utah Department of Public Safety." That is the same day, the same hearing, the same rank and the same agency as Hull's "Sergeant Falmina" (04:29:29, 04:32:57). Counts in day1.txt: /Faumuina/ = 1, /Falmina/ = 2.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt line ~528 (stream 24:19, inside Grunander's turn beginning line 517 at 23:50); Hull's garbled uses at 04:29:29 and 04:32:57
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 4 — an unwarranted hedge is as reportable as an unwarranted assertion. The file says the transcript cannot make the identification when the transcript makes it in plain text 4 hours of stream time earlier. §1.3 should carry the 24:19 locator, and §4.1's "UNCONFIRMED" should be regraded. The Faumuina identification is load-bearing for the crime-scene-management assignment that links Day 1 to CR-E02 and CR-E03 §5A.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "a further **07:15:47–07:37:54** off-record conference (announced as a ten-minute break) is absent" [from the record].
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Three problems. (1) The stated bracket is not a timestamp jump — a transcribed turn falls inside it: "Bailiff (07:19:21): All rise." The actual gap in the transcript is 07:19:21→07:37:54. (2) The break is on the record, not absent from it: at 07:15:47 the court announces "Ladies and gentlemen, we're going to take a 10-minute break for the attorneys to confer and come back at, well, roughly 4:30. So court is in recess," and the resumption is transcribed at 07:37:54 ("We ended with the parties, the attorneys discussing how would we like to proceed?"). What is unrecorded is counsel's private conference during a recess — which is not part of any court record, certified or otherwise. (3) The file misses the actual unrecorded sidebar sitting at the head of the sequence: "Ryan McBride (07:15:45): Judge, could we approach?" / "Judge (07:15:47): You may." — an approach requested and granted whose content never appears.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §8 item 11 makes this an acquisition target and asserts a 22-minute duration derived from the wrong bracket. A researcher ordering the certified transcript or the recording would be looking for a transcription failure that is not there, and would miss the granted bench approach at 07:15:45–47, which is the one thing genuinely off-record at that point.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "a timestamp jump from **06:39:46 to 06:40:55** spans the bench conference on the in-court identification" (repeated at §4.5 and as acquisition target §8 item 6).
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The transcript places the bench conference AT 06:40:55, not inside the jump. The 06:40:55 turn opens with the court's request and then runs straight into the ruling with no intervening timestamp: "Judge Tony F. Graf, Jr. (06:40:55): Counsel, please approach the bench. All right. Based off what's been presented in court, I'm not finding that particular question, as previously posed as suggestive. I find, for the purposes of this hearing only, that in-court identification by Agent Hull of Mr. Robinson has been made…" The next turn is at 06:41:22. So the conference is un-timestamped and cannot be fixed to the 06:39:46→06:40:55 window. That a bench conference occurred is separately confirmed at 07:39:54 ("That's my recollection of the bench meeting") — the substance of the file's claim holds; only the bracket does not.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §8 item 6 names the bracket as what to request from the certified transcript or the recording. The bracket as stated is contradicted by the transcript's own placement of "Counsel, please approach the bench," so the target should be stated as "the unrecorded interval inside the court's 06:40:55 turn," not as a jump preceding it.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.4 ("Twice, private individuals' details entered the proceeding")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Two incidents are listed: the unredacted Exhibit 6.1, and the street address spoken aloud. The file is silent on any third.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: A third exhibit-redaction incident is on the record, ~35 minutes of stream time after the Exhibit 6.1 one. Arguing against State's Exhibit 8.1 (Farnsworth's Rule 1102 statement), defence counsel says at 05:29:47: "I don't have a redacted version of 8.1, but I assume there is one. There is personal information on this one. Do you have the… Okay, I don't have that one." The court then checks at 05:30:23 — "Ms. Nestor, I just wanted to check, did you get a copy of the redacted-" / "I was just handed it" (05:30:26) — and the State subsequently refers to the statement "in its redacted form" (05:32:44). Whether an unredacted 8.1 ever reached the courtroom display is not established by the transcript.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt 05:29:47 (continuation inside the Kathy Nestor turn at 05:28:54); 05:30:23–05:30:31; 05:32:44
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.4 says the Exhibit 6.1 incident is recorded because it is "a fact about the State's exhibit handling that the defence and the court both remarked upon." A second, same-shaped incident on the same day converts the State's "a little bit of a glitch" from a one-off into a pattern in the redaction workflow — which is exactly the fact §1.4 exists to preserve. The count "Twice" is under-inclusive.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "⚠ **Exhibit 6.1 — the statement whose unredacted version carried personal identifiers — had already been displayed on the courtroom screen and captured by the media camera before the publication framework was clarified.**" The file records no countervailing fact.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The transcript contains the strongest available evidence that the unredacted identifiers did NOT reach the courtroom display or the media feed, and CR-E05 omits it. When the State offered to bring the document up electronically, the court said: "All right. I want to make sure that's not coming on screen. It's just coming on my screen to review it… I can look it on my screen because I'm trying to evaluate" (04:50:40). Only after the redacted substitution ("state's exhibit 6.1 with redactions is admitted into evidence and may be published," 04:54:41) does the display-and-filming exchange occur (04:56:26 onward).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions rule. §1.3 bullet 4 juxtaposes "the statement whose unredacted version carried personal identifiers" with "captured by the media camera," leaving the inference that identifiers were broadcast, and the mitigating fact — the judge's explicit instruction keeping the unredacted copy off the courtroom screen — is nowhere in the file. On the project's most legally sensitive item (a named private individual's PII), an audit trail that records only the failure is a bias signal.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.2, table row 5 ("David Hull → Defence counsel, preserving objections | 07:40:43, 07:41:37, 07:43:00")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Three instances, characterised as defence counsel "preserving objections."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two corrections. (a) The list is incomplete: the "David Hull" label carries defence counsel five times, not three — 07:40:43 "Just a moment, Your Honor"; 07:40:48 "No, Your Honor"; 07:41:37 "I mean, I made my objection already"; 07:41:40 "No, thank you, Your Honor"; 07:43:00 "Your Honor, we're happy to accommodate the state on that." Each follows a turn in which the court addresses the defence (07:40:34 "Does the defense want to be heard?"; 07:42:51 "Does the defense wish to be heard about ending for the day?"). (b) Only 07:41:37 is objection-preserving; 07:40:43 is a placeholder and 07:43:00 is a scheduling accommodation. (There is a possible sixth at 05:52:37, "It's three minutes, Your Honor," answering "How long is this video?" — genuinely ambiguous between witness and counsel, so I do not count it.)
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The extent column is the operational part of the table — it tells a later reader which turns to reassign. Two of the five mislabels are missing, and the "preserving objections" gloss mischaracterises two of the three that are listed.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Another witness's street address was spoken aloud in open court** (~06:57:20) while foundation was laid for a doorbell-camera exhibit."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The address is spoken by the prosecutor at 06:56:59, inside the question. 06:57:20 is the witness's answer — "Yes. That's in the [neighbourhood] area. Yep." — which contains no address. (Detail deliberately not reproduced.) The rest of the claim checks out but by a two-step link the file does not state: the residence is identified at 06:58:39 as belonging to "Mr. and Mrs. Noble," who supplied the Rule 1102 statement admitted as State's Exhibit 13 (07:02:56, 07:05:09), which is what makes the occupant "another witness."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The locator points at the wrong turn, and it matters here more than usual: anyone re-verifying §1.4 will open the cited timestamp, find no address, and either conclude the file is wrong or widen the read — which is the opposite of what a PII locator should do. It also under-records that the utterance came from the State, not the witness.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Day 1's stream begins at **06:57** with the call to order."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The stream begins at 00:00: the first turn in the transcript body is "Speaker 1 (00:00): (Silence)." The call to order — "Bayliff (06:57): All rise. The court [inaudible 00:06:57], Judge Tony F. Graf, Jr., presiding." — is 417 seconds into the stream.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Small, but §1.3 exists to fix the reader's frame for every timestamp in the file; the stream origin is the one number that frame rests on. It also matters for the offset test above, where 00:00 rather than 06:57 is the zero point.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The list names Sterk/Sturgill, Falmina, Elschultz/Elle Schultz, Bricker, Clark, Cam Nelson/Ken Nielsen, Erica/Erika, Mr. Cook's, and Bayliff — "flagged where known."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Four unlisted garbles bear on names CR-E05 itself uses. (a) Nestor/Nester: the speaker label is "Kathy Nestor" (302 occurrences) but the court and counsel are rendered saying "Ms. Nester" (50) — including at 43:18 and 04:20:06, the two turns that functionally identify her. CR-E05 uses both spellings inconsistently (§1.2 "Kathy Nestor", §2 "cross (Nester)"). (b) "Mr. Gernander" once for Grunander (23:33) against 514 "Grunander". (c) The witness Hull is rendered "Agent Hall" (05:02:36), "Agent Holt" (06:52:04) and "Sgt. Hull" (06:49:07). (d) "Mr. Olson" (4) alongside "Mr. Olsen" (20) — the §4.4 table's Exhibit 9 / 12.3 source witness.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The list's purpose is to let a later reader recognise a garble when they meet one. Every one of these four attaches to a person CR-E05 names in a finding, and the Nestor/Nester split is the one that made me have to settle the cross-examiner question by content rather than by label.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent on non-printing characters in the rendering.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Eight lines of day1.txt consist of a lone zero-width joiner (lines 204, 1908, 3634, 5379, 7171, 8736, 10066, 10948). Seven fall at turn boundaries and are harmless; line 10066 falls MID-SENTENCE inside the Exhibit 12.1 exclusion ruling: "…for those reasons, I'm going to sustain the" / ZWJ / "objection, and leave it to the parties on how you wish to handle the video." tsearch.py flattens whitespace but does not strip the ZWJ, so /I'm going to sustain the objection/ returns exactly 1 hit in day1.txt — and it is the ME-report ruling at 06:11:18, NOT the 12.1 ruling.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt line 10066 (inside the Judge/06:53:26 block, mislabelled "Ryan McBride"); other ZWJ lines 204, 1908, 3634, 5379, 7171, 8736, 10948
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 5 trap sitting inside the file's headline finding #1 and D-52. Anyone re-verifying the 12.1 exclusion by searching the ruling's own words will get a false null from the project's own tool, on the single passage that most needs re-verification.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "the drone operator is 'Sergeant **Cam Nelson**' at 02:54:06 and 'Sergeant **Ken Nielsen**' at 04:18:21 — **the same person, named two ways by the same witness**" — asserted flatly.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The transcript never says they are the same person, and the two answers respond to different questions. 02:54:02: "Do you know who put the drones in the air?" → "Sergeant Cam Nelson with the Provo Police Department" (post-shooting drone deployment over campus). 04:18:19, on cross about the provenance of State's Exhibits 1, 2 and 3: "Do you know who was operating the drone?" → "Sergeant Ken Nielsen from Provo Police Department." Both are Provo PD sergeants and the names are near-homophones, so the inference is strong — but it is an inference.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Anchors-vs-connections. Two verified renderings do not verify the asserted connection between them. The claim should be graded (Medium-high) rather than stated as fact, particularly since one instance attaches to the provenance of admitted exhibits (1, 2, 3) that §8 item 5 already lists as unheld.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Every one of Bagley's answers**, ~44:17 through 04:22:08"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The 04:22:08 endpoint is doubtful as an answer of Bagley's. The court asks at 04:22:05 "May this witness be excused?" — a question to counsel; the Nestor label answers "Yes, your Honor" at 04:22:07, and the Novak label then says "Yes." at 04:22:08. The last unambiguous Bagley answer is 04:21:57 ("And that's where I could see straight up where the line of sight was"). The 04:22:08 turn is more likely the State's answer swept into the Bagley voice-cluster. The block extent 44:17–04:22:08 is right; the description of its final turn is not.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Minor, but §1.2's whole point is that content beats labels; the endpoint is a place where the file has taken the label's block boundary rather than the content. Better stated as "the mislabelled block runs ~44:17–04:22:08; Bagley's last answer is at 04:21:57."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Six failure rows and the flat statement that "Day 1's diarisation fails so badly that reading it from the labels would produce a corrupted record." No row records a label Rev got right.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Large parts of the label set are correct, and the transcript states the basis. "Richard Novak (18:16): Thank you, Your Honor. Richard Novak for Mr. Robinson" — self-identified, and the court says "Mr. Novak" in the immediately preceding turn (18:04); the label is correct for 18:16, 19:37, 19:41. "Ryan McBride (42:54)" is correct — the court says "All right. Mr. McBride" at 42:49. "Chad Grunander" is correct throughout Bagley's direct ("Mr. Grunander, your witness," 44:40). "John Wilson (10:16): John Wilson, KSL News" is correct — the court addresses "Mr. Wilson" at 10:18. The "David Hull" label is correct for essentially all 379 of its turns bar the five identified above. And within row 6's own bracket, the operative words "… is not admitted" (06:54:26) carry the CORRECT Judge label.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions and, more practically, calibration: a section that lists only failures gives a later reader no way to know which labels are usable, and invites either paralysis or ad-hoc reassignment. The rule §1.2 states ("name a person only where there is a stated basis, normally the court addressing them by name in an adjacent turn") is exactly what makes these five determinable — the section should show it working in both directions.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The parties had already stipulated that **no preliminary-hearing exhibits would be available for inspection or copying**, the defence position being that broadcasting an exhibit \"is essentially giving a copy to\" the public."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The quoted words are the COURT's, not the defence's. Judge Graf at 21:44: "…on the exhibits that the court grants to be published in court and not, going to Mr. Novak's point, not to be given copies to, and the court is trying to be mindful that if it's shown on TV, **that's essentially giving a copy to**." What defence counsel Novak actually said at 18:52 was the opposite of an equation: after noting the prior stipulation that "none of the exhibits would be available, from the preliminary hearing, would be available for inspection or copying," he expressly conceded "**I understand that publishing the exhibits in the courtroom may technically be different than that**." The judge went further than the defence did; the file assigns the judge's stronger formulation to the defence. (The stipulation half of the sentence IS Novak's and is accurate.)
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 445–456 (18:16–18:52, Novak) and lines 485–504, quote at line 496 (21:19–22:44, the court)
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is precisely the error class §1.2 is built to prevent — a judge's words attributed to counsel — occurring inside the file itself, and it overstates the defence position by dropping Novak's own concession. It also sits uncited: no timestamp is given for the quotation, so a later reader cannot check it.

not_verified_items.target_section: §1.3 (timestamp caveat, file line 52) — bears on the whole §2 table
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Timestamps are recording-stream time, not time of day**, and the clock jumps across each recess (CR-E03 §1). They are **identifiers**. Day 1's stream begins at 06:57 with the call to order."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Neither half survives a Day-1 test. (a) The stream begins at **00:00** ("Speaker 1 (00:00): (Silence)"); 06:57 is the call to order, ~7 minutes in. (b) The "clock jumps across each recess" claim is imported from CR-E03 (Days 2–5) and Day 1 contradicts it: all 2,684 timestamp blocks are strictly monotonic from 00:00 to 07:46:52, and the recesses are INSIDE the stream (silence blocks timestamped at 27:27 and 03:24:00). Two independent judicial clock statements bracketing the lunch recess agree to within about a minute on a single constant offset of ≈ +8:57 — at 01:45:47 the court says "So, 10:43… Around 10:44" (offset ≈ 8:57), and at 07:42:51 "We have about 19 minutes until 5:00" (offset ≈ 8:58). Four further anchors are consistent: "come back at 9:35" at 27:26; return at 02:08:08 after "come back at 11 o'clock"; lunch recess at 02:56:53 against "recess for lunch at noon"; return at 04:04:41 against "court will resume at 1:00 PM"; return at 07:37:54 after "come back at, well, roughly 4:30."
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt line 206 (00:00); lines 369–376 (14:59–15:21, the schedule); line 3375 (01:45:47); lines 5393, 5405 (02:56:53, 04:04:41); lines 10733, 10741 (07:15:47, 07:37:54); line 10861 (07:42:51). Monotonicity checked programmatically over all 2,684 timestamp blocks.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 4 — an unwarranted hedge is as reportable as an unwarranted assertion. On Day 1 the stream is a single continuous recording convertible to clock time within a minute or two, which would let the library place every Day 1 event on the clock (e.g. cross-check Bagley's testified 12:23 shot and 12:44 roof arrival against the stream). The file discards that for a caveat it never tested on this day. I am NOT recommending the file start converting timestamps unilaterally — this contradicts a standing project hazard and the orchestrator should adjudicate it — but the caveat as written is unsupported for Day 1 and the correction to "the stream begins at 06:57" is unambiguous.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Discovery was not complete.** The State disclosed (42:54) that additional SBI materials received \"over the last week… due to preparation for this hearing\" had **not yet been provided to the defence** and would be produced \"as soon as this hearing is complete.\" **The defence cross-examined without the newest SBI material.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every quoted fragment is verbatim correct, but the file takes only the adverse half of a three-part exchange. The same turn opens: "My report at the last hearing is the latest report. **As of June 18th, we had provided approximately 100% of the material in our possession.**" The immediately preceding turn (Grunander, 42:33) states "the state has provided copies of **all exhibits for today's proceedings** to the defense in advance of this hearing." And immediately after, the court asked "Defense, require the benefit of the record?" — Nestor: "**No, Your Honor**" (43:17). No defence objection, motion or complaint about discovery appears anywhere in Day 1 ("discovery" occurs 4 times in the whole file; the other three are unrelated).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The both-directions rule is a procedure, not a preference. §7 then lists "discovery incomplete at the time of cross" under "Against the prosecution" with no counterweight anywhere in the file, so a reader is left with a discovery-deficit picture that the record does not support: production was represented as ~100% complete three weeks earlier, all Day 1 exhibits were pre-provided, and the defence expressly declined to be heard.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Sergeant \"**Falmina**\" — ⚠ **probably Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina, but UNCONFIRMED.** …**the transcript does not make it, and this file does not either**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: day1.txt itself supplies the name, correctly spelled, with first name and agency, in the State's opening witness roadmap: Grunander at 24:19 — "And lastly, **Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina, also of the Utah Department of Public Safety.**" Hull's two garbled references ("Sergeant Falmina," 04:29:29 and 04:32:57) are to a DPS/SBI sergeant announced in the same hearing as a State witness and assigned the crime-lab-coordination task that CR-E02/CR-E03 record Faumuina giving evidence about.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 4 directly. The file asserts a scoped null ("the transcript does not make it") that a search of the same transcript refutes — and §6A's standard is that a null is a claim about the search. The correct spelling was available in the file being read and was missed, which also means §1.3's garble list understates what Day 1 itself resolves.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Row 1 reads only: "06:57–~40:00 | Call to order; appearances; **decorum, media and publication rulings**; exclusionary rule invoked; the two case agents permitted to remain"
