not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The same block contains the State's roadmap for the whole hearing, which is the yardstick for "the shape of Day 1" and is nowhere in the file: Grunander at 23:50–24:19 named **four** witnesses — Bagley, Agent David Hull, Agent Brian Davis, and Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina — said exhibits 7, 8 and 9 "will be graphic in nature" and asked for a short break before any publication of them, said one exhibit would be in physical form on an easel, and stated "**we do anticipate admitting between 40 and 50 exhibits**." Day 1 got through one witness and part of a second.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Three separate downstream uses: it quantifies how far short Day 1 fell (1.25 of 4 witnesses; ~16 of 40–50 exhibits), it supplies the Faumuina spelling above, and it shows the graphic-exhibit publication treatment recorded at §4.4 (Ex. 7 "the State itself asked that it not be published"; Ex. 8 publication denied) was flagged by the State in the opening minutes rather than arising ad hoc.

not_verified_items.target_section: §5 and the D-52 register row (file lines 241, 245)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The State announced it would prepare and offer an unaltered version the next day**" … and D-52: "So something changed in the foundation overnight — **most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement**…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State stated its mechanism on the record and it is not the one D-52 speculates about. At 07:42:11: "our intent is to prepare an original version of the video… without the circles, without the blur and without the zooming in. And our intent is to introduce that tomorrow **as a different exhibit**." At 07:43:21: "our intent is to seek to admit the version where it doesn't have the circle or the blur or the zoom in. **And if that is admitted, we do intend to introduce that exhibit 12.1 as well** … I think it would be helpful if you saw that in advance and **you could compare that to the version that doesn't have the circle, the blur and the zooming in**."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: D-52 asks what changed in 12.1's foundation overnight and answers with a guess about an amended Rule 1102 statement. The record contains the State's own announced plan — admit the unaltered original as a separate exhibit, then re-offer 12.1 authenticated by comparison against it — which is a simpler and better-evidenced hypothesis and sharpens what Q-52 should look for on Day 2. Omitting it leaves the register entry speculating past the evidence in its own source file.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The exclusionary rule was invoked by the defence.** On defence stipulation \"**for purposes of this hearing only**,\" **Agents Hull and Davis were permitted to remain** throughout." / table: "the two case agents permitted to remain"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The agents were not the only exception. Immediately on invoking the rule the court stated (16:06): "Of course, **victim representative is excluded from that rule as is the case manager** pursuant to the rules." Related and also unrecorded: at 02:08:08 the court modified its own decorum order for victims — under Art. I §28, victims and victims' representatives "can come back whenever they wish. They're not prohibited to coming back solely at the break" — an express carve-out from the 08:48 rule that anyone leaving may not re-enter until the recess.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The bullet reads as though the two case agents were the sole exception to witness exclusion. The victim-representative carve-out is the legal basis on which Erika Kirk was present throughout (a fact §6A records without its basis), and the 02:08:08 ruling comes from the same turn the file mined for the three-level framework at 02:08:53 — the file read that turn and took only half of it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent on the court's objection protocol.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: At 14:20–14:42 the court set the procedure that produces the transcript's gaps: "When an objection is made, all parties shall pause… **Speaking objections are not permitted. If any party believes that an extended argument is necessary, particularly on sensitive matters, that party may request to approach the bench and all parties will approach the bench.**"
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.3 flags "Two conferences are missing from the record" and §8 item 6 makes the 06:39:46–06:40:55 bench conference an acquisition target. The court's stated protocol is the explanation: bench conferences on sensitive matters were ordered as the default and are inaudible by design. Without it a reader may read the gaps as a rendering failure rather than normal courtroom practice.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**A broadcast-security failure, caught by the defence** (01:04:49)… The court granted the defence request and the lectern monitor was switched off."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Accurate as far as it goes, but the two measures that make it a "failure" are unrecorded. (a) At 21:44–22:44 the court had already ordered the publication monitor "placed against that wall… right behind Jeff, our bailiff" specifically "to reduce the possibility of it being broadcast" and "to minimize the accidental capture by the camera." (b) At 55:37, on the first exhibit, the court ordered: "let's go ahead and **not publish it until it's admitted into evidence**… So table monitors, witness, but not the main monitor." The 01:04:49 leak was therefore a third screen (the lectern) defeating two standing precautions. Also unrecorded: the court left the door open — "if at any point, Mr. Grunander, you do need to use the monitor, let's revisit that. And obviously, Ms. Nester, you can renew your objection."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's own §1.3 records that unadmitted Exhibit 6.1 reached the media camera; §2.1's bullet records a second, earlier leak. Both were failures of a specific, articulated safeguard, and the safeguard is what makes them reportable rather than merely procedural.

not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every item listed in that row concluded at 27:26, when the court recessed for placement of the publication monitor ("let's just come back at 9:35"). Court did not resume until 42:20. Nothing occurs at or near 40:00 — it falls inside the recess. The only business between 42:20 and the first witness at 43:27 is the discovery report the file books separately in §2.1.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The row silently absorbs a ~15-minute recess, and the table's four rows present Day 1 as contiguous when it contains at least four recesses (27:26–42:20; 01:45:56–02:08:08; 02:56:54–04:04:41; 07:15:47–07:37:54, the last of which §1.3 flags separately). A "shape of Day 1" table is exactly where the recesses belong.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The State ended the day early and undertook to rebuild an unaltered version overnight" / "and the day ended early" / "**The State's next act was to end the day**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: True but thinner than it reads. The court's own words fix the size of it: at 07:42:51, "**We have about 19 minutes until 5:00.**" The State's stated reason was practical — "we just can't prepare that in the next hour or so. So, we're going to need this evening to prepare that exhibit" (07:42:11). And the break was agreed, not unilateral: at 07:38:17 the State said "we're all in agreement that we want to break for the day," and when the court asked "Does the defense wish to be heard about ending for the day?" defence counsel answered "**Your Honor, we're happy to accommodate the state on that**" (07:43:00).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Ended the day early" and "the State's next act was to end the day" invite an inference that the exclusion routed the day; the record shows roughly nineteen minutes, a stated logistical reason, and defence concurrence. §8 item 11 then asks whether the 07:15–07:37 off-record conference and the early end "are connected" — a question worth less once the nineteen minutes and the concurrence are on the page.

not_verified_items.target_section: §2 table row 3 (file line 74) vs §4 (line 160); and name orthography throughout
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §2: "04:22:48–end | **Agent David Hull sworn**"; §4: "**Sworn 04:22:54.**"; §2: "cross (**Nester**)" vs §1.2: "**Kathy Nestor** (defence counsel)"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Both timestamps are real and refer to different acts: the oath is put at 04:22:48 and Hull answers "I do" at 04:22:54. Rev's speaker label is "Kathy Nestor" throughout; the court is transcribed saying both "Ms. Nestor" (15:42, 04:04:55, 04:18:53, 04:20:06) and "Ms. Nester" (43:18, 01:05:17, 02:10:37, 04:57:47).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Neither is an error of fact, but a file whose central caveat is attribution discipline should not cite one swearing-in at two different times in two sections without saying which act each marks, nor spell the cross-examiner two ways. §1.3's blanket "no name in this file should be treated as verified orthography" covers the garbles but not internal inconsistency.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "At the bottom he was told on the radio 'we had a shooter in custody' — within roughly a minute."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The record gives ~30 seconds twice, and the witness expressly REJECTED "a minute." Cross, 02:54:50 — Q: "how long do you think between the shot being fired did you hear that?" A: "I was in, like I said, trying to get down the stairs, jumping over people... **Within 30 seconds maybe.**" And at 04:06:02 counsel put it to him that "It took you **a minute** to kind of navigate the stairs" — he corrected her: "Yeah. So **about 30 seconds** to get down the stairs." He also said (02:55:31) "within seconds the other officer... said that he was in custody." A full-text search of day1.txt for /minute/ (25 hits, all read) produces no witness estimate of a minute anywhere in Bagley's testimony.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file has adopted the one figure the witness affirmatively corrected, and it doubles the interval. It is also internally inconsistent with the file's own §3.5 ("taken into custody within ~30 seconds") and §7. The shot-to-custody interval is load-bearing: it is the premise of the "wrong person detained" finding and of his "Oh, that was kind of fast" reaction.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — §3.1 narrates the shot in detail (12:23, right side of body, simultaneous lean, the run down the stairs) but never records how many shots he heard
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Cross, 02:52:13 — Q: "So you heard the shot and **you only heard one shot**, correct?" A (02:52:21): "Yes." This is the only place in Day 1 where the number of shots heard is put to and answered by the closest police witness.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The number of shots is a first-order checkable fact from the nearest sworn observer, and it is one of the recurring public questions about this event. Its absence means a reader of §3 cannot tell whether Day 1 addressed it. It also bears on §3.2's rifle-vs-handgun reasoning (a single report) and on §3.3's single-casing search.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — §3.3 records the gravel disturbance, the "sniper pad" line and the photograph qualification, but nothing about what else the witness said the photographs show
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Describing State's Exhibit 5 on direct, 02:29:00: "You can see more of the length of an individual. So you can see that more of there's two elbows, two knee areas, plus also **towards the far right of the photo is also a marker where somebody laid a gun down**." (02:29:15) "It's like a prone position." This is a distinct, admitted-exhibit description of a marked gun-laydown impression on the roof.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Three consequences. (1) §3.3 omits the single most probative thing the witness said the rooftop scene showed after the body impression. (2) The file's §3.3 analyst layer says "the perch produced nothing" — the perch, on this testimony, produced a marked gun-laydown impression. (3) §6A's scoped null states "The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged 'long black object'" — that is false on the face of the transcript. (The proper caveat is that this is the witness reading a marker placed by someone else, not a gun recovered; the recording-layer fact still belongs in the file.)

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He also found no unfired bullets on the roof." — and then the analyst layer: "This independently corroborates... that no bullets or casings were found on or immediately around the Losee building." The file stops there.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The very next two questions after the unfired-bullet answer, 04:11:58–04:12:10: Q: "Are you aware of there being **a bullet found on another roof**—" A: "I'm not aware." Q: "...in the vicinity? Were you aware of **another bullet being found on the scene not on the roof of the Losee building**?" A: "No."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's corroboration claim is framed geographically ("on or immediately around the Losee building"), and defence counsel put to this witness, in that exact geography, the existence of a bullet found on another nearby roof and elsewhere on the scene. His "not aware" is not evidence a bullet was found — but the question is a recording-layer fact the file drops, and §6A's null ("no bullet recovery") reads as fuller coverage than it has. It is also the only /bullet/ hit in Day 1 outside the two answers the file does quote.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Describing the nighttime photograph: "to me, it looks like a sniper pad, a person that has been [lying there]"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: 02:26:12 in full: "To me, when I got up there and I could see this disturbance of gravel, to me, it looks like a sniper pad, a person that has been **laying in a prone position and you've got markings of elbows, knees, and feet to where somebody was in the line of sight of where Charlie's tent was**." The bracketed "[lying there]" replaces a clear, un-garbled twenty-eight-word continuation.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A square bracket in this library signals a garble-normalisation or a minimal grammatical fix; here it silently truncates the substance of the identification — the three-point body impression and the asserted line of sight to the tent. The file's own §6 tells later readers to carry "his qualification" of the photograph; it should equally carry what he actually said the impression consisted of. This is the selective-quotation hazard operating in the direction of understating the witness.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "⚠ **The holster was never collected.**" (bolded, flagged assertion) and, in §7, "the **uncollected, unfingerprinted holster**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness never said it was not collected. 02:53:27 — Q: "And what happened to that holster?" A: "**I have no idea.**" Q: "Did you ever take custody of it?" A: "Nope." Q: "Did you ever tell anyone else to take custody of it?" A: "Nope." Q: "You just left it on the grass?" A: "I did." Q: "Was it ever fingerprinted to your knowledge?" A: "**I have no idea.**"
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: What is established is that *this officer* did not collect it and does not know what became of it. "Never collected" is a claim about the world that the testimony does not carry — and the file contradicts itself two pages later, at §8 item 7: "Whether it was ever recovered or examined is unknown and is not established by anything read." A bolded ⚠ assertion is exactly where the analyst layer must not outrun the record.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "⚠ His own qualification is preserved: of the daytime photograph he said it 'does not do it justice'" — and, in §3.2, "...and 'just left it on the grass.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Both quoted strings are counsel's, not the witness's. 02:18:42 — Grunander: "And does this photograph **do it justice**?" Bagley: "No." 02:53:37 — Nestor: "You **just left it on the grass**?" Bagley: "I did." In each case the witness's own words are a bare assent.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's headline caveat (§1.2) is that Day 1 attribution must be reconstructed functionally because Rev's labels merge examiner and witness. Quoting an examiner's phrasing as the witness's speech reproduces in substance the error the file exists to guard against. The adjacent quotation the file gives — "I saw a distinct impression in the gravel and this does not show that" — IS the witness's and carries the same point, so the fix is subtractive.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3 (headline result 2; repeated in §6 and the revision log)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "the first officer onto the Losee roof, at 12:44" — stated flatly, four times in the file, with no inference marker
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: No witness and no party says he was the first officer onto the roof. Regex /(were you the first|first officer|first to arrive|first up)/ over day1.txt: 0 hits (method validated against the known positive). The nearest support is defence cross at 02:45:58–02:46:11: "when you got up to the roof, that afternoon, was anybody around that was law enforcement?" "No." / "Nobody on the roof?" "No." / stairway, walkway — "Nope." Complicating it, at 04:08:32–04:09:06 he confirms an unidentified man in civilian clothing wearing a badge and carrying a handgun went up **with** him — "I had somebody with me to back me up as I ran up the stairs" — and at 04:09:47 he describes officers "climbing up and looking, clearing the building."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The inference is a fair one and I am not asking the file to abandon it — over-hedging is a defect here too. But it is an inference from an absence-of-observation answer, not testimony, and the file's own §3.5 records that he did not go up alone. A headline claim repeated four times should say what carries it ("no law enforcement was on the roof, stairway or walkway when he arrived").

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He was on duty in the courtyard when Kirk was shot"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: He was posted on top of the Hall of Flags walkway at its south end, above and west of the courtyard. 01:02:41: "It was to secure the **top** of the Hall of Flags on the south end... So I was put up **on top of** the Hall of Flags on the south end." 01:35:01: "You were securing the Hall of Flags **walkway**... On the south end?" "Yes." 01:36:46: "I happened to glance **over the edge of the railing**." 01:37:58: "when I was **up there looking down**." §3.1 of the file states the post correctly; the §3 summary sentence does not.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: His elevation is not incidental: it is why he saw only the right side of Kirk's body, why he had to run down outside stairs "jumping over people," and why the file's own §3.5 records that a member of Kirk's armed security detail stood beside him "on top of the Hall of Flags." A reader taking §3 at face value places him at ground level in the crowd.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — §3.2 says only "In that pause he concluded the shot had been a rifle, not a handgun"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On direct at 01:42:00 he testified he said so contemporaneously, and was agreed with: "I turned to my chief and I said, '**That was a rifle shot.**' And he said, '**I agree.**' And I looked up at that moment; right in the line of sight, I could see the Losee building had a direct line of sight."
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt ~char 94673 (01:41:58–01:42:00; note the part-seam duplicating "the empty holster. I turned to my chief")
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the both-directions rule cutting the other way: a contemporaneous statement to a superior, agreed to on the spot, is materially stronger than a conclusion recounted ten months later, and it is the strongest available corroboration that the rifle inference preceded any camera evidence — which is exactly what §7 asserts for the prosecution without citing it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "simultaneous with the shot Kirk leaned to the left and **went down**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: 01:37:15: "At that moment, I saw him **lean to the left**..." 01:37:21: "I saw him **go to the left** because I could no longer see the right side of his body. He went further underneath the tent to the north side of the tent, so left." The word "fell" enters only in counsel's follow-up (01:38:35, "When he fell to the left?" — "Yes"). He never testifies to seeing Kirk go to the ground; his stated position was that Kirk passed out of his sight line under the tent.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Went down" asserts an observation the witness expressly could not make, in a paragraph whose whole point is the narrowness of his sight line. Small, but this is the file's most-cited eyewitness moment.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He ran down the outside stairs '**jumping over people lying on the steps**.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The quoted string appears nowhere in day1.txt. It is stitched from two passages a hearing-half apart: direct 01:38:55 — "people were running up, **people were laying down on the steps**. I'm trying to **jump over people** to get to the bottom of the stairs"; and cross 02:54:56 — "trying to get down the stairs, **jumping over people**, trying not to step on people."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The sense is exact and no reader is misled about the facts — but a quotation mark in this library is a promise of verbatim fidelity, and a composite of direct and cross presented as one utterance is not verbatim. Either quote one of them or paraphrase.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.3: "'As a matter of fact, no,' he could not find one." §6 then lists as a confirmed finding: "**No spent casing and no unfired bullet on the Losee roof**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness attached his own temporal limit, which the file drops: 04:11:25 — "I was looking over the edge, looking all over the place, making sure the gravel wasn't disturbed, and **I couldn't find a shell casing at that moment**." He left the roof at ~1:01–1:03 (02:32:47), handed it to a county deputy, and had already testified he never reviewed video for the window before his arrival, during which "there was people up there... clearing the building" (04:09:47).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §3.3's own grade — "Confidence: High **as to the testimony**" — is correctly pitched; §6's bullet is not, because it states the finding as a fact about the roof. Restoring the witness's four-word hedge costs the finding nothing (a purposive negative search is still the strongest form) and keeps the two layers apart.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §7: he "inferred a rifle from **its sound and the holster's presence**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Asked directly what grounded the inference, he gave sound only. 01:41:07 — Q: "And what causes you to say that?" A: "Just from **being around firearms through all my trainings**, the difference is a handgun is more of a short bang pop sound. With a rifle, you have more of a longer violent bang or crackle sound... That's why I recognized it." The holster is temporally adjacent in both his direct (01:40:24) and cross (04:07:42) accounts — the pause it caused is what let him process the sound — but he never offers it as a premise.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the anchors-versus-connections rule: two facts the witness reports in sequence are not a causal chain he asserted. §3.2's own phrasing ("In that pause he concluded...") is right; §7 converts the pause into a reason.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent — §3.1 goes straight from the radio call to "Reaching the tent, 'Charlie was gone.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two dropped items from the same answers. (1) 01:39:26–01:39:52: on hearing the threat was over he "started canvassing the area... looking for anybody that was injured," found a boy on the second or third grass tier next to a wheelchair "almost convulsing," whose father said "he was just having a seizure, that he was fine" — and he observed "no other injuries." (2) 01:37:58: his own crowd estimate, "several thousand people," itemised by location (grass, cement, second level by the Sorenson and Woodbury).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The medical canvass is the whole of what he did between the shot and the holster and is the only Day 1 testimony on casualties beyond Kirk; "no other injuries" is itself a scoped negative observation. The crowd figure is a checkable number from the witness, distinct from the pre-event "had an idea there'd be thousands" the file records at §3.5.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "Nobody was ever assigned to cover the Losee building")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Nobody was ever assigned to cover the Losee building**, and he does not know if anyone was."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The only exchange on the point is Nester: "did anyone ever talk to you about covering anything near or on top of or in the Losee building? Were you ever assigned that area before the shooting?" — "No." / "Do you know who was?" — "I don't." The testimony establishes that HE was not assigned and that he does not know who was; it does not establish that nobody was. A full-day tsearch on /assigned/ (method validated) returns no other Bagley testimony on Losee coverage.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: An unsupported negative asserted in bold, in the defence-favourable direction, and self-contradicted by its own second clause. It propagates to §7 ("no Losee coverage") and to the revision log ("nobody assigned to the Losee building"). Hazard 4 cuts both ways: this is an unwarranted assertion, not an unwarranted hedge.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "He never reviewed the video for the window…")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**He never reviewed the video for the window between the individual leaving the roof and his own arrival**, and **other people were on the roof during that window**, "looking for an individual that ran that way… clearing the building.""
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The quoted words are real but describe a different thing. Asked whether anyone else had been on the roof between the jump and his arrival, he first answered about the search HE had ordered after he was already on the roof: "There was people up there looking for an individual that ran that way because when I first got told the individual ran heading north… So we started climbing up and looking, clearing the building." Counsel then said "I think I either asked it badly or you misunderstood me" and re-put the question; he answered "Yeah, and I didn't see anybody" / "I didn't notice anybody," and only then agreed "No" to not having reviewed that period. The file records the final "No" and the mis-timed quote, and omits the two intervening answers.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Other people were on the roof during that window" is asserted as fact from a non-responsive answer, and it contradicts the same file's §3.3 ("first officer onto the Losee roof") and §3.5's own "there was no law enforcement on the roof, the stairway or the walkway" (02:45:58–02:46:11). The omitted "I didn't see anybody" answers cut against the defence point the bullet is built on.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Exhibit provenance was outside his knowledge.** He does not know who took Exhibit 35, where it came from, or how old it is. He first saw Exhibits 1, 2 and 3 "**a couple of weeks ago**," in preparation for testifying."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: True of Exhibit 35, false as a generalisation. Asked about Exhibits 1, 2 and 3 — "do you have any knowledge about where those pictures came from or who took them?" — he answered "I guess they were drone footage. Just taken from a drone," and, asked who operated the drone, named "Sergeant Ken Nielsen from Provo Police Department." On direct he had already identified State's Exhibit 3 as "a drone picture of the campus" (01:14:25). The §3.5 bullet drops the attribution entirely; it survives in the file only as a name-garble note in §1.3.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions failure: the one exhibit-provenance answer the witness could give is the one the section omits, leaving a blanket "outside his knowledge" that the record does not support.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "The nighttime rooftop photographs rest on hearsay")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Bagley's fair-and-accurate foundation is what she told him by telephone during trial preparation**, weeks before…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: True of State's Exhibit 4; not true of State's Exhibit 5. On Exhibit 5 the prosecutor asked Bagley directly: "With respect to what you observed that day, apart from the evidence tag, the yellow tag as well as the orange or red markers, is this a fair and accurate depiction of what you observed?" — "Yes." The court's admission ruling rested expressly on that: "Given the foundation that has been laid and that the witness has testified that this is a fair and accurate representation of the scene… State's Exhibit 5 is admitted."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The bullet's headline ("rest on hearsay") is overstated for half the exhibit pair. Exhibit 5 has an independent, first-hand fair-and-accurate foundation from the testifying officer, which is precisely the both-directions fact the file's own rules require it to log.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Asked why the mismatch with the shot's direction did not register: "**During [the chaos]…**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The answer is not a trailing-off. In full: "During the chaos moment, no. They said they had a person in custody. I figured those guys saw something I didn't see. They took that person in custody and I thought that was him." The ellipsis removes the whole substantive explanation.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Standing hazard 7 — reliable as to the words, not as to the answer. The truncation converts a coherent explanation into an apparent evasion, in the defence-favourable direction, inside the section the file says is recorded "in full because the both-directions rule requires it."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The wrong person was detained.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "The wrong person" is defence counsel's phrase, inside a question the witness did not adopt: "But it didn't occur to you that, 'Well, that's not where I heard the shot come from. They must have the wrong person. I should talk to somebody.'" Bagley's answer was "During the chaos moment, no… I thought that was him." No witness and no ruling states that the detainee was the wrong person; the file's own §6A records that the detainee is never named.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A recording-layer bullet states an analyst conclusion — one that presupposes who the right person was — as established fact. It sits badly with the file's own presumption-of-innocence header ("no court has found any fact below to be true"), and it propagates to §7 and the revision log.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "His report omits the direction of the shot")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**His report omits the direction of the shot** — "I don't see a direction" — and he wrote no supplement."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The very next exchange has him disputing the wider premise. Counsel: "you also don't state whether or not… You don't mention anything about thinking it came from the Losie building or anything like that, right?" — "Later on when I saw the empty holsters, when I… I think I actually said that in there, where I see the empty holster that I realized the line of sight." Counsel did not press it and moved to the holster.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions omission. The file records the concession and drops the (hedged) rehabilitation on the same subject, leaving "the report says nothing about direction" stronger than the record supports.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He **saw "a long black object in the left hand"** as the person crossed the roof; asked what it was, he said "**It looks like a rifle or something to that effect, a long object… like skinny and long**.""
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The question was not "what was it" — it was expressly hindsight-framed: "knowing what you know about the case today, do you have an idea about what that object was?" And the exchange ends the other way: "So you can see a towel, but you can't see an actual gun." — "I don't know if it was a towel or a blanket. I don't know what it was." / "But you can't see an actual gun in the video?" — "No. Like an object, like a form of a gun, like a long object." He also said of the object "it's almost like it's covered over something."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: As written, the rifle characterisation reads as an observation. On the record it is a hindsight inference the witness immediately qualified with an express "you can't see an actual gun." The "covered over something" / towel-or-blanket detail is dropped entirely although it is the reason he could not identify the object.

not_verified_items.target_section: NEW — not in the file at all (belongs in §3.5, and bears on §6A and §8)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Immediately after the casing/unfired-bullet questions, defence counsel twice put the existence of other recovered ammunition to the witness: "Are you aware of there being a bullet found on another roof—" — "I'm not aware." — "…in the vicinity? Were you aware of another bullet being found on the scene not on the roof of the Losee building?" — "No."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Counsel's question is not evidence, but the fact that the defence put a bullet found on another roof / elsewhere on scene to the first officer up is a Day 1 lead the file never records — and §6A's null "No ballistics, no bullet recovery" is stated without it. It is exactly the kind of item §8 exists to hold.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §6A: "**The rifle is never recovered, described forensically, or photographed** in this record. The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged "**long black object**" (§3.4)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Describing State's Exhibit 5 (the nighttime rooftop photograph) Bagley testified: "You can see more of the length of an individual. So you can see that more of there's two elbows, two knee areas, plus also towards the far right of the photo is also a marker where somebody laid a gun down." Earlier, on Exhibit 4, he described the impression as showing "markings of elbows, knees, and feet." Neither passage appears anywhere in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Sworn testimony that an admitted photograph carries a marker at the point where a gun was laid down is a second, non-hedged reference to a weapon on the roof, and it is a specific feature of an exhibit the library is trying to acquire (§8 item 5). The §6A null as phrased is inaccurate, and §3.3's description of the impression drops its most detailed element.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: he "**look[ed] at the footage to verify for myself exactly what [t]ranspired**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Rev reads: "I then look at the footage to verify for myself exactly what expired on that moment." The bracketed "[t]" implies the source read "ranspired"; it read "expired." A tsearch for /expired|ranspired|transpired/ across day1 returns exactly one hit — this one (method validated).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Silent repair of a garble inside quotation marks, in a file whose §1.3 practice is to record garbles as rendered and flag them. Small, but it is the one quotation in §3.4 that a reader checking against the transcript would fail to find.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**No drones** over campus before the shooting."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two things. The question was about "that day," not before the shooting: "as far as you know, were there any drones that were flying above campus that day?" — and the answer was hedged: "Not that I know of." Later he confirmed drones WERE in the air after the shooting, put up by "Sergeant Cam Nelson with the Provo Police Department."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's re-scoping to "before the shooting" is the correct reconciliation of the two answers and should be kept — but the witness's hedge is dropped, turning "not that I know of" into a flat negative. Mixed direction: the re-scoping is a fair reading, the de-hedging is not.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "His report omits the direction of the shot") vs §8 item 4
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "…and **he wrote no supplement**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The question was about a FURTHER report: "did you write any kind of supplement to your report to add onto your report other than what we've gone through today, that one report you wrote? Have you ever written another one?" — "I have not." But at 02:49:30 he testified that the report he did write WAS a supplement: "I did a supplement on it. I didn't prepare the report because the incident was a big agency assist."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: As phrased, §3.5 flatly contradicts §8 item 4 of the same file ("a supplement within a larger agency-assist report"). The accurate statement is that he wrote no further or corrective supplement.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He does not know who took **Exhibit 35**…"; "He first saw **Exhibits 1, 2 and 3**…"; "**Exhibits 4 and 5** were taken by Melissa Richards…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: All are State's exhibits, but the same cross-examination also runs on a defence-marked document, "Bagley 1" (his report), and at the moment it was called up the prosecutor interjected "State's Exhibit 1" — i.e. the numeral 1 is live for two different documents in the same passage.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Standing hazard 3. In the one passage where the ambiguity is actually realised on the record, §3.5 writes bare exhibit numbers. §8 item 4 gets it right ("used on cross as 'Bagley 1'"), so this is an internal inconsistency as well.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.1: "At the bottom he was told on the radio "**we had a shooter in custody**" — **within roughly a minute**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The direct (01:39:26) gives no interval at all: "By the time I got to the bottom of the stairs, I was informed on the radio that we had a shooter in custody." On cross the only interval testimony is "Within 30 seconds maybe" (02:54:56) and "about 30 seconds to get down the stairs" (04:06:25) — the latter given as a correction to counsel's loose preamble "It took you a minute to kind of navigate the stairs."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Roughly a minute" appears to have been taken from counsel's question, which the witness corrected, and it contradicts §3.5's own "~30 seconds" and §7's "within ~30 seconds" for the same event.

not_verified_items.target_section: §3.5 (bullet: "The nighttime rooftop photographs rest on hearsay")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Admitted over preserved objection under URE 1102 and Utah Const. Art. I §12.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Correct as far as it goes, but the State's answer to the hearsay objection — which the court then adopted — was broader: Rule 1102(b)(3) (hearsay admissible to establish foundation or authenticity), Rule 1101(c)(1) with Rule 104 (rules of evidence do not apply to preliminary questions of admissibility), and State v. Griffin, 384 P.3d 186 (Utah 2016), cited for the proposition that hearsay is admissible to lay foundation "even at trial."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Both-directions: the file logs the objection and the rule the defence is attacking, and omits the authority that makes the ruling unremarkable. It also matters for §4.4's Rule 1102 architecture, which the file treats as the central defence line.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**An unidentified armed man in civilian clothing accompanied him up to the roof** — visible on his body camera, wearing a badge and carrying a handgun. **Bagley does not know who he was or what agency he was from.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every element checks out, but the witness's explanation is dropped: "I don't know who he was exactly. He had a badge on and I had somebody with me to back me up as I ran up the stairs to make sure I had somebody with me." On the handgun, counsel asked "And it looked like he had a pistol?" — "Yes… A handgun, yes."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Minor, but the omitted clause is the witness's own innocuous account (a badged backup officer he took up the stairs with him), and the file elevates this item to §7 and the revision log.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Dispatch reported a male on the roof at the time of the shooting who "**ran to the edge, dropped down, crawled, got in a prone position**," then after the shot stood and ran northeast.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The account as relayed included the direction, which the prosecutor stopped to pin down: "Ran to the edge. What direction and what edge?" — "Running west and southwest of the Losee building, so ran towards the tent of where Charlie Kirk was so they could get a line of sight."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The omitted clause is the only part of the dispatch account that connects the roof movement to the tent, and it is the part the court's limiting ruling most obviously covers. Recording-layer completeness.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two further security-posture answers are not recorded: (a) asked whether any other law-enforcement agency besides Kirk's private security and the six UVU officers covered the event — "I don't know" / "No, not until the response came in" (02:47:08–02:47:31); (b) the six UVU officers were armed with "Glock pistols" (02:45:03–02:45:06).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Item (a) is a defence-favourable fact the file omits — noted so the audit trail is not one-directional. Both belong in a bullet list the file says is "recorded in full."

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On the crime-scene tape: "By the way, where did you get that tape?" — "Officers responded on the scene that he was down on the bottom and threw it up to me" — and he confirmed he neither had it on him nor left the scene to get it. Counsel then conceded: "But once you put the tape up, then we're confident from that point on the scene was preserved, right?" — "Yeah."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Pro-State material inside the section the file calls "the most defence-favourable stretch of Day 1": the defence itself conceded scene preservation from the taping onward, and the officer never left the roof to fetch tape. Logged for the both-directions rule.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "the drone operator is "Sergeant **Cam Nelson**" at 02:54:06 and "Sergeant **Ken Nielsen**" at 04:18:21 — **the same person, named two ways by the same witness**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The two answers are to different questions: "Do you know who put the drones in the air?" (after the shooting) — "Sergeant Cam Nelson with the Provo Police Department"; and "Do you know who was operating the drone?" (that took State's Exhibits 1–3) — "Sergeant Ken Nielsen from Provo Police Department." Both are Provo PD sergeants; the transcript nowhere says they are one man.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Plausible inference — but asserted flatly ("the same person") in the caveat section whose whole point is that no name in the file should be treated as verified. It should read as an inference, or the two references should be kept separate.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Sergeant "**Falmina**" — ⚠ **probably Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina, but UNCONFIRMED.** The crime-lab-coordination task matches her Day 2/Day 4 testimony exactly (CR-E02, CR-E03 §5A), which is why the identification is likely; **the transcript does not make it, and this file does not either**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: day1.txt contains the correctly spelled name, in the same day, in the State's own announced witness list: "The third witness will be Agent Brian Davis again with the State of Utah, a case agent who's here presently. And lastly, Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina, also of the Utah Department of Public Safety." The speaker is functionally the prosecutor announcing the State's case (the court addresses him as "Mr. Grunander" in the immediately following turn at 24:39). So the transcript supplies, from within Day 1 itself, a DPS sergeant named Jennifer Faumuina on the State's witness list, matching Hull's SBI/DPS "Sergeant Falmina" who was assigned crime-lab coordination. The file's own §1.3 already makes the identification — it lists the garble as "Sergeant **Falmina**" (**Faumuina**).
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt line 528, stream 24:19 (turn opened line 517, stream 23:50); cf. Hull at line 6659 / 04:29:29 and line 6791 / 04:32:57
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Three problems at once. (1) The premise is factually wrong: "the transcript does not make it" is false as to the name's presence and DPS affiliation — the correct orthography is in day1.txt. (2) The file contradicts itself: §1.3 makes the identification, §4.1 says "this file does not either." (3) It is an over-hedge (standing hazard 4). The honest calibration is not "UNCONFIRMED" but something like Medium-high on a same-document basis — one DPS sergeant on the State's Day 1 list, whose assignment matches. Under-identifying here also risks a false null later ('the library has no basis to connect Falmina to Faumuina').

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**ADMITTED over defence hearsay and confrontation objection**, under **URE 1102(b)(5)** … and Utah Const. Art. I §12."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence objection was broader and its lead ground was different. Ms. Nester: "this is an expert report without the expert being present, being offered by an individual who's not an expert in this field. If they're presenting him as an expert in this field … **I'd like to voir dire him on his qualifications to opine about it.** This is hearsay. It's highly technical. It should be presented only through an expert. **It could never come in trial in any other way.**" She then argued separately that "even though 1102 has a provision about exams … the court still has the overarching mission under 1102 to make this reliability finding … It's just completely in a vacuum being offered by someone who's a police officer." The express request to voir dire the witness was never ruled on — the court asked "Anything further from the parties?" and went straight to its ruling, which recited Art. I §12 and the categorical (b)(5) listing without any articulated reliability analysis.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §4.3 is the section the library will cite for how its "decisive artifact" entered evidence. Compressed to "hearsay and confrontation," the reader loses (a) the defence's actual lead ground — expert report through a non-expert, inadmissible at trial; (b) an unruled-on voir dire request; and (c) the fact that the court's ruling rested on the categorical rule rather than an express reliability finding, which was precisely the defence's second argument. All three are defence-favourable and belong in §7's both-directions list, which currently mentions none of them.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Q: "Prior to September 10th, 2025, how familiar were you with the Utah Valley University campus?" A: "Not very. I think I maybe had been there once before." He then described becoming "a lot more familiar" by walking the campus, viewing surveillance video, and general involvement in the investigation.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the factual predicate for a defence objection the file itself records the other half of. At 07:39:28 Ms. Nester objected to the in-court identification not only on 14th Amendment suggestiveness grounds (which §4.5 records) but also because "we believe there's a **lack of foundation establishing his ability to interpret the surveillance video**" — a ground §4.5 omits. The case agent who reviewed the campus surveillance and made the in-court ID had been on that campus perhaps once before the shooting. Recording the State's foundation build-up while dropping both the "once before" answer and the foundation objection is exactly the one-directional audit trail CLAUDE.md §Objectivity-1 warns about. (The §4.5 half is flagged here because it is adjacent to my span and would otherwise fall between assignments.)

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**State's Exhibit 11 is the nine-page report of examination.**" … analyst layer: "That report is Exhibit 11, **it is nine pages**, its author is named…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The page count is the examining prosecutor's, hedged, not the witness's and not read off the document: "And **I believe there's nine pages**. So let me know when you see that on your screen" (06:03:30), then "look at this as it scrolls down through the nine pages … I want you to be able to look at all nine pages" (06:03:38). Hull's only answers were "It's on the screen" and "Yes, sir"; asked what it was, he said "That's the medical examiner's report of examination for Mr. Kirk." No one else states a page count.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The substance holds up — the witness reviewed all nine pages, the judge had the document, no one contradicted the figure — so this is not a hedge-me-harder finding. But the file's own §0 rule is that "a quotation by an interested party is reliable as to the words, not the document," and here an analyst-layer assertion ("it is nine pages") traces to counsel's "I believe." One clause naming the source would fix it, and the count is one of the two identifying features by which the library will try to acquire the exhibit.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The autopsy date/doctor and the Hull–Davis visit to Dr. Guajardo are recorded as testimony, with no note that they were objected to.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The hearsay objection came first at 06:00:38, aimed at the autopsy testimony itself and before Exhibit 11 was offered: "if this is not personal knowledge, we object to the hearsay if someone told him all of this. I don't believe this individual was present at the autopsy, so **we object to any testimony about the autopsy or what he was told about it**." The State answered that it would "simply lay foundation for the report itself." The court expressly declined to rule: "So as it hasn't been moved into evidence just yet, **I'm not making a ruling**." No ruling on that objection as to the pre-offer testimony ever follows; the next ruling (06:08:50) is on the exhibit.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's first two §4.3 bullets are exactly the testimony that was objected to and never ruled on. A reader takes them as cleanly received Tier-1 testimony. Recording the unruled objection costs one clause and correctly qualifies the standing of the autopsy-timing and personal-visit facts.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "It is evidence about **recall under examination**, and **the defence used it that way**."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: On Day 1 the defence did not use it that way. Nester's objection was an accuracy objection: "Your Honor, I object. It's not stated as a murder. I believe it's stated as a homicide, which is an important distinction." She then added, separately, "I also need to make an objection on the Best Evidence Rule too." Nothing in Day 1 has the defence arguing from Hull's misstatement to his reliability or to the reliability of the 1102 hearsay, and — as §6A of the file itself states — there is no cross-examination of Hull on Day 1 at all. Searches of the flattened day1.txt for /misspoke/ (2 hits, both witness turns) and for Nester turns containing recollect|memory|misspoke|correct|notes (5 hits, all read) find no such argument.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 9353 (06:10:34), 9381 (06:11:12); method: ./tsearch.py, day 1, validated against the known positive
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Steelmanned, the Best Evidence objection is in substance an argument that the witness's characterisation should not stand in for the document — so the claim is not baseless. But as written it asserts a defence litigation posture that Day 1 does not contain, and the parallel claim at §4.4 point 3 ("The defence used these to argue that 1102 hearsay from absent witnesses is unreliable") compounds it. If the argument was in fact made, it was made on Day 2 cross, which this file did not read. Scope: I checked day1.txt only.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**Kirk's own security detail removed him from the scene** … conducted "**what would be called a hasty transport**" to **Timpanogos Regional Hospital** — in one of the team's own vehicles rather than waiting for an ambulance."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Three hedges in the witness's own words are dropped: "**My recollection is** that Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team removed him from the scene whilst administering first aid…"; "**I believe** he was thrown into one of the team's vehicles and then transported to the hospital as opposed to waiting for an ambulance"; "**I believe** it's referred to as Timpanogos Regional."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Recording-layer fidelity runs in both directions: the file is scrupulous about preserving the State's hedges in §4.5 ("the vehicle we believe to belong to Mr. Robinson", "fairly unique") but flattens them here, so §4.2 reads as firmer first-hand knowledge than Hull claimed. Hull was not present at the evacuation; every element of this bullet is his recollection or belief, and the file's next sentence (pronouncement known only via Officer Bullock) shows it knows the sourcing is second-hand.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "*(CR-E04 records that he **left SBI in March 2026** and is now an investigative sergeant at POST.)*"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The POST position is Day 1's own sworn testimony, not something the library owes to CR-E04: "What is your current assignment with the Department of Public Safety?" — "I'm currently positioned as an investigative sergeant at Peace Officer Standards and Training" (04:24:11), followed by "Was that your assignment in September of 2025?" — "No, it was not." Only the March 2026 departure date is outside Day 1: /March/ returns 0 hits in day1.txt (tsearch, method validated).
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 6415–6427, stream 04:24:08–04:24:19; null: /March/ 0 hits, day1.txt
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A fact established by the primary artifact under review is credited to a secondary library file. Minor in consequence but it is the exact provenance discipline the project runs on, and it mis-states which half of the parenthetical Day 1 can carry.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He was later directed to Utah Valley… **SBI was then designated the lead investigative agency, with Hull and Agent Davis as lead case agents.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Both directing officials are named or referred to and neither appears in the file. "Do you recall who directed you to come down to Utah Valley?" — "**I believe it was Lieutenant Jensen**" (04:27:44). And on the lead designation: "I was informed by **my lieutenant** that myself and Agent Davis would be taking lead on the investigation on behalf of the State Bureau of Investigations" (04:31:11).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The section is titled "The response, and who ran it" and the one named person in the SBI chain of command above Hull is dropped. "Jensen" is also absent from §1.3's garble list, so a later reader has no flag on the spelling. The designation was made by a lieutenant, not by the multi-agency command — a small but real fact about how SBI took the lead.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "a large multi-agency presence — **FBI, DEA, ATF**, "I think some US Marshals," plus state, county, city and local agencies"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull hedged the whole federal list, not just the Marshals: "There was a large law enforcement presence, federal entities, **I believe** the FBI, the DEA, ATF, **I think** some US Marshals."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Quoting only the second hedge implies the first three agencies were stated flatly and only the Marshals were uncertain. Selective quotation is reliable as to the words, never as to the turn (standing hazard 7). Trivial in substance; listed because the file elsewhere depends on being trusted for exactly this kind of hedge-preservation.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Sergeant Elle Schultz — "Work with the **SIAC** and other partners"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: "Sergeant Elle Schultz was working with the SIAC and **other administration** to try and **manage the flow of information that had started to occur**." Hull separately defines SIAC later as "our State Information and Analysis Group" (06:32:32).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Other partners" is a substitution for "other administration," and the assignment's stated purpose — managing the flow of information — is dropped, which is the only row of the four whose function the table does not actually state. The three other rows are rendered accurately, so this is a lone drift, not a pattern.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**This is the decisive artifact for Q-15 / D-49**" and "Q-15 names "the medical examiner's report + photograph" as decisive. **That report is Exhibit 11**…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Day 1 establishes only that Exhibit 11 is a nine-page "report of examination" in the medical examiner's standard format, received electronically or on compact disc. Nothing states or implies that it contains photographs. All twelve /autops[a-z]*/ hits in day1.txt fall inside 05:59:58–06:09:27 and none concerns imagery; /fragment/ returns 0 hits in day1.txt (tsearch, method validated against the known positive).
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 9177 (06:03:11), 9217 (06:04:49), 9241 (06:05:09); nulls across the whole of day1.txt
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's own analyst note is properly careful that Exhibit 11 "does not resolve D-49," but the headline and §8 call it *the* decisive artifact for a question the file says turns on "the report **+ photograph**." Day 1 locates the report half only; whether the photograph is inside Exhibit 11, in a separate ME exhibit, or not in evidence at all is unestablished. An acquisition target built on the assumption that Exhibit 11 answers the fragment count could come back empty.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: file is silent
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull described the inflow of evidence and gave a crowd figure: "We were getting a large volume of information from the general public, phone tips, people sending videos. **Analysts were scrolling through social media and social sites** as people were posting information onto the internet"; and "If you imagine there's **3000 people at an event** and everybody has a cell phone, there was a lot of information that people were willing to share with us."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "3000 people" is a checkable attendance number from the lead case agent and the library has only Bagley's "thousands" (§3.5) to set beside it. The social-media-analyst detail is also the only Day 1 indication that open-source monitoring fed the investigation. Both fall in the gap between §4.1's close and §4.4's opening and are recorded nowhere in the file.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The defence used these to argue that 1102 hearsay from absent witnesses is unreliable where even the case agent's recall needs correcting."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: No such argument exists in Day 1. Every defence objection during Hull's direct is on record and none of them mentions Hull's corrections: 04:42:16 (confrontation + UCJA 4-202.02), 04:46:58 ("it's difficult for the court to make a reliability finding when the individual is not here"), 05:03:21, 05:05:37 (UCJA 4-202.02(4)(R)), 05:16:48, 05:22:38 + 05:23:04 (Rule 403), 05:28:54 ("we don't know who, and we don't know how"), 05:36:00 (Rule 901), 05:44:56 ("verified the recordings but doesn't say how"), 06:08:18, 06:46:43, 07:03:36, 07:10:08. Hull was never cross-examined on Day 1 — the file states this itself at §6A. Method-validated tsearch for /misspoke|misspeak|corrected|correction/ returns 0 hits in day2.txt as well, so the argument is not made on Day 2 cross either.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the cardinal error the project guards against: an analyst inference written into the recording layer as something a party said. It puts words in defence counsel's mouth, and it is the sentence that converts three neutral memory corrections into an adversarial theme. §7 ("Hull's four corrections on the stand") inherits the framing.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: D-52 reasons that the foundation must have changed overnight, "most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement, since the 12.3 language CR-E04 quotes expressly addresses the alterations ('the only changes are some zooms and red highlights') while the 12.3 admitted on Day 1 at 05:46:10 evidently did not, or the objection could not have succeeded."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The Day 1 version of Exhibit 12.3 already contained that content, and it was read into the record before the exclusion. At 06:49:45 the prosecutor argued: "Judge, if you refer to Mr. Olson's written statement, it's plaintiff's exhibit 12.3. He, too, has reviewed this video, and he has also identified this video as being accurate with the exception of those additions. In his words, it's the zooms and the red highlights. They weren't part of the original recording, according to Mr. Olson." The objection was sustained four minutes later anyway, on a different ground.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's stated "most likely" resolution of D-52 is refuted by Day 1's own record — and the file's fallback ("or the objection could not have succeeded") is the inference that fails. D-52 should be re-opened on a different hypothesis, and the Q-52 acquisition target should be re-aimed at what the State supplied on Day 2 about the ALTERER, not at whether 12.3 was amended.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "nobody accounted for who made the alterations (zooms, red circles, face-blurring)"; §5: "no witness and no Rule 1102 statement accounted for who made those alterations."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The identity was stated on the record. Hull, 06:42:37: "Utah County Attorney's Office. I believe Ms. Derfler is the one that produced the video"; 06:42:43: "Kimberlie." And the prosecutor, 06:52:04: "I will proffer that those changes made to the video were not done by either. I know who that person is. We could actually call that person as a witness if that would cure that, and we're prepared to do that if necessary." The court's stated ground was narrower: "I do not have the person who made the alteration, an 1102 to substantiate that... I'm missing a link" (06:53:26).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Nobody accounted for who made the alterations" reads as ignorance of the alterer's identity; the record shows a named individual whom the State offered to call. The defect is evidentiary form (no sworn or 1102 account from her), not anonymity. It also hands the library a concrete, named acquisition target for D-52/Q-52 that the file currently lacks.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The State announced it would prepare and offer an unaltered version the next day, and the day ended early."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State announced a two-exhibit plan, not a replacement. 07:42:11: "our intent is to prepare an original version of the video that has been in dispute today without the circles, without the blur and without the zooming in. And our intent is to introduce that tomorrow as a different exhibit." Then 07:43:21: "our intent is to seek to admit the version where it doesn't have the circle or the blur or the zoom in. And if that is admitted, we do intend to introduce that exhibit 12.1 as well... it would be helpful if you saw that in advance and you could compare that to the version that doesn't have the circle, the blur and the zooming in."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: D-52's premise is that Day 2's admission of a still-altered 12.1 means "something changed in the foundation overnight." The record shows the State said on Day 1 that it would re-offer 12.1 alongside an unaltered comparator. That is a competing and simpler explanation, and it must be stated before D-52 can be resolved either way.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "A verbal identification — 'He is, yes' — came at 06:37:40; the defence objected that it was unduly suggestive (14th Amendment due process)... The defence renewed its objection."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: At 06:37:44 the objection was: "Your Honor, we object to unduly suggestive in-court identification for constitutional grounds" — no amendment cited; when the court asked her to specify (06:37:57) counsel gave only the single-defendant-at-counsel-table case-law point. The 14th Amendment / due-process framing appears for the first time at 07:39:28, on the renewal: "we would impose an objection based on the 14th Amendment for due process due to an unduly suggestive in court ID. Also, we believe there's a lack of foundation establishing his ability to interpret the surveillance video." tsearch for /14th Amendment|Fourteenth Amendment|due process/ across day1.txt returns that passage only.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two errors in one sentence: a ground is back-dated to the first objection, and the renewal's second, distinct ground — that no foundation established Hull's competence to interpret surveillance video — is dropped entirely. That second ground is a direct attack on the witness whose surveillance testimony carries CR-E04's movement findings, and it belongs in §4.5 and in §7's defence column.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Exhibit 13 (Ms. Noble's Rule 1102 statement...) carries a Nest-versus-Ring inconsistency in how the camera is described. Recorded as an internal inconsistency in an admitted document."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: It is not internal to the document. day1.txt contains exactly one word-bounded occurrence of "Nest" as a brand — the judge reading Exhibit 13's own text at 07:05:50: "I confirmed that the above files were taken from our Nest doorbell videos and are accurate." All three "Ring" references are Hull's sworn oral testimony (06:56:56 "We collected Ring doorbell footage"; 06:57:31 "It was a Ring doorbell video"; 06:59:53 "on that Ring doorbell camera").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The discrepancy is between the sworn testimony and the text of the very 1102 statement offered as its foundation — a sharper point than an internal inconsistency, and one that sits squarely inside §4.4's reliability theme. Mischaracterising it also under-states it, so the correction runs against the State and must be logged as such (standing hazard 4).

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "sixteen exhibits offered" on Day 1.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Twenty distinct State's exhibit numbers were offered on Day 1: 1, 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 6, 6.1, 7, 7.1, 8, 8.1, 9, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 13, 35. Nineteen were admitted; only 12.1 was excluded. No exhibit numbered 10 or a bare 12 appears (tsearch /[Ee]xhibit (10|12)[^.0-9]/ → 0 hits), and no defence exhibit was offered (/defense exhibit|defence exhibit/ → 0 hits). Spot-verified offers: Ex. 2 admitted 01:07–01:08, Ex. 3.1 offered 01:44:25, Ex. 3.2 offered 02:15:46, Ex. 35 offered 01:26:38, Ex. Eight offered/admitted 05:35:35–05:37:44.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's own §8 item 5 already lists eight scene-photograph exhibits, which with the eleven other admitted exhibits exceeds sixteen — so the headline is internally inconsistent as well as wrong against the transcript. It is the load-bearing number in the sentence that introduces the whole Rule 1102 architecture.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The bullet discusses "the vehicle we believe to belong to Mr. Robinson" and the wheels, but the file never says what the vehicle is.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull testified the SIAC workup on the Washington County name produced a DMV record with an associated vehicle: "The Dodge Challenger" (06:33:27), "It was silver in color, and I believe there were two registered owners of the vehicle" (06:33:32) — Robinson and a family member (06:33:39). At 07:12:15, asked what leads him to believe it is Robinson's vehicle: "The shape of the vehicle can be clearly seen as it pulls up, and the distinctive wheels on the vehicle also."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §4.5's hedging bullet cannot be evaluated, or cross-checked against CR-E02/CR-E04, without the make, model and colour. The co-registration is also part of why "we believe to belong to" is the accurate formulation — it is evidence for the hedge, not merely a hedge.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Four bullets covering Ex. 6, 7, 8, 9 only.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Every Rule 1102 written statement was itself admitted and published, most of them to the media camera: 6.1 "admitted into evidence and may be published" (04:54:41) and in fact filmed before the framework was clarified (04:56:26–04:57:26); 7.1 "published... in court, and that the media may capture that" (05:20:52); 8.1 "published both in court, and may be published by the media" (05:33:09); 12.3 "publish it both in the courtroom and so it can be captured by the media" (05:47:44); 13 "publication in the courtroom and by the media" (07:06:24). The court even scripted scroll-and-pause timings so the media could read them.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The section's four bullets leave the impression of across-the-board restriction. In fact the written hearsay — the part the defence said it could not cross-examine — went fully public while the videos were restricted. That inversion is the most interesting publication fact on Day 1 and it is absent.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Ex. 12.2 — a sequence of short doorbell videos of a vehicle at about 00:38 on 2025-09-11 — admitted over objection, with Ex. 13 (Ms. Noble's 1102) as foundation."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: 12.2 was not only admitted: "state's exhibit 12.2, I believe, is admitted over the objection, and may be published in the courtroom and by the media if so chosen" (07:11:39), and it was then played in open court with sound (07:12:26–07:13:55; the prosecutor: "There is, Judge, but it's night sounds. It's crickets chirping"). It is the only civilian video on Day 1 published to the public. The defence's objection also had a specific authenticity component the file omits — whether 12.2 was a compilation or a subset of "at least six videos they took from the Nobles" (07:10:08) — which forced the State to lay further foundation (07:10:48–07:11:26) before re-seeking admission.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Publication status is the file's own three-level framework (§2.1); omitting it for the one video that was fully published breaks the pattern the file is trying to establish, and the compilation-versus-subset objection is the same authenticity attack that killed 12.1 twenty minutes earlier.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Ex. 7 — admitted; the State itself asked that it not be published." The Ex. 8 and Ex. 9 bullets give only the court's reasoning.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State requested non-publication for three of the four videos. Ex. 7: "We would ask, however, that it not be published beyond that... due to the graphic nature" (05:22:17). Ex. 8: "it's our position that it not be published here in the courtroom, and that it not be published so that the cameras can display it" (05:35:35). Ex. 9: "we'd ask that it not be published here in the courtroom, nor published in any way that the media camera could capture it... out of deference to the victims and the victim's rights" (05:50:37) — and the defence expressly agreed: "We agree it should not be published" (05:51:14).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Singling out Ex. 7 makes the State's restraint look exceptional when it was the norm, and it makes the Art. I §28 denials look contested when two of them were unopposed. This is an omission that runs against the State, which standing hazard 4 makes as reportable as one that runs the other way.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Collection chain given as: "Flash drive to Lt. O'Brien on 2025-09-10, then downloadable versions to Agent Mortenson." No 1102 date, no 1102 collector.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull, 05:26:19: "Mr. Farnsworth originally provided, I believe, a flash drive to Lieutenant O'Brien with one of the local agencies, and a short time after that on September 10th, he provided downloadable versions, electronic versions to Agent Mortenson, and an 1102 was collected from him on May 6th of 2026." And 05:27:07: "It was Agent Mortenson who collected it," with Hull adding that he "subsequently spoke to Terryl Farnsworth personally regarding his statement" (05:27:13). Read as written, "on September 10th" attaches to the transfer to Mortenson, not to the O'Brien flash drive.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The other three rows carry their 1102 dates; this one silently does not, and 2026-05-06 is the outlier date in the set (a month after the April cluster, six weeks before Olsen). The row also attaches the only stated date to the wrong link in the chain, and omits that this 1102 — unlike Phillips's, Olsen's and Noble's — was not collected by Hull.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hull conceded 'some edits were made by your office' — the prosecutor's own office — to Wright's video (04:39:43)" — listed as one of "Three defence attacks on this architecture."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The statement was volunteered on the State's own direct examination, in answer to the prosecutor's open question "And so what, if anything, has been done with that video in preparation for today?" Hull: "My understanding is that some edits were made by your office in order to protect some of the participants in the video" (04:39:43). No defence question or objection is pending at that point, and Hull was never cross-examined on Day 1 (§6A records this).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Conceded" and "defence attack" both imply extraction under adversarial pressure. The two other items in the same list genuinely are defence counsel's words (05:28:54; 05:44:56); this one is the State's own direct. Blending them mis-states which layer the fact came from.

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.5, the second stage of the identification
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "the State returned to it at 07:41:10, the prosecutor conceding the follow-through had been 'neglected'"; and "Both rulings are expressly limited 'for the purposes of this hearing only.'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State returned to the identification at 07:38:44; the "neglected" concession is at 07:39:54 ("after you ruled, I just neglected to come back and follow through with the question and the answer"); 07:41:10 is Hull's completed point-out ("Mr. Robinson is between Ms. Nester and other counsel wearing a gray suit, a jacket with a dark tie and a light colored shirt"). On the limitation: the first ruling says "for the purposes of this hearing only" (06:40:55); the second says "For the purposes of this hearing, I find that Agent Hull has identified Mr. Robinson. Again, this is only for the preliminary hearing" (07:41:42) — the quoted phrase with "only" appears once, not twice.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Timestamps are the file's only citation handles, so pointing at the answer rather than the return misdirects any later reader. And presenting one quoted phrase as covering both rulings is exactly the selective-quotation hazard (7) — the substance survives, the quotation does not.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hull repeatedly said 'the vehicle we believe to belong to Mr. Robinson'; the wheels are 'fairly unique,' expressly not 'wholly unique'... and the four-campus-visits timeline rests solely on UVU surveillance review."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The hedging is real but the file preserves only one side of each answer. On the wheels, the full answer is: "The vehicle has very distinct wheels. I won't say that they're wholly unique, but in terms of the video footage that we were reviewing, the wheels on the vehicle are fairly unique and stand out" (07:00:36), and later, unhedged, "the distinctive wheels on the vehicle" (07:12:15). On the visits, Hull's own answer was unhedged as to identity: "We were able to establish that Mr. Robinson had been on campus approximately four times throughout the day, twice before the shooting, the time of the shooting, and then after the shooting later in the evening into the early hours of the 11th" (06:34:55) — with "approximately," which the file drops. And before agreeing to the prosecutor's "that's all based on UVU surveillance video" (06:35:49), Hull had just said the tracking used "the UVU footage and additional information that was obtained" (06:35:35).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Three corrections in this project have run toward the State; this one runs the other way. Quoting only the hedges makes the testimony sound weaker than it was, and "solely" is the prosecutor's leading formulation adopted over the witness's own qualifier eighteen seconds earlier. Both the anchor (four visits) and the connection (that it is Robinson) need grading separately, and the file grades neither.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "a timestamp jump from 06:39:46 to 06:40:55 spans the bench conference on the in-court identification"; §8 item 6: "The bench conference at 06:39:46–06:40:55 on the in-court identification — absent from the transcript."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The bench conference is called at the start of the 06:40:55 turn, i.e. after the gap, and the ruling follows inside the same turn: "Counsel, please approach the bench. All right. Based off what's been presented in court, I'm not finding that particular question, as previously posed as suggestive..." (06:40:55).
