The 69-second gap that precedes it follows the prosecutor's cut-off sentence at 06:39:46 ("...I believe it's worth noting that Mr. Robinson is in plain clothes. Well, he's... Yeah, he's in plain clothes-").
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The unrecorded conference is real and is a legitimate acquisition target, but it sits inside/after 06:40:55, not in the 06:39:46–06:40:55 window. An acquisition request built on the stated window would ask the court for the wrong minute of audio. The prosecutor confirms a bench meeting occurred at 07:39:54 ("That's my recollection of the bench meeting").

not_verified_items.target_section: §4.4 source table, Wright and Phillips rows (and §4.5 by extension)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hull contacted her 2026-04-06 (corrected on the stand from April 7)"; "Hull and Davis met him 2026-04-06"; "Hull met Olsen 2026-06-24 (corrected from July 2)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The year is never stated for the April dates. Hull says "April 7th" (04:37:07), then "I contacted her, I think it was April 6th specifically, but Agent Davis met with her on April 7th" (04:39:09), and "that was in April" (04:39:59); for Phillips, "myself and Agent Davis met with Mr. Phillips on April 6th" (05:14:41); for Noble, "it was in April... April 6th, I believe" (07:04:53). Only Olsen carries "of this year" (05:42:12) and only Farnsworth's 1102 carries an explicit year, "May 6th of 2026" (05:26:19).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: 2026 is a sound inference from "of this year," "May 6th of 2026," and "in preparation for the proceedings today" — but it is an inference, printed in ISO form as if spoken. The table also omits that the April 7 in-person visit to Wright and the 6.1 collection were Agent Davis's, not Hull's (04:40:57–04:41:10), which is the same collector distinction the row's own bracketed correction turns on.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "not one of the five source witnesses testified" — presented immediately above a table with four rows.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The count is correct: Wright (Ex. 6.1), Phillips (7.1), Farnsworth (8.1), Olsen (12.3) and Noble (13) are the five Rule 1102 civilian sources. But Noble and Exhibit 13 appear only in §4.5, so §4.4 asserts five and shows four with no note.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt: Noble 1102 at lines 10363–10475 (stream 07:02:56–07:05:16); the other four in the table
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A reader auditing the section counts four and reads five. Adding Noble as a fifth row (or a one-line note) makes the section self-verifying, which matters because "five" is one of the file's headline numbers.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "...since the 12.3 language CR-E04 quotes **expressly addresses the alterations** (\"the only changes are some zooms and red highlights\") while the 12.3 admitted on **Day 1 at 05:46:10** evidently did not, or the objection could not have succeeded"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The Day-1 12.3 DID contain that language, and the objection succeeded anyway. Three independent points in the very passage §5 cites establish it. (1) The prosecutor argued from 12.3 in exactly those terms at 06:49:45: "Judge, if you refer to Mr. Olson's written statement, it's plaintiff's exhibit 12.3. He, too, has reviewed this video, and he has also identified this video as being accurate with the exception of those additions. **In his words, it's the zooms and the red highlights. They weren't part of the original recording**, according to Mr. Olson." (2) Hull at 06:44:00: "I believe he specifically referenced the exhibit by name stating that it was a true reflection of the footage from the campus." (3) The court, in the sustaining ruling itself at 06:53:46: "And what I have is the original video, and **Mr. Olson saying, 'This is the video, minus the alterations.'**" The court sustained not because 12.3 failed to describe the alterations but because no one accounted for them from the alterer's side: "I do not have the person who made the alteration, an 1102 to substantiate that... but I'm missing a link." Secondary check outside the assigned artifact: on Day 2 the prosecutor treats 12.3 as "actually been admitted into evidence" (day2.txt 00:25:00) and has Hull read the sentence aloud verbatim from it (00:25:49) — the same exhibit, neither amended nor replaced.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt lines 10021 (06:49:45), 9901 (06:44:00), 10065 (06:53:46); ruling turn lines 10058–10083 (06:53:26–06:54:26). Corroborating, outside the assigned artifact: day2.txt lines 531, 551.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: This is the inferential core of the library's newest register entry. The premise is false on the face of the transcript CR-E05 cites; the entry's "most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement" hypothesis is built on it; and its stated resolution test — "whether 12.3 was amended or replaced" — is aimed at a question the Day-1 record already answers in the negative. D-52 as written sends Q-52 looking for a change that did not occur. This is the analyst layer asserting an inference the recording layer contradicts.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: Headline 1: "**nobody accounted for who made the alterations** (zooms, red circles, face-blurring)"; §5: "**no witness and no Rule 1102 statement accounted for who made those alterations.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The maker of the alterations was identified by name, under oath, four minutes before the exhibit was offered. Hull, 06:42:35–06:42:43: Q "Do you know who did?" A "Yes. **Utah County Attorney's Office. I believe Ms. Derfler is the one that produced the video.**" Q "Do you know Ms. Derfler's first name?" A "**Kimberlie.**" And the State expressly offered to call her, at 06:52:04: "I will proffer that those changes made to the video were not done by either... **I know who that person is. We could actually call that person as a witness if that would cure that, and we're prepared to do that if necessary.**" The court's actual gap was narrower than "nobody accounted for who": "you don't have a person testifying 1102 saying, 'I made the alterations'" (06:51:13) and "I do not have the person who made the alteration, an 1102 to substantiate that" (06:53:26). The name appears nowhere in the library (grep, all *.md: zero hits).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: As written the headline reads as though the alterer was unknown to the parties; the record names her and the State volunteered to produce her. This is the single most obvious overnight cure and it is missing from D-52's list of hypotheses, which offers only a revised Olsen 1102. It also under-records what the defence was actually up against. (Orthography is Rev's and unverified — "Derfler"/"Kimberlie" as rendered; she is a named public-office employee acting officially, so naming is within the living-persons rule, but the identification should carry the same ⚠ the file gives "Falmina".)

not_verified_items.target_section: §5 ("What the library records") and the D-52 row
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The State announced it would prepare and offer an unaltered version the next day**, and the day ended early" / revision log: "the State undertook to **rebuild it** overnight" / D-52: "So something changed in the foundation overnight — **most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State announced a TWO-exhibit plan, not a rebuild of 12.1. At 07:42:11: "our intent is to prepare an original version of the video that has been in dispute today without the circles, without the blur and without the zooming in. And our intent is to introduce that tomorrow **as a different exhibit** and we just can't prepare that in the next hour or so." At 07:43:21, inviting the court to pre-review: "our intent is to seek to admit the version where it doesn't have the circle or the blur or the zoom in. **And if that is admitted, we do intend to introduce that exhibit 12.1 as well.** And I think it would be helpful if you saw that in advance and **you could compare that** to the version that doesn't have the circle, the blur and the zooming in." CR-E04 §3 — the section §5 quotes — records precisely that outcome: "**12.4 was admitted and published**... **12.1 was admitted but NOT published** — Judge Graf reviewed it on his own monitor, reasoning that as it is 'the exact same video… simply zooming in,' publication was unnecessary." §5 quotes CR-E04 §3's 12.1 line and its 12.3 block and drops 12.4 entirely; the string "12.4" does not appear in CR-E05.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: D-52 presents an unexplained overnight change in foundation. The Day-1 transcript states the mechanism in the State's own words, and the companion file already records the exhibit it produced. What is genuinely open is narrower and better posed: on Day 2, what carried 12.1 in once 12.4 was admitted — the comparison, a fresh witness, or something else. As written the entry omits the two most probative facts already in hand. It is also standing hazard 7 firing inside CR-E05's own use of a companion file: the quotation of CR-E04 §3 is reliable as to the words and misleading as to the document.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The defence objected on authenticity: the compilation contained **zooms, red circles and face-blurring**, and **no witness and no Rule 1102 statement accounted for who made those alterations.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The defence objection at 06:46:43–06:49:06 had four distinct grounds, of which §5 records one; and the ground §5 does record is the COURT's formulation, not the defence's. Nester's grounds: (i) personal knowledge/foundation — "This is a compilation video that was put together from a bunch of different sources by the County Attorney's Office. **This individual did not create this compilation, cannot testify to the accuracy of the actual materials that it was taken from.**" (ii) alteration/authenticity — "they admit it's been altered, so we have real concern about authenticity of it." (iii) protected-record classification — "the video should be classified as protected under **UCJA 4-202.0[2]**... subsection five, J as in jelly bean, and then little i and little double ii," because it "is going to interfere with the defense's ongoing investigation" and Robinson's "ability to get a fair trial," and "it would be extremely prejudicial for people that may ultimately serve on this jury." (iv) "We don't believe a proper foundation's been laid," plus objection "to its publication both in the courtroom and to the media." The "no 1102 accounting for the alterations" formulation is the court's, first raised sua sponte at 06:50:43–06:51:13: "you don't have a person testifying 1102 saying, 'I made the alterations.'"
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two costs. First, the 4-202.02(5)(J) protected-record ground raised here on Day 1 is the seed of the Day 2 publication fight CR-E04 §3 records (Kearns/Allgier, the public-opinion survey, media counsel Ryman) — CR-E05 severs a thread it is otherwise tracing. Second, transposing the court's reasoning into the defence's mouth blurs the argument/ruling line that the file's own §1.2 rule exists to protect; the file elsewhere is scrupulous about this.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "the 12.3 admitted on **Day 1 at 05:46:10**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: 05:46:10 is the start of the court's turn, in which it first asks to review the document ("I'll have if the state representative can scroll through so I can review it in its entirety"). The admitting words fall in the turn timestamped 05:47:13: "...of the Utah Constitution, that final paragraph, **the court overrules the objection and admits State's Exhibit 12.3**." The offer is at 05:44:43 ("the state would seek to admit what's been marked State's Exhibit 12.3"), the defence objection at 05:44:56 (standing hearsay/constitutional, plus "the individual basically states they verified the recordings but doesn't say how"), the State's response at 05:45:39 citing "Rule 1102, subsection B8."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The register entry hangs a contested inference on this single timestamp; the ruling actually spans 05:46:10–05:47:13. Small, but a later reader jumping to 05:46:10 lands on the court asking to scroll, not on an admission, and may conclude the citation is wrong.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: File is silent: nowhere records that State's Exhibit 12.3 was published on Day 1.
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: After admitting 12.3 the court published it in full, in the courtroom AND to the media camera, and described the mechanics: "the court is going to publish it both in the courtroom and so it can be captured by the media. What we'll do is the same thing. We'll start at the top, pause for 10 seconds and go to this middle section and we'll pause about 20 seconds because it is more dense and then we'll scroll down to the very bottom for about 10 seconds" (05:47:44). The State had asked for exactly that: "the presumption is that it's a public record and we would ask that it be published both here in the courtroom and that the cameras be allowed to capture it" (05:47:25).
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to D-52. The Day-1 contents of 12.3 were not opaque — the whole statement was scrolled on the courtroom screen and to the media camera on Day 1, which is why the "evidently did not [contain the sentence]" inference was avoidable and is checkable. It also completes §4.4's publication-outcomes list, which records outcomes for Exs. 6, 7, 8 and 9 but not for the 1102 statements themselves.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "An off-record conference at 07:15–07:37... **The State's next act was to end the day**; whether the two are connected is **not established.**"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two things. (a) Sequence: after the 07:37:54 resumption the State's next act was to complete the in-court identification it had "neglected" (07:38:44–07:41:52); only then, at 07:41:52, did it ask to break. (b) The connection between the 12.1 exclusion and the early end IS established, in the State's own words at 07:42:11: "we just can't prepare that in the next hour or so. **So, we're going to need this evening to prepare that exhibit** and we'd like to return with that." What remains unestablished is only what the off-record conference itself was about.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file names over-hedging as a defect (standing hazard 4) and then hedges a link the record states outright. The residual uncertainty should be scoped to the conference, not to the exclusion→adjournment connection.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "**The State ended the day early** and undertook to rebuild an unaltered version overnight" / §5: "and the day ended early."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The magnitude is small and the decision was joint. The court, at 07:42:51: "**We have about 19 minutes until 5:00.** What is the defense-" The break was floated as already agreed after the off-record conference — prosecutor at 07:38:17: "we're all in agreement that we want to break for the day. Is that right, Ms. Nester?" — and the defence assented: "Your Honor, we're happy to accommodate the state on that" (07:43:00). The court then adjourned "until 9:00 AM tomorrow morning."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: "Ended the day early" without the figure invites a reading of a substantially truncated session; it was about 19 minutes, by agreement, with the State's reason on the record. Recording the number costs nothing and forecloses the inflation.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "No confession, no motive, no text messages, no family or roommate material."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The "no family material" element is false. On Hull's direct, the SIAC workup of the vehicle tied to the name received from Washington County produced two registered owners. Ryan McBride label: "And who were the registered owners?" — Hull: "Mr. Robinson and then his mother." The vehicle is also identified as a silver Dodge Challenger ("The Dodge Challenger" / "It was silver in color, and I believe there were two registered owners of the vehicle"). CR-E05 §4.5 records the doorbell canvass and Ex. 12.2 but never records the make, the colour, or the co-owner.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: A null in a scoped-null section is a positive claim about the corpus, and this one is contradicted by sworn testimony in the same file's own subject matter. It is also evidentially load-bearing in both directions: the mother's co-ownership is the State's route from a name to a vehicle, and simultaneously the defence's point that the Challenger seen on the doorbell footage had a second registered owner. A reader relying on §6A would wrongly conclude Day 1 contains no Robinson-family material at all.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "A brand discrepancy inside an admitted exhibit. Exhibit 13 (Ms. Noble's Rule 1102 statement, foundation for the doorbell footage) carries a Nest-versus-Ring inconsistency in how the camera is described. Recorded as an internal inconsistency in an admitted document."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The discrepancy is not internal to Exhibit 13. /Nest\b/ returns exactly ONE hit in the whole of day1.txt, and it is the court reading from Exhibit 13 when admitting it: "I note in particular that it states that, 'I confirmed that the above files were taken from our Nest doorbell videos and are accurate.'" Every "Ring" reference is Agent Hull's own sworn testimony: "We collected Ring doorbell footage from the surrounding neighborhoods" (06:56:56); "It was a Ring doorbell video that was provided" (06:57:31); "we were able to locate the footage of his vehicle on that Ring doorbell camera" (06:59:53). /Ring doorbell|Ring camera|a Ring/ = 3 hits, all Hull. So the conflict is exhibit-text vs case-agent testimony.
not_verified_items.locator: Exhibit 13 quoted by the court at 07:05:50; Hull at 06:56:56, 06:57:31, 06:59:53
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: An internal inconsistency in a document is close to trivial and the file treats it as such ("not resolved here, and not weighted"). A conflict between the sworn description given by the lead case agent and the text of the very exhibit offered as the foundation for that footage is a foundation problem for State's Exhibit 12.2, and it is exactly the kind of thing the defence's standing Rule 1102/confrontation objection is aimed at. §4.5 compounds it by adopting Hull's "Ring" ("A Ring doorbell canvass produced Ex. 12.2… with Ex. 13 (Ms. Noble's 1102) as foundation") without noting the exhibit says Nest.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The rifle is never recovered, described forensically, or photographed in this record. The only reference to a weapon is Bagley's hedged 'long black object' (§3.4)."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The first sentence holds. The second is plainly false and contradicts CR-E05's own §3.2 and §3.5. Day 1 contains at least: the empty holster — "An empty concealed holster" / "For what type of weapon?" / "For a pistol" (02:53:17–02:53:21); the six UVU officers' sidearms — "What type of weapons do you carry?" / "Glock pistols" (02:45:04–02:45:06); Bagley's rifle-vs-handgun sound reasoning ("a handgun is more of a short bang pop sound. With a rifle, you have more of a longer violent bang or crackle sound", 01:41:11); and the unidentified armed man carrying a handgun that §3.5 itself records. /weapon/=3, /handgun/=5, /pistol/=5, /rifle/=7, /gun\b/=13, /firearm/=1.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §6A is the section a later reader will cite for what Day 1 does not contain, and this sentence is internally contradicted by two other sections of the same file. The intended claim — that no reference to the murder weapon itself exists beyond the hedged object — is defensible; as written the null is false and would be caught the first time anyone re-ran it, discrediting the section.

not_verified_items.target_section: §6A — "No ballistics, no bullet recovery…" (and §3.3 analyst layer)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "No ballistics, no bullet recovery, no fingerprints, no DNA of any kind."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: /ballistic/ = 0 and /DNA/ = 0, both confirmed. But "no bullet recovery" is not a clean null: immediately after the casing sequence, defence counsel put two express propositions to Bagley — "Are you aware of there being a bullet found on another roof-" (Bagley: "I'm not aware") and "...in the vicinity? Were you aware of another bullet being found on the scene not on the roof of the Losee building?" (Bagley: "No"). The file records the casing search and "He also found no unfired bullets on the roof" but never records that a bullet found elsewhere was put on the record at all.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Counsel's question is not evidence and Bagley disclaimed knowledge — but the record is not silent, and §3.3's analyst layer asserts that "the perch produced nothing" and that Bagley corroborates "no bullets or casings found on or immediately around the Losee building." A defence question presupposing a bullet recovered on another roof in the vicinity is directly adverse to that scope and feeds D-48. Omitting it means the file's strongest analyst-layer claim was written without the one Day 1 passage that qualifies it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "He saw 'a long black object in the left hand' as the person crossed the roof; asked what it was, he said 'It looks like a rifle or something to that effect, a long object… like skinny and long.' ⚠ His report mentions neither a gun nor the object"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The quotations are accurate but the passage is cut before its two most consequential turns. Bagley: "You can see it's almost like it's covered over something." Counsel: "So you saw the cover, which was the towel, right?" Bagley: "Yes. And the shape of it is long." Counsel: "So you can see a towel, but you can't see an actual gun." Bagley: "I don't know if it was a towel or a blanket. I don't know what it was." Counsel: "But you can't see an actual gun in the video?" Bagley: "No. Like an object, like a form of a gun, like a long object." Separately, at 04:14:31 counsel put it to him that his report described the object as a bag — "And in fact, did you describe that in your report as a bag?" / "I don't know. I have no idea." — then pulled the report and withdrew it: "Nevermind. I don't think you mentioned what you saw."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The object was wrapped, and the witness gave a categorical "No" to being able to see a gun — both materially more favourable to the defence than the hedged rendering the file preserves, in a section the file itself bills as "the most defence-favourable stretch of Day 1." The both-directions rule is breached in the direction the file least expects. The withdrawn "bag" question is also the source of the file's "his report mentions neither a gun nor the object," so the file has kept counsel's conclusion while dropping the exchange that produced it.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "…because although Rule 1102 statements covered the original recordings, nobody accounted for who made the alterations (zooms, red circles, face-blurring)" / §5: "no witness and no Rule 1102 statement accounted for who made those alterations."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The identity of the alteration-maker was on the record four minutes before the exhibit was offered. Hull: "Did you prepare this video compilation?" — "I did not." — "Do you know who did?" — "Yes. Utah County Attorney's Office. I believe Ms. Derfler is the one that produced the video." — first name given as "Kimberlie." And during argument the State proffered: "I know who that person is. We could actually call that person as a witness if that would cure that, and we're prepared to do that if necessary." The court's stated ground was narrower than the file's: "I do not have the person who made the alteration, an 1102 to substantiate that… I'm missing a link."
not_verified_items.locator: identification at 06:42:34–06:42:43; State's proffer at 06:52:04–06:52:45; ruling at 06:53:26–06:53:46
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The file's #1 headline result and its new register entry both rest on the proposition that nobody knew who made the alterations. What was actually missing was sworn testimony or a Rule 1102 statement FROM a named, available person — an evidentiary gap, not an informational one. That distinction changes D-52's whole hypothesis (see next finding) and it changes how the exclusion should be characterised: the State had the cure in hand and the court still declined to accept the proffer.

not_verified_items.target_section: §5 and the D-52 register row ("What would resolve it")
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "The State announced it would prepare and offer an unaltered version the next day" / D-52: "something changed in the foundation overnight — most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement…"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The State's announced plan on the record was two-part, and the file records only the first half: "our intent is to seek to admit the version where it doesn't have the circle or the blur or the zoom in. And if that is admitted, we do intend to introduce that exhibit 12.1 as well. And I think it would be helpful if you saw that in advance and you could compare that to the version that doesn't have the circle, the blur and the zooming in." Defence counsel also put 12.1's length on the record: "It's kind of a little bit of a long video. I think it's just about five minutes maybe."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: D-52 speculates that the overnight change was "most likely a revised or supplemental Rule 1102 statement." The transcript supplies a competing, State-stated mechanism — admit a clean version first and then introduce the altered 12.1 alongside it for comparison — which independently explains CR-E04's observation that the exhibit admitted on Day 2 was still altered, with no amendment to Ex. 12.3 required. Since D-52 is the file's flagship new register entry and Q-52 is scoped to resolve it, an omitted sentence that redirects the hypothesis is material. The five-minute runtime is also a free identifying detail for the acquisition target.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §3.1: "He worked an overtime shift, checking in about 11:00 a.m., posted at the south end of the Hall of Flags." §3.5: "No briefing, no debrief, no meeting that morning; he does not know whether any security meeting occurred; no operational or tactical plan, no written materials."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Bagley gave a reason for both the posting and the missed briefing, and the file drops it. On direct: "Did you receive a specific assignment shortly after coming onto duty?" — "It was to secure the top of the Hall of Flags on the south end. So we had people that were gathering on top of that that were looking down on top of the tent, so we wanted to secure that area." On cross, asked whether he attended any briefing: "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags… Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area." He also describes putting up barrier tape on that rooftop "so people wouldn't go above that and walk."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Two separate costs. (1) Both-directions: the file's §3.5 and §7 present the absence of a briefing as unexplained institutional failure; the witness gave an operational explanation, which is the State-favourable reading and is not logged anywhere. (2) Substantively, an unfolding pre-event incident in which people were on an adjacent rooftop looking down on and throwing objects at Kirk's tent, requiring the on-duty officers to be redeployed, is a Day 1 fact of independent interest to the library's rooftop-access and security-posture questions, and it appears nowhere in CR-E05.

not_verified_items.target_section: §6A — "Bagley's entire testimony contains no reference to Tyler Robinson."
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Bagley's entire testimony contains no reference to Tyler Robinson."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: True of Bagley's own answers; not true of his examination. /Robinson/ returns 46 hits in day1.txt. Exactly one falls between Bagley's swearing (44:10) and his excusal (~04:22), and it is defence counsel introducing herself to him: "Officer Bagley, my name is Kathy Nester. I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Robinson today and I do have some questions for you." Bagley himself never utters the name and is never asked to identify anyone in the courtroom.
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt stream 02:43:01 (flattened-char 136,725); Bagley sworn 44:10, passed 02:42:15, excused ~04:22
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §6A opens by defining each null as "a claim about a full-text search of this Rev rendering," which invites the whole-text reading under which this null fails. The substantive point — that Bagley never names, identifies or connects Robinson to anything — is sound and is the point worth keeping; it just needs to be scoped to the witness's answers rather than to the examination. Left as written it is the kind of null that gets falsified on the first re-run.

not_verified_items.target_section: §6A — "The Washington County tipster is not identified" (vs §7 and the revision log)
not_verified_items.claim_in_file: §6A: "The Washington County tipster is not identified — the record does not say whether it was Robinson himself or a third party (§4.5)." §7: "the name Tyler Robinson arrived from a person seeking to turn himself in, not from investigative guesswork."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Hull: "Eventually, on the evening of the 11th, we received word from Washington County that an individual in that area had reached out to law enforcement and was wanting to turn themselves in for the incident at UVU." — "And at that point in time, did you receive a name from Washington County?" — "Yes, we did." — "And what was that name?" — "Tyler Robinson." Grammatically the same individual both reached out and wanted to turn themselves in, and the name then received is that individual's.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 4 — an unwarranted hedge is as reportable as an unwarranted assertion. The steelman for §6A is real (Hull never says in terms "Robinson called us," and a third party could in principle have relayed that someone wanted to surrender), so the hedge should survive in some form. But it cannot survive in its current form while §7 and the revision log both state the definite version as a point logged "for the prosecution." The file currently says the record is silent on the very fact it elsewhere relies on; one of the two has to move.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "State's Exhibit 11 is the nine-page report of examination. Offered 06:05:31; ADMITTED over defence hearsay and confrontation objection"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The nine pages, the "report of examination" description, the 06:05:31 offer, the Rule 1102(b)(5) and Art. I §12 grounds and the Art. I §28 publication denial all confirm exactly. But the defence's lead objection ground is not recorded: "this is an expert report without the expert being present, being offered by an individual who's not an expert in this field. If they're presenting him as an expert in this field based on the limited questions about his experience… I'd like to voir dire him on his qualifications to opine about it… He's not qualified to do that."
not_verified_items.locator: day1.txt stream 06:05:36–06:06:42; page count at 06:03:30; ruling at 06:08:50–06:09:27
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: The expert-qualification and voir-dire ground is a distinct objection from hearsay and confrontation, it was argued first and at length, and it is the ground most likely to recur if the ME report becomes contested — which matters because §8 item 1 makes Exhibit 11 the file's top acquisition target for Q-15/D-49. Both-directions: this is a defence argument dropped from a file that otherwise records defence objections carefully.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Hundreds of hours of video were available, predominantly UVU's; Hull personally watched perhaps 10–20 hours that day."
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The 10–20 figure is exact ("Myself, maybe 10 or 20 hours of video"). The aggregate is not: "And combined, how much video do you think you watched that first day, on the 10th?" — "It would be in the tens or hundreds of hours of video was reviewed." The witness's own hedge spans an order of magnitude and the file reports only its upper bound.
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Recording-layer fidelity: the analyst layer may characterise, but the recording layer must carry the claim as made. "Tens or hundreds" is a materially weaker statement than "hundreds," and the file elsewhere is scrupulous about preserving witnesses' own qualifications (it does exactly this correctly for Bagley's "this does not show that" at §3.3).

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: "Asked why the mismatch with the shot's direction did not register: 'During [the chaos]…'"
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: The answer was not a trailing fragment. Counsel: "But it didn't occur to you that, 'Well, that's not where I heard the shot come from. They must have the wrong person. I should talk to somebody.'" Bagley: "During the chaos moment, no. They said they had a person in custody. I figured those guys saw something I didn't see. They took that person in custody and I thought that was him."
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: Hazard 7 — reliable as to the words, not as to the document. The ellipsis renders a complete, responsive four-sentence answer as an evasion, which overstates the defence's best moment in a bullet already framed as defence-favourable. The full answer is the witness's (and the State's) explanation and belongs in §7's "for the prosecution" column.

not_verified_items.claim_in_file: The named-garble list gives "David Sterk"→Sturgill, Falmina→Faumuina, Elschultz/Elle Schultz, Bricker, Clark, Cam Nelson/Ken Nielsen, "Erica Kirk"→Erika, "Mr. Cook's presentation", "Bayliff".
not_verified_items.what_the_transcript_shows: Two further garbles are present and unlisted. During the 12.1 argument the State refers to "Agent Holt here today on the stand" — Rev's rendering of Hull (/Holt/ = 1 hit, at 06:52:04). And the UVU witness's surname is rendered both ways: /Olsen/ = 20 hits, /Olson/ = 4, including in the same argument ("Mr. Olson in the form of his written statement", "Mr. Olson saying, 'This is the video, minus the alterations'").
not_verified_items.locator: "Agent Holt" at 06:52:04; "Olson" at 06:52:04, 06:53:46 among four occurrences; "Olsen" elsewhere
not_verified_items.why_it_matters: §1.3 closes with "No name in this file should be treated as verified orthography," so the principle is safe — but the Olsen/Olson split matters operationally because Exhibit 12.3 is his 1102 statement and is the artifact Q-52 must retrieve; a searcher working from one spelling will miss a fifth of the passages. "Agent Holt" matters because it is a garble of the witness's own name inside the single most important argument on Day 1.

finding.claim_in_file: Headline 4: "Day 1 is where the entire documentary architecture of the State's case was built — sixteen exhibits offered." On the State's pre-testimony roadmap the file is silent.
finding.what_the_transcript_shows: At 23:50–24:39, before any witness, Grunander gave the court the State's whole roadmap: "we anticipate presenting four witnesses. They're all law enforcement witnesses" — Officer Chris Bagley (now Spanish Fork PD, formerly UVU PD); Agent David Hull ("those exhibits seven, eight, nine, we anticipate coming in through him"); Agent Brian Davis; and "Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina, also of the Utah Department of Public Safety." He closed: "we do anticipate admitting between 40 and 50 exhibits."
finding.why_it_matters: Two of the file's own claims move. (a) If the State planned 40–50 exhibits across the hearing, Day 1's sixteen is not "the entire documentary architecture" — the headline overstates. (b) The State announced at the outset that it would call four witnesses and that all four were law enforcement, which is the strongest available support for §4.4's finding that "not one of the five source witnesses testified": no civilian source witness was ever going to be called. A reader of CR-E05 alone cannot see either.

verdict.reasoning:
TRANSCRIPT VERIFIED, VERBATIM. day1.txt lines 517–528 (stream 23:50–24:39) read directly plus ~120 lines either side. The finder quoted it accurately.

HAZARD 1 (speaker labels) — the finder's identification survives, on the file's own §1.2 standard. The Rev label reads "Chad Grunander," but I did not rely on it: the court addresses him by name in the *immediately preceding* turn (line 516, "And Mr. Gernander, as it relates to that…" — a Rev garble of Grunander) and again in the *immediately following* turn (line 532, "Mr. Grunander, I apologize, you walked away before I got my question out"). Two adjacent court addresses = stated basis. Functionally the turn is a party's housekeeping proffer, not a ruling. Grunander is also the counsel who entered the State's appearances (line 224) and conducted Bagley's direct.

HAZARD 2 (timestamps) — clean. The finder wrote "stream 23:50–24:39" and converted nothing. (The "10:30" and "9:35" in the same passage are the judge's *spoken* clock times, not stream conversions.)

verdict.reasoning:
WHAT I DID. Read CLAUDE.md; read CR-E05 in full (331 lines); read day1.txt lines 400–658 (covering the locator with ~120 lines either side) and lines 6595–6814 (Hull's SBI-assignment passage); ran tsearch.py across all five days for /Faumuina|Falmina|Fomina|Fahmina/ and /Jennifer|Jen /, and opened every hit rather than counting them (hazard 6). Method validated by the tool's own known-positive check on each run (hazard 5).

THE LOCATOR IS VERIFIED. day1.txt line 528, stream 24:19, reads verbatim: "The third witness will be Agent Brian Davis again with the State of Utah, a case agent who's here presently. And lastly, Sergeant Jennifer Faumuina, also of the Utah Department of Public Safety. And we do anticipate admitting between 40 and 50 exhibits." No hazard-1 problem: the speaker is functionally the prosecutor giving the court his witness roadmap ("we anticipate presenting four witnesses. They're all law enforcement witnesses, Officer Chris Bagley…"), and the court addresses him by name on both sides of the turn — "Mr. Gernander" at line 516 immediately before and "Mr. Grunander, I apologize, you walked away before I got my question out" at line 532 immediately after. The Rev label agrees with the content here, which is the one situation where a Day 1 label may be relied on.

TWO OF THE FINDER'S OWN ASSERTIONS ARE REFUTED AND MUST NOT ENTER THE LIBRARY.
(a) "Roughly two hours of stream earlier" is wrong twice over. 24:19 to Hull's list at 04:29:29 is about four hours five minutes of raw stream, not two; and hazard 2 forbids measuring a duration across a recess at all — the 9:35 recess (27:26→42:20) alone sits inside that span. The correct formulation is "earlier in the same stream."
(b) "The same transcript makes it" is an overstatement. Day 1 contains exactly three occurrences of the name in any rendering: Grunander's "Faumuina" at 24:19, and Hull's "Falmina" at 04:29:29 and 04:32:57. No passage anywhere in Day 1 equates the two. CR-E05's literal proposition — "the transcript does not make it" — is therefore TRUE as written, and the finder's charge that it "is factually wrong about day1.txt" over-reads what the file said. Adopting the finding as phrased would put a false statement about the transcript into the library.

BUT A REAL DEFECT SURVIVES, IN TWO PARTS.
(1) Omission. Grep of the entire CR-E05 returns only two "Faumuina" hits — §1.3 (line 53) and §4.1 (line 172). The State's opening roadmap at 24:19 is recorded nowhere: not in §2's shape-of-the-day table (whose first row, "06:57–~40:00", covers the very stretch it sits in), not in §2.1's "preliminary rulings worth keeping" (which does reach forward to 42:54 for the discovery disclosure), not in §4.1. Day 1 is the only day whose file this belongs to, and it is the only place in Day 1 supplying the name in unmangled form.
(2) Over-hedge with a mis-stated basis (hazard 4). §4.1 gives the sole reason the identification is "likely" as the cross-day task match — "The crime-lab-coordination task matches her Day 2/Day 4 testimony exactly" — which represents Day 1 as contributing nothing toward it. Day 1 contributes something specific and checkable: the State designated a Utah DPS sergeant named Jennifer Faumuina as its fourth witness in this case, and Hull's list of SBI responders (Falmina, Bricker, Elschultz, Clark, Davis) contains no other candidate — day1.txt has exactly one occurrence of "Jennifer" in the whole file, so no competing person exists in the Day 1 record. Bold "UNCONFIRMED" is also internally inconsistent with the same file's §1.3 (line 53), which already normalises 'Sergeant "Falmina" (Faumuina)' with no hedge at all, while hedging the parallel Sturgill garble explicitly ("very likely"). The file hedges harder in its analytic section than in its caveat section, which is backwards.

STEELMANNED CR-E05 BEFORE CONFIRMING. The strongest defence of the file is that its null is a properly scoped one — it names what would confirm (the transcript equating the renderings), states it is absent, and discloses its actual basis — and that CLAUDE.md's "never infer identity from partial information" rule pushes toward caution on a named living person. That defence carries the sentence "the transcript does not make it," which I leave standing in my proposed wording. It does not carry "UNCONFIRMED", and it does not carry the omission of line 528.

VERIFYING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON THE IDENTIFICATION ITSELF, so the replacement grade traces to actual verification acts by me, not to the finder: Day 2 01:42:35 — Hull on cross: "Agent Falmina was assigned to process and document the crime scenes"; Day 2 ~05:00:00 — "we are going to call Jen Faumuina, a sergeant with the SBI… The State calls Sergeant Jen Faumuina," sworn as Jennifer Faumuina; Day 3 10:59 — the same prosecutor, giving the same kind of roadmap, is rendered as "Sergeant Jennifer Falmina is also present in the courthouse and prepared to testify," the garble carrying her given name, which is the decisive orthographic link; Day 3 48:00 — Davis: "a team led by Sergeant Faumuina with SBI along with the Utah State Crime Lab"; Day 4 04:35:22 and 06:08:41 — Faumuina herself on which teams processed which scenes and on the state crime lab's crime-scene response team. Same rank, same agency, same assignment, no competing candidate anywhere in five days. That supports High, not "UNCONFIRMED".

SEVERITY. I downgrade the finder's "material" to MINOR–MODERATE. No headline result, register entry, resolution or open item in CR-E05 turns on this identification; §1.3 already carried the correct form; the practical harm is that the file sends a later reader out of Day 1 for something Day 1 partly answers, and understates a name it holds. It warrants a correction in place and a revision-log row, not a re-grading of anything the file concludes.

Verdict: CONFIRMED as to the defect (omission + over-hedge), with the finder's own characterisation expressly rejected.

verdict.reasoning:
I read the transcript at the locator and well beyond it, then read CR-E05 in full and grepped it for every possible place the point could hide. The finding survives, and is understated.

TRANSCRIPT — the finder's quotations verify verbatim.
- State's Exhibit 1: offer at day1.txt 1357–1360 (57:22). Objection 1361–1380 (57:25/57:35): "we would object to inability to authenticate. There's not been a foundation laid that this officer took this photo, can verify when it was taken or by whom it was taken." State's argument 1385–1396 (57:54): "it's very clear, well-established law that the person who took the photograph is not required to be present to lay the foundation for it. What's required for foundation is that the witness has knowledge of what's depicted in the photograph and can testify to its accuracy." Ruling 1413–1416 (58:58): "I'm going to overrule the objection and admit Exhibit 1. This witness has firsthand knowledge of the location as well as the building locations. That foundation has been laid. He also stated it was a fair and accurate representation."
- State's Exhibit 2: 1829–1848. Objection at 01:07:03 verbatim as quoted; overruled 01:07:34, "He was there on the day, on September 10th."
- State's Exhibit 3: 2154–2193. Objection at 01:15:52 verbatim. Ruling at 01:17:27 (the finder's locator stopped at the objection).

HAZARD CHECKS — all pass.
- Hazard 1 (speaker labels): the finder's attributions are functionally sound and do not rest on Rev's labels. The court addresses "Ms. Nester" in turns adjacent to every objection (lines 1376, 1400, 1414, 3305, 3702, 3974, 4050) and "Mr. Grunander" adjacent to every State argument (1384, 1408, 1840, 2165, 2589, 3714); the ruling turns are functionally judicial. This is one stretch where Day 1's labels happen to hold, and the basis is stated.
- Hazard 2: no timestamp is converted to clock time or used to measure a duration; they are used as identifiers only.
- Hazard 5/6: I did not rely on counts — I opened every passage.
- Hazard 3: the finder writes "Ex. 1/2/3" loosely; the adopted wording below uses "State's Exhibit N".

THE FINDING IS LARGER THAN CLAIMED. A full sweep of Day 1's exhibit offers (tsearch, /state (?:offers|would offer|moves? to admit)[^.]{0,60}Exhibit/, method-validated, 8 hits, every one read) shows **all eight** exhibits in §8 item 5 drew a defence objection: Ex. 1 (1357–1416), Ex. 2 (1829–1848), Ex. 3 (2154–2193), Ex. 35 (2578–2605), Ex. 3.1 (3298–3361), Ex. 3.2 (3695–3754), Ex. 4 (3967–4058), Ex. 5 (4235–4246). The State cited two authorities as rendered by Rev — State v. Purcell, 711 P.2d 243, 245 (Utah 1985), which the judge paused to read from the bench (2174–2189), and State v. Wager, spelled W-A-G-E-R, 372 P.3d 91 (Utah Ct. App. 2016) (2593) — and argued the required showing is "essentially a prima facie showing," not preponderance or beyond reasonable doubt (2173). On Ex. 3.1, 3.2 and 4 the court did not simply overrule: it identified the foundation gap itself and made the State cure it on the spot (3314–3317, "did you state that this was a fair and accurate representation as of September 10th"; 3983–3986, "other artifacts on this image that I haven't heard any testimony about").

DOES CR-E05 SAY IT ANYWHERE? No. Checked the whole file including caveats and the revision log. "Authentic*" appears once (line 239) and concerns State's Exhibit 12.1 only. "Foundation" appears 11 times across 9 lines (62, 74, 152, 199, 201, 228, 245, 292, 305) — doorbell exhibit, Hull's video marathon, Exhibits 4/5, Exhibit 13, and 12.1. None concerns Exhibits 1, 2, 3, 35, 3.1 or 3.2. "Overrul*" appears twice (127, 193) — the dispatch hearsay ruling and the ME-report exchange. The finder's supporting statement is right on substance; the only imprecision is "nine uses of foundation" (11 occurrences on 9 lines) and "authentication" vs. the single "authenticity" at line 239, neither of which affects the finding.

STEELMAN OF CR-E05, taken seriously and rejected on three grounds.
(1) Best defence: §4.4 item 1 already records that "a standing constitutional objection ran against every exhibit," so arguably these admissions are not presented as unopposed. This fails on the record. The standing objection is the Rule 1102 / Art. I §12 confrontation challenge, and Nester expressly distinguished it at Exhibit 1 (1409–1412): "I know this is not a ... There's no written testimony in this, but just out of an abundance of caution, I want to also refer to our standing objection." The authentication objections were a separate line, separately argued and separately ruled. §4.4's note does not reach them.
(2) Second-best defence: this is courtroom housekeeping the file was right to compress. It fails against the file's own editorial standard. §2.1 is titled "Preliminary rulings worth keeping" and keeps the media-devices ruling and the three-level publication framework; §5 gives an entire section to one exhibit ruling. A standard the court applied eight times to admit every scene photograph, argued with cited appellate authority, is squarely inside that scope. §1.1 also claims a full end-to-end read, so this reads as a coverage gap rather than an editing choice.
(3) The file already records objections to Exhibits 4 and 5 (§3.5, "Admitted over preserved objection under URE 1102 and Utah Const. Art. I §12") — that rendering is defensible on the record (3975–3978, 4238–4242) and is logged here as a confirmation in the file's favour. But it covers two of eight and characterises them as 1102/confrontation, not authentication.

MATERIALITY — stated without inflation (hazard 4 cuts both ways here). No factual finding in CR-E05 is falsified; nothing about the shooting, the roof, the casing search or the ME report changes. What changes is threefold. First, §8 item 5's flat "all admitted Day 1" invites the reader to treat the State's entire photographic foundation as unopposed; it was contested eight times on stated grounds. Second, §3.5's cross entries ("He first saw Exhibits 1, 2 and 3 'a couple of weeks ago'"; "He does not know who took Exhibit 35, where it came from, or how old it is") float as stray provenance points instead of the defence returning to the exact ground on which it had already lost — which is what makes that cross live. Third, and most sharply, §7 asserts in the analyst layer that "the rulings admitting exhibits were considered rather than reflexive." That is a both-directions claim the file makes without the evidence that best supports it: the court twice halting an offer to make the State cure the foundation, and reading the cited case from the bench. The omission therefore weakens the file's own pro-State ledger as well as its defence ledger.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE FINDER. "The pattern-setting evidentiary ruling of the entire hearing for photographic evidence" is not established by Day 1 and must not be adopted. Day 1 establishes the standard the court applied on Day 1, eight times. Whether it governed Days 2–5 is checkable and unverified; the wording below scopes it accordingly.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The finder is right, their speaker identification survives a functional (non-label) test, and they did not read a stream timestamp as a clock time.

WHAT THE TRANSCRIPT ACTUALLY SHOWS (day1.txt, read directly)

1. The phrase is the court's. At line 496 (stream 21:44), the speaker says: "on the exhibits that the court grants to be published in court and not, going to Mr. Novak's point, not to be given copies to, and the court is trying to be mindful that if it's shown on TV, that's essentially giving a copy to." At line 500 (22:12): "And so the court is taking Mr. Novak's point in consideration."
   Speaker identified FUNCTIONALLY, not from Rev's label (hazard 1): the turn announces what "the court" will do, directs the camera operator ("this is going to the camera operator"), instructs staff on monitor placement, calls the bailiff "our bailiff," and refers to Mr. Novak in the third person twice. It is the bench. Rev's label (Graf) happens to agree, but the identification does not rest on it.

2. The defence's actual recorded position ran the OTHER WAY on the nearest point. Novak's turn (lines 445-456, 18:16-18:52 — basis for the name: the court calls on "Mr. Novak" at 18:04, line 444, and the speaker self-identifies "Richard Novak for Mr. Robinson," line 448) reports the stipulation — "the parties had earlier stipulated that none of the exhibits, from the preliminary hearing, would be available for inspection or copying" — and then expressly reserves the distinction: "I understand that publishing the exhibits in the courtroom may technically be different than that." So the defence did not argue the broadcast=copy equation; it flagged that the two might not be the same and asked the court to resolve it. The court supplied the bridge itself.

3. Scoped null, method validated first (hazard 5). tsearch.py --validate passes (known positive /use pliers/, day 4). Pattern /giving a copy|essentially giving/ returns exactly ONE hit in day1.txt — the 21:44 judicial turn — and zero in days 2, 4, 5. Day 3's single hit is unrelated ("use of immunity is essentially giving the individual…"). There is no defence utterance of this formulation anywhere in the banked five days. I opened every hit rather than counting (hazard 6).

4. The file's locator points somewhere the language is not. At 01:04:49 (lines 1685-1720) the exchange is: Ms. Nestor asks that the lectern screen be turned off because "we're getting reports that the documents shown on the lectern screen are being live-screamed. Live-streamed," and that State's Exhibit 2 not be shown "until it's admitted"; the court grants ("I'll go ahead and grant the request by Ms. Nester," 01:05:17) and the monitor is switched off. There is no stipulation language and no "copy" language anywhere in that passage.

STEELMAN OF CR-E05, TAKEN SERIOUSLY AND REJECTED
(a) "Going to Mr. Novak's point… and the court is taking Mr. Novak's point in consideration" could be read as the court merely restating an argument Novak had made. This is the strongest reading available to the file and I tested it. It fails on two grounds: the antecedent the court supplies for "Mr. Novak's point" is the no-copies stipulation ("not to be given copies to"), not the TV equation; and Novak's own words at 18:52 disclaim rather than assert the equation. A judge crediting a party's premise while formulating the inference himself is the classic case the standing hazard covers.
(b) The file might be read as offering the phrase as its own paraphrase rather than as the defence's words. It cannot be: the construction is "the defence position being that broadcasting an exhibit 'is essentially giving a copy to' the public" — quotation marks around the exact courtroom phrase, immediately governed by an attribution to a party.

WHAT VERIFIED FOR CR-E05 (both-directions rule; logged explicitly)
- "A broadcast-security failure, caught by the defence (01:04:49)" — CORRECT, and the locator is exact. The speaker is defence counsel Ms. Nestor on a stated basis (the court names her when granting).
- "unadmitted exhibits reportedly reaching the public feed" — supported and correctly hedged ("We're getting reports"; "until it's admitted"; the exhibit being laid was State's Exhibit 2).
- "The court granted the defence request and the lectern monitor was switched off" — CORRECT (01:05:17-01:05:34).
- "The parties had already stipulated that no preliminary-hearing exhibits would be available for inspection or copying" — SUBSTANTIVELY ACCURATE and temporally correct ("earlier stipulated").
- The file correctly kept "the public" OUTSIDE the quotation marks — the court's sentence trails off and never names the recipient. That was careful handling.
- The neighbouring bullet (line 83) attributes the three-level framework to the court correctly. This is a single bundling slip, not a pattern of misattribution.
- Incidentally corroborated CR-E05 §1.2: line 1680, "Richard Novak (01:04:18): Down below, yes, on the south. I was down there" — Bagley's sworn answer under defence counsel's label, exactly as the file warns.

TWO DEFECTS IN THE FINDER'S OWN WRITE-UP, which must not be carried into the file
- "some forty-five minutes of stream" is a duration measured across the 27:26-42:20 recess. That is standing hazard 2, and the arithmetic is also loose (22:12 to 01:04:49 is ~42.5 min of stream). Drop it; say only that it is an earlier, separate colloquy.
- The offered locator "lines 469-500" begins after the sentence the finding relies on. Novak's turn runs 445-456 (the stipulation sentence is line 456); the court's runs 485-500.

SEVERITY, STATED PRECISELY. Material as an attribution/citation defect: this is the only place in the library recording the "no copies" rationale, it is the stated ground of the level-3 (media-capture) bar that CR-E05 §2.1 and CR-E04's "admitted but not published" finding both sit inside, and a reader following the citation to 01:04:49 finds neither the stipulation nor the phrase. It corrupts NO substantive finding about the events of 2025-09-10, resolves or unsettles no register entry, and does not touch D-52. The correction runs neither toward the State nor toward the defence — it moves a sentence from a party's mouth to the bench's, which is a provenance fix, not a merits fix (hazard 4 observed: I am not hedging the confirmation, and not inflating it either).

RESIDUAL SCOPE. I verified the Day 1 publication colloquy, the 01:04:49 incident, and the five-day distribution of the phrase. I did not re-verify any other bullet in §2.1, and nothing outside §2.1. This is the Rev rendering, not the certified transcript.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED as an omission, but with the claimed severity DOWNGRADED from "material" to minor, and with three of the finder's supporting assertions REFUTED on the record. The library should adopt the corrected wording below, not the finder's.

WHAT SURVIVES ADVERSARIAL TESTING

1. The transcript reading is substantially right, and clears both speaker and timestamp hazards.
- day1.txt:1904 (01:09:10) — examining counsel asks that the witness step down and point out the courtyard on the exhibit. Functionally a question; speaker labelled "Chad Grunander," and the label is corroborated by the court addressing "Mr. Grunander" in adjacent turns at 01:05:07 (l.1692), 01:07:20 (l.1840) and 01:10:44 (l.1977). Hazard 1 cleared with a stated basis.
- day1.txt:1909 (01:09:20) — the court permits it, asks for a second microphone, and says "Ms. Nester, thank you for allowing us." Label = Judge Graf, content = a judicial ruling/direction. Label and content agree.
- The answers at l.1941/1949/1957/1965/1973 carry defence counsel Richard Novak's label but are the sworn witness Bagley's, exactly as CR-E05 §1.2 (l.37) establishes. The finder identified the speaker functionally and correctly.
- day1.txt:1977 (01:10:44) — the court's instruction. I read the passage; the finder's quotation is verbatim, including "because the video isn't being captured" and "just so the record knows to some degree where you're pointing." This is a Tier 1 judicial statement about the limits of the court's own record.

2. CR-E05 is genuinely silent. I read all 331 lines and grepped for point/monitor/gesture/captur/indicat/screen. §1.3 (l.50–55) lists timestamp hazards, name garbles, two missing conferences and the Exhibit 6.1 display; §9 (l.316–323) lists six residuals. Nothing records that gestures are outside the record. §4.5 (l.229) mentions the in-court identification "point-out" and its re-asking "for the benefit of the record," but never states why, and never treats it as an access-path limit. A library-wide grep found no equivalent caveat in any sibling file (CR-E01–E04, both CR-AUDITs, CR-ACQ).

3. It is the right class of caveat, and a stronger one than §1.3 currently holds. Every other §1.3 item is a Rev rendering defect that the certified transcript would cure. This one is in the recording medium — the court said so on the record — so it survives acquisition of the certified transcript (Q-36) and bears directly on §8 item 5 (l.308: the eight scene photographs, "all admitted Day 1, none held"). Per standing hazard 4, refusing a real, court-stated, verifiable caveat because the finder's arithmetic is loose would itself be a defect.

WHAT IS REFUTED — do not adopt the finder's version

(a) "Roughly a minute and a half ... exists only as 'this one right here'" is wrong twice over. The deictic-only run is five answers between stream identifiers 01:09:51 and 01:10:44 (l.1925–1973), not ~90 seconds. And the figure is itself a hazard-2 violation: it converts stream identifiers into a measured duration. Any adopted wording should cite the identifiers as identifiers and state no duration.

(b) "Irrecoverable from the certified transcript as well as from Rev" overstates the loss badly. The court's instruction was immediately effective and largely retrospective: Grunander re-asked, and the courtyard (l.1985), Hall of Flags (l.1993), Sorenson (l.2001), Losee (l.2017) and Fugal ("on the left of the picture," l.1993) were all re-located with orientation words within a few turns. Beyond that, every building involved had already been placed by cardinal direction in non-exhibit testimony at 51:53–52:48 and again on State's Exhibit 1 at 01:00:38–01:01:54 (Woodbury, for instance, "right directly east of the Fugal," 52:11). The only genuinely uncured items on State's Exhibit 2 are Woodbury's specific screen position and the Institute backside / parking structure — and that answer's substance was "No, not really," i.e. they are not usefully visible. Nothing in CR-E05's substantive findings depends on an uncaptured gesture; §3.3's "10–15 feet in from the guardrail" is spoken, not pointed (02:13:47).

(c) The finder missed the more useful half of the fact, which cuts against the "one window" framing. The instruction was given once and never enforced. Deictic-only identification recurs across the rest of the exhibit testimony: 01:21:48 ("The Sorenson building that's right here"), 01:29:44, 01:30:38, 01:31:00, 01:32:25, and on State's Exhibit 3.1 the screwdriver at 02:13:47 ("about right there") and the tape line at 02:32:28 ("it was right here, actually"). A search for /indicating|isn't being captured|for the benefit of the record|general location/ over day1.txt returns six hits, only one of which is this instruction — there is no second one. The recurrence, not the 01:09–01:11 window, is the caveat worth writing.

(d) Two minor finder errors not to carry forward. The court's "Ms. Nester, thank you for allowing us" (l.1909) does not say what she allowed; do not assert it was the step-down. And the parenthetical that the court addressed "Mr. Grunander" though the witness was pointing is ordinary practice — the court directs examining counsel to elicit the description — and should not enter the file as though it were an anomaly. (Incidentally the transcript renders defence counsel as both "Nestor" and "Nester"; §1.3's garble list at l.53 does not include this pair.)

SEVERITY. Minor. One §1.3 bullet and one §9 residual line. It corrects no existing finding and opens no register entry.

SEARCH SCOPE. All assertions of absence above are claims about full-text searches of the Rev rendering day1.txt via tsearch.py (method validated against the known positive /use pliers/ in day4.txt), and about a full read of CR-E05 plus a recursive grep over the library's .md files. Not claims about the certified transcript or the world.

**3. Does CR-E05 say it anywhere? No.** `grep -niE "parking|tunnel|heat ?plant|institute|garage|campus drive"` over the whole 331-line file returns **zero hits** — body, caveats, scoped nulls, open items and revision log alike. Method validated against a known positive (hazard 5): the same grep style returns 17 "parking" hits in day1.txt and 82 "Losee". The file is genuinely silent. §3.5 and §8 item 5 mention Exhibit 35 only as an item of unknown provenance, never saying what it depicts.

**4. The finder's transcript reading is accurate but INCOMPLETE, and one clause is a garble.** Two problems:

(a) **A second, fuller pass was missed.** The testimony occurs twice. Pass 1 (lines 1193–1224, 53:31–55:21) with no exhibit up. Pass 2 (lines 2565–2569 and 2697–2733, 01:26:17 and 01:30:38–01:32:17) with Bagley pointing at **State's Exhibit 35**, admitted at 01:28:02 over a defence objection that the aerial bears no date — followed by the street-grid testimony at 2737–2845.

At 01:31:13, pointing at Exhibit 35, Bagley says a person parking in "this LDS Institute parking lot over here on the north side" reaches the garage via "a tunnel that goes underneath the road that still comes out into the parking structure itself." So the tunnel connects the north parking **lot** to the **garage** under the road — not the garage to the Institute building. Adopting the finder's verbatim clause would import a garble into the library as a fact about physical geography.

**5. Materiality — CONFIRMED, and stronger than the finder argued.** This is not inert courtroom detail:
- The parking structure is where the State's entire movement narrative begins. CR-E04's timeline (line 59 ff.) has a vehicle believed to be Robinson's arriving there ~8:30 a.m., the driver leaving on foot for the quad, and a later return up the structure's stairs toward the Losee (day2.txt 908–1252).

**6. Steelman of CR-E05 — considered, and it fails.** The best defence is real: this is uncontested foundation elicited to qualify the witness for exhibit admission, the defence never crossed on it, CR-E05's stated job is findings rather than a turn-by-turn record, and CR-E04 already carries the structure. CONTENT CHECK — every quoted geometry answer verified verbatim: Hall of Flags "directly west," "butts up right against," "kind of like a bridge between two buildings," "an inside one and an outside one," the Fugal-to-science-building span, "windows so you can see through all the way to the Utah Lake" (51:00–51:38); Fugal south and abutting (51:50–51:57); Woodbury southeast, abutting, "directly east of the Fugal," "directly south of the Sorensen" (52:03–52:40); Sorensen "kind of like a northeast," abutting (52:25–52:35); Losee "Directly east of the courtyard, amphitheater area" / "No, not really… It doesn't run right up against it. So the Sorensen building is kind of like right between those two" / east of the Sorensen (52:51–53:12); LDS Institute north of the Losee (53:21). All accurate. "Fugal"/"Woodbury": zero — and zero anywhere in the library. No section, caveat, table or revision-log entry states the courtyard-to-Losee relationship. So the omission is real. The strongest defence is that this is textbook foundation testimony for photographs — the court admitted Exhibit 1 precisely because "This witness has firsthand knowledge of the location as well as the building locations" (line 1416) — and that a 331-line synthesis of ~2,600 turns must drop courtroom scaffolding. verdict.reasoning:
THE OMISSION IS REAL — BUT THE FINDER FOUND THE RIGHT HOLE THROUGH THE WRONG WINDOW, AND THEIR STATED RATIONALE MUST NOT BE ADOPTED.

TRANSCRIPT VERIFICATION (hazards 1, 2, 6, 7 checked)
- Speakers, functionally identified: the questioner labelled "Chad Grunander" is the examining prosecutor (the court addresses him as "Mr. Grunander" at day1.txt 1384, 1692, 1740); the answers labelled "Richard Novak" are the witness's (the questioner addresses him "Officer Bagley" at 1532; defence counsel introduces herself to "Officer Bagley" at 4718). So the answer at stream 01:02:41 (line 1584) IS Bagley's. The finder did not misidentify a speaker.
- The finder used 01:02:41 / 01:03:13 as identifiers only; no clock conversion. No hazard-2 violation. (Independently confirmed as stream time: at stream 02:42:17 the judge says lunch is "in that 12:00, 12:10 range," line 4690.)
- Quotation is faithful to line 1584 verbatim. The tape quote at line 1608 is faithful as to words but elides the opening clause — the witness first said it "looks like yellow crime scene tape," THEN said "That was some of our barrier..." (hazard 7).
- No objection or ruling attaches to either passage; the direct passage runs into the republication of State's Exhibit 1, granted at 01:02:59.

CR-E05 REALLY IS SILENT (whole-file check)
grep over the entire file for throw|gather|looking down|barrier|overtime|Hall of Flags|assignment|posted: line 97 is the only place the posting appears, and it gives no reason. Nothing in §3.5, §6, §6A, §7, the caveats or the revision log carries it. Not a "made elsewhere" false positive.

WHY THE FINDER'S RATIONALE IS REFUTED — the decisive passage they never reached
The finder read only the direct examination. The cross gives the fuller and materially DIFFERENT account, twice:
- day1.txt line 4746 (stream 02:43:36), asked why he attended no briefing: "I did not because that morning when I got there, we had individuals on top of the Hall of Flags... The Chief Long got a text or an email or phone call stating that there was people on top of the Hall of Flags throwing stuff down to the tent. Therefore, he sent the two officers that were on duty down to secure the area. I got dressed and then came back and then went to the Hall of Flags to secure that area."
- day1.txt line 4762 (02:44:18): "when I got there, it was starting to... People were throwing stuff down on the tent."
- day1.txt line 4978 (02:48:12), asked about written briefing materials: "No, not that morning. Like I said, it started getting hectic, so we were trying to get down there to secure the area and push people away from the top of the tent."

That refutes the finder's for-the-State half outright. The deployment was REACTIVE — a crowd-disorder call on the morning of the event — not "affirmative pre-event security thinking." The witness gives it as the reason NO briefing happened. Adding it to §7's for-the-prosecution column in the finder's words would put a false statement into the library and would be a correction running toward the State (the mirror of hazard 4).
It also over-reads the defence half. What UVU PD recognised was a crowd on a walkway throwing objects, not an elevated firing position; the barrier's stated purpose was "so people wouldn't go above that and walk" — pedestrian control. The Hall of Flags is part of the venue itself (a bridge between the Fugal and science buildings on the west edge of the courtyard, 51:22), not a standoff overwatch post. The finder's "they secured one elevated position over the tent and not the other" is a CONNECTION the record does not carry (objectivity mechanic 2). §3.5's Losee bullet is fully supported without it (verified at 02:45:43–02:46:11, lines 4838–4882).

STEELMAN OF CR-E05, AND WHY IT STILL FAILS
Best case for the file: §3.1 is a compressed scene-setter; §3.5's "in full" claim is about the CROSS, and the direct-exam reason at 01:02:41 falls outside it; the negatives it records ("No, not that morning") are faithful to the answers' bottom line; and §9.4 pre-warns the file is provisional. That defends omitting the 01:02:41 line the finder cited. It does NOT defend the file, because the fuller account is in the cross, inside §3.5's own stated scope, and it is the CAUSE of §3.5's lead bullet. Recording "no briefing, no debrief, no meeting" while dropping the reason the witness gave twice leaves a reader with pure negligence where the witness described a disturbance in progress — and simultaneously loses a previously unrecorded pre-shooting fact: a crowd-disorder incident directly over the principal's tent that diverted the only two on-duty officers. Both directions lost. Material.

BOTH-DIRECTIONS LOG (confirmations recorded, per the rule)
Confirmed FOR CR-E05: §3.5's Losee bullet, the six-of-fifteen officers count, no magnetometers, no drones, the armed private-security member beside him on the Hall of Flags, and the "no written materials" bullet all verify against 4746–4978. The redirect (04:20:10–04:22:03, lines 6207–6271) is a single holster question and does not touch the assignment — so the file did not miss a later correction.

VERDICT: CONFIRMED as an omission at material severity — relocated from the finder's §3.1/01:02:41 locator to the cross at lines 4746 and 4978, with the finder's "affirmative pre-event security thinking" framing and their proposed §7 for-the-prosecution entry REJECTED.
