findings.finding: FOUR FBI/DOJ REPORTING LIMITS confirmed by the witness as followed in this case: (1) an examiner may not state or imply that a match provides an ABSOLUTE IDENTIFICATION of the individual from whom the material originated — "You never said it was an absolute identification of Mr. Robinson, did you?" "Correct. No, I did not."; (2) an examiner shall not use "reasonable degree of scientific certainty" or similar — "That is correct. I was not."; (3) an examiner may not state or imply forensic autosomal DNA examinations have a ZERO ERROR RATE or are INFALLIBLE — "I am not, no."; (4) an examiner shall not assert that a likelihood ratio OF ANY MAGNITUDE provides an absolute identification or source attribution — "You're not implying that those numbers, that a previous witness quoted and are stated in your report, provides an absolute identification of Mr. Robinson or Mr. Twiggs?" "No, I'm not."

Sources of error, as she gave them: "Human error could be an error… One of the big things is potential human error. I guess you could also associate the DNA testing itself and how items are collected or how those items are tested."

ACTIVITY LEVEL AND TIMING — she cannot opine on either. FBI policy: "I cannot give an opinion as far as activity level goes… just because DNA is on an item doesn't necessarily mean that an individual touched it or utilized that item." On timing: "I cannot give exact timing as to when DNA was deposited on an item," and on a found item she agreed flatly: "Sure, that's correct." DNA in ideal conditions "can persist on an item rather indefinitely"; the lab has recovered DNA from items 40 and 50 years old.

ITEM IDENTITY AND PROFILE QUALITY. Item 7 = "Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863"; Item 8 = "Screwdriver from perch" (read from State's Exhibit 31 by Sgt. Faumuina). Bakker: Item 8 (screwdriver) showed degradation — "a ski slope-type effect"; Item 7 (transcribed "the tau") had "slight amount of degradation, but not as much as Item 8." Item 7 yielded a FULL profile; Item 8 yielded a PARTIAL profile — "I did not develop DNA at every single location," so "I did not have data at all 23 locations to compare it to either Mr. Robinson or Mr. Twiggs." Known reference samples from both men were full profiles.

TEST PLATFORM: GlobalFiler kit, "21 different locations on a human's DNA, in addition to three sex determining locations" — she then said "21 and three sex type determining, so 24 total." The transcript ALSO carries "all 23 locations" twice, once in counsel's question and once in her own answer. 24 and 23 both appear; the record does not reconcile them. Sex-determining loci as she named them: amelogenin, "Y indel," and "DYS385" — but she later testified "DYS391 is actually that male location." DYS385 is not a GlobalFiler marker; DYS391 is. The "DYS385" utterance is either a misspeak or a transcription error.

STR METHOD LIMIT conceded: the testing measures LENGTH ONLY, not sequence. "the sequence would be equivalent to letters in a word. What I'm looking at is the number of words versus the letters that make up that word." At the close of direct: "Correct. I only utilize length differences, STRs in this case. The FBI laboratory does not use sequencing for nuclear DNA testing, nor am I qualified in it." She agreed she cannot distinguish the evidence samples from Mr. Robinson at the five isoallele locations charted in Baker 34/35. The FBI uses next-generation sequencing only for mitochondrial DNA.
findings.locator: day2.txt L5942, L8822-L8842; charts at L8638-L8782

findings.finding: MIXTURE PROPORTIONS — recorded EXACTLY, with the ambiguity preserved. Item 7: "Yes, it was. For one of the runs when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs, it was a 5% to 95%." Item 8: "For item eight, one of the contributors was 11% and the other was approximately 89%." WHICH person is the 5% and which the 95% is NOT stated on the record. She also testified she did not calculate the proportions personally — STRmix produces them.

PCAST EXCHANGE — the defence's strongest line and her answer to it. Burt read the PCAST conclusion that published evidence supports foundational validity of probabilistic genotyping "of DNA mixtures of three individuals in which the minor contributor constitutes at least 20% of the intact DNA in the mixture…"; she answered "That sounds accurate, yes." She agreed both samples had minor contributors below 20%. Her rebuttal, verbatim: "That is true, but in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals." She also stated PCAST "called into question mixtures of three or more individuals with that minor or that low level contributor making up 20% or less," and disputed the defence's framing that PCAST was written by practitioners: "the PCAST report was written by individuals that were not practitioners or any type of laboratory personnel."

NUMBER OF CONTRIBUTORS (NoC) IS THE EXAMINER'S SUBJECTIVE INPUT: "That's my determination based on my experience and training looking at the data. That's something I input into STRmix." She resisted "complex" ("Not necessarily") but conceded it "could be" in mixtures of many individuals with similar peak heights. On the NIST 2024 report she answered: "we never truly know the number of contributors in a forensic sample… I'm making the best determination based on the DNA evidence that I have." She reads NoC using peaks BELOW the 150 RFU analytical threshold.

THE 3→2 CHANGE, IN HER OWN SEQUENCE. Original NoC for Item 7 was THREE, reached "somewhere around September 12th." Technical reviewer Tara Benson independently read it as TWO; they discussed; "she agreed with me calling it three." Bakker changed it to TWO on "September 13th of 2025" — the SAME DAY she reported the technically reviewed inclusion result to the agents. The stated cause of the change was not the reviewer: "I was submitted an elimination sample from Mr. Twiggs… When I compared him to this sample, all of the DNA, unlike that major contributor, matched to Mr. Twiggs. So because of that, I determined that there's actually only two individuals, because those small peaks, there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to."

THE CONDITIONING MECHANISM, STATED BY HER: "if I'm utilizing someone as a known elimination sample, I will apply their DNA profile both to the HP and HD" — i.e. to BOTH the prosecution and the defence hypothesis. She confirmed HP = prosecution hypothesis, HD = defence hypothesis, and that HD for a comparison is "another unknown unrelated person." On the Item 7-1 Twiggs run (Baker 38, pp.39-44) the STRmix input was: assume TWO contributors; known contributor under HP = sample 61, Twiggs's known sample; known contributors under HD = LEFT BLANK.

THE LIKELIHOOD RATIO FOR TWIGGS WAS ONE. Q: "what was the likelihood ratio that you calculated based on this chart?" A: "The likelihood ratio was one." Q: "So that doesn't rise to the level of even limited inclusion, correct?" A: "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative." Her explanation: "I didn't utilize this calculation to determine that Mr. Twiggs was a possible contributor or that I could use him as an assumed contributor. I visually looked at the DNA sample… We don't have a threshold. I don't have to see two, four, eight peaks to determine I think an individual is present given that the field submitted him as an elimination… I assumed he was a contributor. When I compared him to that data, I did see his DNA present. So when I calculated the statistic for Mr. Robinson, I used Mr. Twiggs as an elimination."

THE VERBAL SCALE (State's Exhibit 31 p.5): likelihood ratio ≥ 1,000,000 = "very strong support for inclusion"; a likelihood ratio of TWO is the floor for "even limited support for an inclusion" ("Correct, yes"); a likelihood ratio of ONE is "uninformative." NOTE: as transcribed she assigned "very strong support for inclusion" to BOTH the ≥1,000,000 band AND the "10,000 to less than one million" band — internally inconsistent as recorded, and consistent with a misspeak or a transcription error.

WHY TWIGGS WAS TREATED AS AN ELIMINATION — and the towel problem. Her basis: "Mr. Twiggs was a roommate of Mr. Robinson. And it was thought that those items came from potentially Mr. Robinson's home… in talking to the investigators, based on their investigation, it was important to assume potentially Mr. Twiggs was present." She was asked whether any investigator told her the towel did not come from Robinson's home but was found in a bush at the university: "I was aware of that, yes." And: "That is correct. It was found outside of a home. But again, based on speaking with the investigators, they had information to suspect that that towel came from Mr. Robinson's home and I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination."

THREE LOCI WHERE THE ELIMINATION DONOR'S TYPES WERE ABSENT FROM ITEM 8, as she testified: at D16 Twiggs is 9,12 and Item 8 yielded only a 12; at D19S Twiggs is 14,16 and no 16 was found in 8A; at THO1 Twiggs is 7, 9.3 and no 7 was found in 8.1. Her answer: "this is a mixture and there is some dropout. So just because I didn't see a seven, for example, does not mean I would automatically exclude someone," and at the THO1 location "there's only one individual represented there. So when comparing an elimination, I would essentially ignore that location." She distinguished single-source from mixture: a one-locus mismatch is an exclusion for single-source, but for a mixture "it's not that cut and dry."

STRmix NON-DETERMINISM, conceded: "each time you run the software, you will get a different number"; "you will never get the same answer twice, but it will be no more than a magnitude of 10"; "I might get 10 quadrillion the first time, two quadrillion the second time." On changing NoC: "But it does change it, correct?" "Yes" — with the qualification that for a major contributor the change from three to two "doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much."

SAMPLE CONSUMPTION. She requested and received permission for destructive testing BEFORE receiving any samples. Consumed: Items 1-6 (swabs from possible smudge, hand swipe, possible sweat drop, possible smudge, possible smudge, possible sweat drop) plus Items 54 and 55 (swabs of swiped finger areas; swabs of stairwell railing). Items 1-6 were taken from the northeast corner of the Losee building (transcribed "loci building") and yielded NO DNA — "There was nothing for me to compare to." Approximately 3 microliters of extract remained after 10 microliters were used; she agreed the remaining 3 would still yield no DNA. She confirmed both the NRC 1996 statement about preserving the accused's opportunity for repeat testing and FBI standard 7.4 on retaining or returning a portion.

ITEM 55 — TWO SWABS COMBINED INTO ONE SAMPLE. She did not inquire whether the two stairwell-railing swabs came from different areas: "They were both labeled as coming from the same stairwell and they were packaged together. So our policies and procedures is that we can combine those two together." Result: "I got DNA from more than five individuals, so I could not provide a conclusion."

THE BACKPACK. Item 9 was a backpack plus a number of items from it. She testified: "initially we didn't have any information. So we processed that… As the investigation continues, it was determined that that backpack was potentially left behind by a bystander and there was no comparisons needed at that time." Defence pressed with her case notes at page 20 — "The backpack belongs to Kirk's detailees" — and she answered that this was not her communication log entry but another laboratory staffer's record of information received.

THE COURT'S POSTURE. The State objected repeatedly that the line was beyond the scope of a preliminary hearing and into Rule 702 territory; the judge cited State v. Ramirez 2012 UT 59 ¶10 ("the magistrate's role does not encompass an assessment of whether such inference is more plausible than an alternative that cuts in favor of the defense"), and later State v. Merrill and "State v. Drozbeck" (as transcribed) via the State. The judge repeatedly allowed "one more question" and framed the limit as "whether we walk one mile or a hundred miles down the path." Defence's counter-argument was that the court had already ruled it retains the ultimate determination of the RELIABILITY of Rule 1102 hearsay, which the defence characterised as "the law of this case." NO ruling was made on the reliability of the DNA evidence during this testimony.

REV SPEAKER-LABEL FAILURE ON DAY 2, CONFIRMED (hazard 1). The oath administered to Bakker carries the label "Ms. Nestor." Kathy Nestor is DEFENCE COUNSEL for Mr. Robinson — she identifies herself at L239 ("Kathy Nestor, Michael Burt, Richard Novak, Stacy Visser here for Mr. Robinson") and at L2026 ("my name's Kathy Nestor. I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Robinson") and she conducts defence cross-examination for hundreds of turns. The content shows the court directing the witness to "come forward right up here by the bailiff and being sworn in." Both oaths administered on Day 2 (L4417 and L5086) carry the "Ms. Nestor" label. Rev is systematically mislabelling the oath-giver on Day 2 exactly as it does on Day 1.

TRANSCRIPT GARBLES IDENTIFIED, with the basis for each. "loci building" (L8438) = LOSEE building — day2.txt spells "Losee" correctly 26 times elsewhere. "the tau" (L5850) = the towel. "TPOC's location" (L6179) = TPOX. "BWA" (L6155) = vWA — spelled "VWA" at L8770. "D3S-loci" (L6131) = D3S1358. "SDRs" (L8570) = STRs. "ACTNG" (L8562) = ACTG. "scene a DNA profile" (L7885) = seeing. "Item 7, sub 1 and what are 1.7 octillion" (L4877) = "are." "Special Agent Folger" (L5277) vs "Fulger" (L7617) = one person. "Ms. Baker" throughout = Bakker. "National Resource Council" (L6235, L6251) = National Research Council. "DNA Technology in Forensic Science" and "The Evaluation of Forensic DNA Evidence" (1996) are named correctly. "State v. q06_a.both_directions:
"CUTS FOR THE STATE. Bakker held up well under a long, technically aggressive direct by defence counsel, and she declined to concede several propositions the defence put to her — that mixtures are inherently challenging (she gave the coffee-cup illustration and said 'Not necessarily'), that dropout risks misreading a heterozygote as a homozygote (the stochastic threshold governs, and she said she would not automatically exclude), that number-of-contributors determination is inherently complex, that she 'disregarded' STRmix, and that PCAST was 'written by experts in your field' (she corrected: 'individuals that were not practitioners or any type of laboratory personnel'). Her answer to the defence's single strongest point — that both minor contributors fall below PCAST's 20% threshold — is directly responsive and, if correct, dispositive of it: PCAST's caveat is addressed to mixtures of THREE OR MORE individuals, and she interpreted these as two-person mixtures. Item 7 gave a FULL profile. The technical reviewer independently reviewed the data and, after discussion, agreed with the three-contributor call; the later change to two was driven by receipt of a new known sample, not by the reviewer's dissent. Her credentials, elicited by the State on cross, are substantial: eleven years as a forensic examiner after six as a bench biologist, a two-year training programme with oral and written boards and moot court, a competency exam, ANAB accreditation audited every four years, annual continuing education and vendor proficiency testing, and STRmix validated both developmentally in peer-reviewed work and internally by the FBI, in use in approximately 120 laboratories. She was scrupulous about reporting limits, volunteering the boundaries of her own opinion rather than being cornered into them, and she twice refused to overstate ('I don't want to use the word source'; 'I don't know that I would say if it has significance. I report the value that's calculated'). The court, for its part, repeatedly cut the defence's line short as beyond the probable-cause standard.

CUTS AGAINST THE STATE. The conditioning is the whole of it: both headline figures compare 'Twiggs and T. Robinson' against 'Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person,' so the elimination donor's presence is not a finding of the statistic — it is the floor the statistic stands on. And the one calculation that could have supported that floor returned a likelihood ratio of ONE, which by her own verbal scale is 'uninformative' and falls below the value of 2 needed for even 'limited support for an inclusion.' She placed him in the sample visually instead, on the strength of the field having submitted him as an elimination — and the 15 September log entry records that the decision to issue the report 'with Twiggs as an assumed contributor' was already settled 'per previous discussions' with investigators before the confirming statistic was run. The premise investigators gave her (that the items came from Mr. Robinson's home) sits awkwardly against her own acknowledgement that the towel was found in a bush at the university. The number of contributors is her subjective input, read partly from peaks below the analytical threshold; it moved from three to two on 13 September, the same day she reported the inclusion result; and she agreed changing it changes the output. STRmix is non-deterministic within a factor of ten by her own account. Item 8 was a partial profile — she had no data at every location to compare against either known sample — and at three loci the elimination donor's own types were absent from Item 8, explained by dropout in a mixture. Both minor fractions (5% and 11%) fall below PCAST's 20% figure; her answer to that turns entirely on the two-contributor call, which is the very determination at issue. The testing measures length only and cannot distinguish isoalleles at five or six of the compared loci — she conceded she cannot distinguish the evidence samples from Mr. Robinson on sequence, and is not qualified in sequencing. Items 1 through 6 were consumed entirely and yielded no DNA at all, leaving about three microliters of extract; Items 54 and 55 were consumed, and two stairwell swabs were combined into a single sample that produced a mixture of more than five individuals on which no conclusion was possible. Finally, she may not opine on how or when any DNA was deposited, may not claim absolute identification or a zero error rate, and disclaims any 'reasonable degree of scientific certainty.'

WHAT NEITHER SIDE GETS. The anchors verify; the connection does not follow from them. That an examiner's reported likelihood ratios are enormous is a fact about a conditional calculation, not about who touched a towel — she said so herself. Equally, that the elimination donor's stand-alone likelihood ratio was one is not evidence he is absent, and the defence never established that assuming an elimination contributor is improper practice rather than routine. This transcript establishes what a witness said under oath. It establishes nothing about the world, and the court made no reliability ruling on any of it."

q06_b.headline: The astronomical likelihood ratios in State's Exhibit 31 are conditioned on Lance Twiggs being a contributor in BOTH the prosecution and defence propositions — and the only STRmix statistic ever run on Twiggs alone (item 7-1, 2025-09-15, NoC=2) returned a likelihood ratio of 1, which on the FBI lab's own verbal scale is "uninformative." Bakker testified she reported Twiggs as a contributor anyway, on visual inspection plus the investigators' designation of him as an elimination sample, and then used him as an elimination when calculating the statistic for Robinson. She also conceded both mixtures had minor contributors below PCAST's 20% threshold (5% on item 7, 11% on item 8), and that her original three-contributor call on item 7 was changed to two only after Twiggs's sample arrived.

findings.finding: WITNESS POSTURE (context established outside the range but governing it). Bakker is a DEFENCE witness taken out of order during the State's case-in-chief. At day2 L4412 the prosecutor previews: "we're going to call an FBI DNA analyst out of order. It's a defense witness, but that's to accommodate that witness's schedule." At L7601 the court says on resuming: "We are still with Mr. Burt and Ms. Baker on direct examination." Everything in lines 6550-8100 is therefore DEFENCE DIRECT, not cross. Michael Burt = defence counsel (functionally: he examines, he says "the defense is entitled to inquire", "when we objected"); Mr. McBride = State (functionally: he objects, argues "light most favorable to the state").
findings.locator: day2.txt L4412, L7601; Burt functional markers L6831, L7965

findings.finding: SPEAKER-LABEL CHECK (standing hazard 1). Across lines 6550-8100 the Rev labels and the content AGREE at every turn. "Michael Burt" always asks or argues; "Ms. Bakker" always answers; "Mr. McBride" always objects/argues for the State; "Judge" always rules or directs. Blank-label continuation turns (L6812, L6816, L7249, L8155, L8167, L8207, L8215, L8235, L8263, L8267) each continue the immediately preceding speaker and are consistent on content. No Day-1-style label inversion found in this range. This is a positive method check, not an assumption.

MIXTURE PROPORTIONS, AND WHAT THEY ARE CONDITIONED ON. Item 7: "For one of the runs when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs, it was a 5% to 95%." Item 8: "one of the contributors was 11% and the other was approximately 89%." CONDITIONING: the item-7 figure is expressly the output of a STRmix run in which Robinson was the person compared and Twiggs was conditioned on (assumed). She also stated she did not calculate the proportions herself — STRmix produces them as a by-product of deconvolution.
findings.locator: day2.txt L6551, L6559; method statement L6543

findings.finding: PCAST 20% THRESHOLD — CONCEDED FOR BOTH ITEMS. Burt: "you do know that in this case, both your samples had minor contributors below 20%?" Bakker: "That is true, but in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals." Her rebuttal is that PCAST's stated concern is confined to mixtures of three or more ("PCAST called into question mixtures of three or more individuals with that minor or that low level contributor making up 20% or less", L6527), and her final call on these items was two.

THE CIRCULARITY THE RANGE EXPOSES (analyst observation, not a resolution). The PCAST escape at L6699 depends on the mixture being two-person. The two-person call on item 7 was itself reached only by assuming Twiggs: she changed from three contributors to two on 2025-09-13 after receiving Twiggs's elimination sample, because once Twiggs accounted for the non-major DNA "there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to." Neither counsel put this circularity to her in this range. This is an observation about the structure of the testimony, not a finding that her conclusion is wrong.

THE HYPOTHESIS PAIR AS SET UP IN STRmix. "likelihood ratio compares the probabilities of seeing a DNA profile given one of two different scenarios or explanations or hypotheses. One is that a particular person of interest is a contributor and the other is that an unknown unrelated individual is a contributor... if I'm utilizing someone as a known elimination sample, I will apply their DNA profile both to the HP and HD." HP = prosecution hypothesis, HD = defence hypothesis, both confirmed by her. HD with no known contributor entered means "another unknown unrelated person."

THE 2025-09-15 STRmix RUN ON TWIGGS ALONE — INPUTS. Defence exhibit "Baker 38, pages 39-44" (six-page STRmix report, dated September 15, item 7-1). Summary of input as walked through: number of contributors ASSUMED = 2; evidence sample = 7A, entered as raw data ("just the numbers from the graph"); HP known contributors = sample 61 (Twiggs's known sample); HD known contributors = LEFT BLANK. Output columns are FBI population databases: BAH (Burt: "Bahamians"; Bakker adds "And African Americans"), Caucasians, SEH = Southeast Hispanics, and Southwest Hispanics.

THE RESULT: LIKELIHOOD RATIO = 1, "UNINFORMATIVE." Q: "what was the likelihood ratio that you calculated based on this chart?" A: "The likelihood ratio was one." Q: "So that doesn't rise to the level of even limited inclusion, correct?" A: "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative." This is the only numeric likelihood ratio stated anywhere in lines 6550-8100.

SHE REPORTED TWIGGS AS A CONTRIBUTOR NOTWITHSTANDING THE LR OF 1, AND SAID SO PLAINLY. "I did. So actually I didn't utilize this calculation to determine that Mr. Twiggs was a possible contributor or that I could use him as an assumed contributor. I visually looked at the DNA sample and the DNA, unlike that major contributor, he also had those peaks... There are multiple different ways. We don't have a threshold. I don't have to see two, four, eight peaks to determine I think an individual is present given that the field submitted him as an elimination." Then, decisively: "So when I calculated the statistic for Mr. Robinson, I used Mr. Twiggs as an elimination."

SHE REFUSED THE 'EXCLUDED' FRAMING — a point that cuts FOR the State. Burt: "when you ran Mr. Twiggs' sample through STRmix, the result you got was that he was not a contributor, correct? Or that it was not even of limited value in including him?" (compound question). Bakker answered only the second limb: "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative, but I did use my own knowledge and training to determine that I was going to utilize him as an assumed contributor." She also rejected "disregarded": "I can't say that I disregarded it. When I'm comparing someone, that's my first determination: do I think this person is potentially included or excluded? If I determine that I think they're included, I will run STRmix to give weight to that inclusion."

REPORT LANGUAGE ASYMMETRY, PUT TO HER AND ANSWERED. Burt: "in the body of your report, you say that one of the contributors is Twiggs. You don't say he's a possible contributor, like you do for Mr. Robinson, you say he is a contributor." Bakker: "I do. And with elimination samples, that's slightly different" — analogising to a consensual partner in a sexual-assault case. She resisted the word "source": "I don't want to use the word source... using the word assumed, that's verbiage that we use when we calculate our statistical calculation. I'm letting the software know I know this individual is there."

THE ELIMINATION DESIGNATION CAME FROM THE INVESTIGATORS, NOT FROM THE ANALYST'S OWN KNOWLEDGE. "from what I recall in speaking with the investigators, Mr. Twiggs was a roommate of Mr. Robinson. And it was thought that those items came from potentially Mr. Robinson's home. And I don't recall exactly if it was a situation where a particular towel was known to have been in that house. I don't remember that exactly. But in talking to the investigators, based on their investigation, it was important to assume potentially Mr. Twiggs was present." She also testified she consulted investigators on WHETHER to treat Twiggs as an elimination at all: "I talked to them with regards to if I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination versus comparing him and offering a statistic."

THE TOWEL-PROVENANCE CONCESSION. Burt: "Did any investigator ever tell you that the towel did not come from Mr. Robinson's home but was found in a bush out at the university?" Bakker: "I was aware of that, yes." Burt: "So you knew that that towel was not found in a place where you would [expect] Mr. Twiggs' DNA to be present?" Bakker: "That is correct. It was found outside of a home. But again, based on speaking with the investigators, they had information to suspect that that towel came from Mr. Robinson's home and I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination." (Rev renders "expect" as "inspect" at L7512; content wins.)

THE 2025-09-15 CASE NOTE, READ INTO THE RECORD BY COUNSEL AND ADOPTED BY THE WITNESS (page 24 of 379). "Spoke with Special Agent Fulger, gave update on report timeline, discussed it upon review it was decided that additional statistics needed to be run. Report will still be issued with Twiggs as an assumed contributor per previous discussions with Fulger and Carmack." Bakker: "Yes, I do [see that]." She explained the additional statistic was the Twiggs-alone comparison, run "After discussion with my reviewer."

NUMBER-OF-CONTRIBUTORS CHRONOLOGY, ITEM 7. Original call = 3 contributors, reached "somewhere around September 12th" (2025). Changed to 2 on "September 13th of 2025," after receiving Twiggs's elimination sample: "When I compared him to this sample, all of the DNA, unlike that major contributor, matched to Mr. Twiggs. So because of that, I determined that there's actually only two individuals, because those small peaks, there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to."

NoC IS THE ANALYST'S SUBJECTIVE INPUT — CONCEDED, WITH A LIMIT. "That's my determination based on my experience and training looking at the data. That's something I input into STRmix." Asked if it is a complex determination: "Not necessarily"; but "It could be. Again, if there's mixtures of a lot of individuals and a lot of the peak heights, the size of the spikes are relatively the same, it could cause some trouble for me as an examiner." And when pressed on the NIST finding: "we never truly know the number of contributors in a forensic sample."

TWO ANALYSTS, TWO NoC READINGS OF THE SAME DATA — AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. Defence exhibit "Baker 4, page 365" is the technical reviewer's note, stamped "approved by Tara Benson." Notation: "71 male discussed three NOC and okay with three." Bakker: "she determined that male DNA was present and she concluded that she would have called it a number of contributor of two. She compared it to my conclusions. I said number of contributor three. So we had a discussion... And she said she agreed with me calling it three." It was "a quick discussion. And this is not unusual." AGAINST the State: two qualified analysts read the same electropherogram differently, and the reviewer moved by discussion rather than new data. FOR the State: the reviewer's independent first reading (two) is the number Bakker ultimately reported.

THE REVIEWER NOTE POST-DATED HER CONCLUSIONS — AND THE COURT'S STATED ADMISSIBILITY RATIONALE WAS NOT SUPPLIED IN THE TERMS THE COURT FRAMED. The judge asked directly: "as it relates to State's Exhibit 31, was this relied upon in order for State's Exhibit 31 to be put together as the report?... that's a crucial point I don't have the answer to just yet." Bakker twice put it the other way: "this was created after I had already drew my own conclusions" and "They are kept with the case file after I draw my conclusions." She also declined Burt's "took into account" framing: "I don't know that I would agree that I took into account. We had already had that conversation." The court nonetheless found it relevant and admitted it.

findings.finding: STRmix IS NOT RUN-TO-RUN REPRODUCIBLE — CONCEDED, WITH A STATED BOUND. "each time you run the software, you will get a different number based on the math that the software system does. But there are studies and validations that show we don't expect that math to be greatly different, usually by a factor of 10." And: "you will never get the same answer twice, but it will be no more than a magnitude of 10." Illustration: "I might get 10 quadrillion the first time, two quadrillion the second time." (The quadrillion figures are HER ILLUSTRATION, not this case's numbers — /quadrillion/ returns only these three hits in the whole of day2.txt.)

CHANGING NoC CHANGES THE LR — AND HER REASSURANCE IS EXPRESSLY CONDITIONED ON THE COMPARED PERSON BEING THE MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR. "if that major contributor is the individual that I'm comparing to, if I change the number of contributors to two... it doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much." Burt: "But it does change it, correct?" Bakker: "Yes." Record the conditioning exactly: the insensitivity claim is asserted for a MAJOR contributor only; she said nothing in this range about the effect on a minor contributor's LR.

THE VERBAL SCALE (page 5 of State's Exhibit 31), AND A PROBABLE SLIP IN IT. "this is our verbal scale. In addition to the numerical likelihood ratio value that I provide, I also give a qualitative or a verbal equivalent to that numerical value." As spoken: "if I have a likelihood ratio that's greater than or equal to one million, I designate that as very strong support for inclusion. The next example, 10,000 to less than one million, I would say that's very strong support for inclusion and so forth." The identical adjective for two adjacent bands is very likely a verbal or transcription slip, but I record what was said. Bottom of the scale confirmed: LR of 2 is the floor for "limited support" for inclusion; LR of 1 is "uninformative." Burt described the chart's left column as running from "greater than one million" to "less than one in a hundred," implying exclusion bands she did not describe.

ANALYTICAL THRESHOLD = 150 RFU, AND SUB-THRESHOLD PEAKS ARE USED FOR NoC. "our analytical threshold is 150. Any peak that is 150 or greater, the software system will give me that allele call... Any peak that's below the 150, the software system will not give me an allele call for it." Burt: "Even though it might be a true allele?" Bakker: "Correct. Yes." Burt: "in determining the number of contributors, you look below that 150 RFU level?" Bakker: "And that is true, yes." RFU = relative fluorescent unit. A stochastic threshold exists but no number for it was given in this range.

HOW SHE GOT TO THREE CONTRIBUTORS — the electropherogram walkthrough (defence exhibit "Baker 4, page 128"). Four loci displayed; three named: D2S441, D19S433, FGA. Method: count labelled peaks per locus; three called peaks at each of those three loci means "at least two individuals"; then examine UNCALLED sub-threshold peaks to ask whether a third person is present — "that 12 in that bottom box, is it the same contributor as, for example, the 22 under FGA... Because I'm able to use information below the threshold and I see peaks, that gives me an indication that I can increase my number of contributors to three, which I did in this case." Burt told the court, and she confirmed, that SHE identified this page to both counsel pre-hearing as illustrating why she originally called three.
findings.locator: day2.txt L7416-7420; pre-hearing point L7252, L7308-7312

findings.finding: ALLELE-LEVEL DISCREPANCIES BETWEEN TWIGGS'S KNOWN PROFILE AND ITEM 8. D16: Twiggs = 9,12; "The only piece of information I had for sample eight at item D16 was a 12." D19S: Twiggs = 14,16; no 16 allele found in 8A. TH01 ("THO"): Twiggs = 7, 9.3; no 7 allele in the 8.1 sample. Her answers: mixtures allow dropout, so absence is not automatic exclusion; and at TH01, "There's only one individual represented there. So when comparing an elimination, I would essentially ignore that location. I'm looking at the other locations where there was two individuals present."

THE EXCLUSION RULE — HOW SHE BOUNDED IT. Burt read from Butler's textbook: "if any STR locus fails to match when comparing the genotypes between two or more samples, then the comparison of profiles between the question and the reference sample is usually declared a non-match regardless of how many other loci match." Bakker: "I would agree with that if it's a single source sample... If I have a mixture, it's not that cut and dry. I have to take into account how many people are in that mixture, how many pieces of information I have, is there potential dropout? So just because someone may not be present in a mixture doesn't necessarily mean that I'm going to automatically exclude them."

PCAST — HER CHARACTERISATION AND THE CONCESSION ON IT. She first said the PCAST report "was written by individuals that were not practitioners or any type of laboratory personnel," then agreed it lists experts who provided input, including Bruce Budowle, whom she agreed "was the head of your unit for a number of years before you came on board" and who "has written extensively" on forensic DNA. She did not recognise two other named FBI Laboratory forensic examiners put to her. She agreed the PCAST finding as read to her "sounds accurate": foundational validity supported "of DNA mixtures of three individuals in which the minor contributor constitutes at least 20% of the intact DNA in the mixture." Asked why 20% raises reliability issues: "I do not know."

THE 2024 NIST REPORT — RAISED, LARGELY EXCLUDED, AND NOT CONFIRMED BY THE WITNESS. Title as given by Burt: "Forensic DNA Interpretation and Human Factors: Improving Practice Through a Systems Approach" (2024), NIST, which she agreed is a federal body in the Department of Commerce. She is "familiar" with it but "I've read highlights of it" and does not recall the authors. The single question the court allowed — whether NIST concluded "it remains unclear if visual inspection renders consistent number of contributor estimations across analysts over time" — she did NOT confirm or deny as to the report's content; she answered about her own practice instead, conceding only that "we never truly know the number of contributors."

This is not a conflict between sources — it is a structural feature of the statistic that no library file currently records. Recommend opening it as an OPEN entry framed as a conditioning question, not as a challenge to any person's competence or good faith. Resolving artifacts: State's Exhibit 31 plus Baker 38 pp.39-44.

CANDIDATE NEW ENTRY: 'The NoC 3-to-2 revision and its dependence on the elimination assumption.' Distinct from the above: it concerns whether the two-person interpretation — which is what removes the PCAST three-person caveat — is independent of the Twiggs assumption. The technical reviewer's independent first reading of TWO cuts in favour of independence; the sequence (three on 09-12, two on 09-13 after Twiggs's sample arrived) cuts against. NOTHING HERE RESOLVES ANY REGISTER ENTRY AGAINST A NAMED PERSON, and none should be resolved that way on this material. Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and has not been bound over; Lance Twiggs is not charged in this case; the analyst's methodology was contested by counsel and no court finding was made on it — the magistrate expressly declined to weigh reliability at this stage.
q06_b.both_directions:
CUTS AGAINST THE STATE. (1) The conditioning. Both reported likelihood ratios place Twiggs inside the prosecution AND the defence proposition; the only STRmix statistic ever run on Twiggs by himself returned LR = 1, which the analyst agreed is "uninformative" on her own lab's scale — and she nevertheless reported him as an unqualified "contributor," the stronger word she withholds from Robinson. She then used him as an elimination when computing Robinson's statistic (L8122). (2) The 20% concession. Both mixtures had minor contributors below the PCAST threshold: 5% on item 7, 11% on item 8, conceded outright. (3) The escape from that concession — that these were two-person mixtures — depends on the very assumption at issue, since item 7 was called three contributors until Twiggs's sample arrived on 2025-09-13. (4) Subjectivity of the number-of-contributors call: two qualified analysts read the same electropherogram and initially differed (3 vs 2); the reviewer moved by "a quick discussion," not new data; and the call uses UNCALLED peaks BELOW the 150 RFU analytical threshold. (5) Non-reproducibility: "you will never get the same answer twice"; and changing NoC changes the LR ("But it does change it, correct?" "Yes"). (6) Context flow to the analyst: the elimination designation came from investigators who believed the items came from Robinson's home, while the analyst knew the towel was recovered outdoors at the university and could not recall any towel being known to have been in the house; the 2025-09-15 case note records the reporting decision made "per previous discussions with Fulger and Carmack." (7) Three loci where Twiggs's own alleles are not fully represented in item 8, at one of which she said she would "essentially ignore that location."

CUTS FOR THE STATE — and this is not a short list. (1) She refused the defence's framing every time it overreached: "uninformative" is not exclusion; "I can't say that I disregarded it"; absence in a mixture is not automatic exclusion; the Butler single-locus rule binds single-source samples, not mixtures. Her corrections were specific and immediate, including correcting counsel about which exhibit page he was displaying. (2) PCAST's stated concern, on the very words counsel read to her, is confined to three-person mixtures — hers was called two. (3) The technical reviewer's INDEPENDENT first reading of item 7 was two contributors, which is the number ultimately reported: the exhibit the defence introduced to prove subjectivity also shows independent convergence on the final answer. (4) Applying an assumed contributor's profile to both HP and HD is, on her account, the ordinary treatment of an elimination sample, not a thumb on the scale; and her described workflow (visual include/exclude first, statistics to weight an inclusion) is a stated standard procedure, not a post-hoc override. (5) She bounded STRmix variability ("no more than a magnitude of 10") and grounded it in validation studies. (6) The 3-to-2 change is attributed to new data arriving and is contemporaneously documented rather than concealed — the defence's best exhibits came out of the analyst's own case file, and she had volunteered the key electropherogram page to BOTH counsel before the hearing (L7252, L7308-7312). (7) Legally, the court sustained the State's position in substance: it curtailed the reliability inquiry four times, quoted Ramirez on the magistrate's limited role, and made no finding that any of this evidence is unreliable.

WHAT NEITHER SIDE ESTABLISHED — stated plainly rather than hedged, since over-hedging is itself a defect here. No court has found any of this testimony true; the hearing tests probable cause only. Nothing in this range shows the likelihood ratios are miscalculated, and nothing shows Twiggs's DNA is absent: an LR of 1 means the data are equally probable under either proposition, which is neither inclusion nor exclusion, and the witness said exactly that. Equally, nothing in this range independently verifies the conditioning assumption. The honest statement of the record is narrow and firm: the octillion/quintillion figures are CONDITIONAL statistics whose condition — that Twiggs is a contributor — is supported by the analyst's visual judgment and the investigators' expectation rather than by any statistic she produced, and that is now on the record from the analyst's own mouth. No library file currently records it.

q06_c.headline: The two headline DNA statistics offered against Robinson — 1.7 octillion for item 7.1 (the towel swab) and 30 quintillion for item 8.1 (the screwdriver swab) — are, on their face and by the examiner's own testimony, conditional likelihood ratios that ASSUME Lance Twiggs is one of exactly two contributors, in both the numerator and the denominator. In this stretch the examiner testified that STRmix returned a likelihood ratio of ONE for her Twiggs comparison, which she classified as "uninformative" and which sits below her own stated threshold of 2 for even "limited support for inclusion." She assumed Twiggs in anyway, on visual inspection of the peaks plus the fact that the field had submitted him as an elimination sample. The State's cross did not revisit that assumption; it restated the two conditioned sentences verbatim and confirmed the DOJ-permitted descriptor.

findings.finding: ROLE ASSIGNMENT (functional, not label-based): Amanda Bakker was a DEFENCE-called witness taken out of order during the State's case. Michael Burt conducted DIRECT examination; Mr. McBride conducted CROSS for the State; Burt then redirect; McBride then recross. Basis: the defence announced 'out of order, the defense would be calling Amanda Bakker' (stream 05:14:22); the court on returning from recess said 'We are still with Mr. Burt and Ms. Baker on direct examination' (stream 07:03:46); McBride asked for time because 'I need to cross-examine this witness' (L8722); the court allowed 'the state the appropriate time for cross-examination' (L8726); and Burt said 'I'll save that for redirect' (L8858) BEFORE McBride's exam. Rev's labels happen to agree with content throughout this stretch, but the roles are established by content.
findings.locator: day2.txt L8722, L8726, L8858, L8866; plus char-offset 178307 (stream 05:14:22) and stream 07:03:46, both outside the assigned line range

findings.finding: WHAT '7.1' IS. '7.1' is NOT a figure or a statistic. It is an item designator — Item 7, sub 1 — identified on cross by State's counsel as 'the swabbing from the towel from the rifle' (L9095) and confirmed as 'item seven is the towel' (L9359-9363). The magnitude attached to item 7.1 is 1.7 octillion (1.7 x 10^27 on the short scale). Any prior note recording '7.1' as a figure has either recorded the item number as a magnitude or transposed the digits of '1.7'. The companion item 8.1 is the screwdriver swab (L9367-9371), with a magnitude of 30 quintillion.

WHAT THE 1.7 OCTILLION FIGURE IS CONDITIONED ON. Five conditions, all on the face of the record: (1) the mixture was interpreted as originating from exactly TWO individuals; (2) one of those two is ASSUMED to be Twiggs — Twiggs appears in BOTH competing propositions, so the statistic never tests whether Twiggs is there; (3) the numerator proposition is 'Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors'; (4) the denominator proposition is 'Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors' — 'unrelated' excludes relatives from the alternative; (5) the typing is length-based STR only, with no sequence (isoallele) resolution, which the examiner expressly conceded. The same five conditions attach to the 30 quintillion figure for item 8.1.
findings.locator: day2.txt L9119 and L9143 (restatements); original report paragraphs read into the record by an earlier State witness at stream 05:10:57 and 05:11:41 (char offsets 174333 / 175172), outside the assigned range; sequence concession at L8826

findings.finding: DOJ VERBAL-SCALE ANSWER #1 (defence direct, describing the scale chart on page five of the admitted FBI report). The examiner explained her report's 'verbal scale': alongside the numerical likelihood ratio she gives 'a qualitative or a verbal equivalent to that numerical value' (L8045), then described the bands (L8053). She confirmed that a likelihood ratio must reach TWO before even 'limited support for an inclusion' is available (L8057-8061).

DOJ VERBAL-SCALE ANSWER #2 (State cross). State's counsel established that the DOJ 'ULTR' directive limits the adjectives an examiner may use; that the philosophy is to publish the number and let the reader assign the descriptor; and that for BOTH the item 7.1 and the item 8.1 figures the only permitted descriptor is 'very strong support for inclusion.' The witness confirmed each. She rendered the acronym as 'Uniform Language for Reporting and Testimony, I believe' (L9067); on direct the same document had been named 'Department of Justice Uniform Language for Testimony and Reports for Forensic Autosomal DNA Examinations Using Probabilistic Genotyping Systems' (stream 05:28:09, outside range).

STRmix returned a likelihood ratio of ONE on the chart identified as her Twiggs comparison, which she classified as 'uninformative' — below her own stated threshold of 2 for even limited support. PRECISION CAVEAT: the record in this stretch does NOT specify which item (7 or 8) that chart pertains to. Defence counsel's follow-up premise assumed it covered 'both item seven and item eight' (L8113); the witness did not correct that premise but answered on other grounds — that she had not used the calculation to decide the question at all.

THE ASSUMED-CONTRIBUTOR MECHANISM, in the witness's own words. She testified she did NOT use the STRmix calculation to determine Twiggs was a contributor: she looked at the DNA data visually, saw that he had the peaks, and — because the field had submitted him as an elimination sample — assumed him as a contributor, then used him as an elimination when calculating the statistic for Robinson. She stated 'We don't have a threshold. I don't have to see two, four, eight peaks to determine I think an individual is present.' She distinguished suspects from elimination samples: for a suspect she first judges included/excluded and then runs STRmix 'to give weight to that inclusion.' On redirect she rejected the characterisation that she ignored STRmix: 'I did not ignore it.'

STEELMAN OF THE EXAMINER'S POSITION (logged per objectivity mechanics). Her account is internally coherent and is a recognised practice claim, not an improvisation: STRmix is run to give WEIGHT to an inclusion already judged plausible, not to make the include/exclude call; elimination samples are handled differently from suspects; and the Twiggs assumption sits in both propositions of the ratio, so it is not a simple thumb on the scale. Nothing in this stretch quantifies the direction or size of its effect on the Robinson statistic.

OVER-HEDGE GUARD (this one runs toward the State). The record in this stretch does NOT establish that assuming Twiggs inflated the Robinson likelihood ratio. No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was computed, offered, or even requested anywhere in lines 8050-9640. The defence attack was on the propriety of the assumption, not on a demonstrated numerical consequence, and no file should imply otherwise.

LOCI WHERE TWIGGS' ALLELES WERE NOT OBSERVED. Three were put to her and confirmed: at D16 Twiggs types (as rendered) '912' but sample eight yielded only a '12'; at D19S Twiggs types '1416' and no 16 allele was found in the '8A' sample; at TH01 ('THO') Twiggs types '79.3' and no 7 allele was found in the '8.1' sample. She explained these by mixture dropout, and said that at the TH01 locus only one individual was represented so she 'would essentially ignore that location.' She accepted the Butler-textbook single-locus exclusion rule only for SINGLE-SOURCE samples, expressly not for mixtures.

ALLELE-NOTATION GARBLE (recording-layer artifact). '912', '1416' and '79.3' are almost certainly the paired allele calls 9,12 / 14,16 / 7,9.3 run together by the transcription. Basis: counsel's own follow-ups treat them as two separate alleles ('did you find a 16 allele', 'did you find a seven allele'). No downstream file may treat '912' as a single allele call.

LOSEE BUILDING / NORTHEAST CORNER — SIX SWABS, CONSUMED, NO DNA. The witness confirmed that items 1 through 6 were swabs taken from the northeast corner of the building (transcribed 'the loci building' — a garble of 'Losee'; 'Losee' is spelled correctly 22 times elsewhere in day2). The six were listed as swabs from possible smudge, of hand swipe, from possible sweat drop, from possible smudge, of possible smudge, and from possible sweat drop. ALL SIX WERE CONSUMED, and she concluded there was NO DNA present on any of them, so no comparative testing was possible. Approximately three microliters of extract remained; she had used ten microliters for testing and testified she would expect the remaining three also to yield nothing. Cross-reference: earlier Day 2 testimony placed the shooter at the northeast corner of the Losee building 'preparing to jump' (L3548).
findings.locator: day2.txt L8418, L8438-8450, L8462-8482; garble comparison L808 / L3548 / L4504

findings.finding: CONSUMPTION / DESTRUCTIVE TESTING. She requested permission to consume before receiving any evidence and before seeing it. Consumed: items 1 through 6, plus item 54 (swabs of swiped finger areas) and item 55 (swabs of stairwell railing). She agreed the NRC 1996 report contains the passage about preserving a wrongfully accused person's opportunity to have testing repeated, and agreed her lab's standard 7.4 requires retaining or returning a portion of the sample or extract where possible — testifying that the residual extract liquid IS returned, she believed on all items. Defence counsel signalled he would contest that scope ('Well, we'll get to that in a minute') but the assigned range contains no follow-up.

ITEM 55 (STAIRWELL RAILING) — TWO SWABS COMBINED, CONSUMED, NO CONCLUSION POSSIBLE. She confirmed she combined two swabs into one sample and consumed the whole; she did not inquire whether they came from different areas of the railing (they were labelled from the same stairwell and packaged together); the result was 'DNA from more than five individuals, so I could not provide a conclusion.' FIDELITY NOTE: defence counsel's question embedded the premise 'where the suspect touched the railing' and the witness DECLINED it — 'As far as I know, they were swabs from a stairwell.' That refusal must survive into any file citing this passage.

BACKPACK — TWO COMPETING IN-LAB ATTRIBUTIONS. She testified the backpack (which she labelled Exhibit 9) and items from it were processed for DNA with no investigative information, and that 'as the investigation continues, it was determined that that backpack was potentially left behind by a bystander and there was no comparisons needed at that time.' Defence counsel put to her that her notes at page 20 read 'The backpack belongs to Kirk's detailees'; she answered that this was not her communication log but another person in the laboratory recording information they had received. She therefore has NO personal knowledge of either attribution — both are lab-recorded hearsay, and they do not agree with each other.

SEQUENCE / ISOALLELE CONCESSION. She confirmed she used length-based STR typing only: 'The FBI laboratory does not use sequencing for nuclear DNA testing, nor am I qualified in it.' NGS is used at her laboratory for mitochondrial DNA only. She agreed she cannot distinguish the evidence samples from Robinson on the basis of sequence differences at the charted loci (D3 allele 17 has variants 17A/17B/17C; vWA 18-19 has 18A/18B/19A/19B). She was 'not aware' whether the makers of STRmix also market a sequencing platform.

OBJECTION 1 AND RULING — defence chart 'Baker 34'. State's counsel objected: 'Unless this exhibit is reasonably likely to defeat the prima facie showing a probable cause, this is irrelevant to the preliminary hearing.' Argument followed (defence: it goes to the reliability of the report the State itself offered; State: this is effectively a Rule 702 hearing, the magistrate cannot weigh it, and the exhibit is not relevant without the testimony). The court ADMITTED the exhibit but cabined the inquiry: 'This is on the cusp of whether it is applicable to the probable cause standard... I still have to reign it in to keeping it to probable cause and not going into a full exploration.' Defence was limited to the four to five minutes it requested.

OBJECTION 2 AND RULING — defence chart 'Baker 35' (the isoallele version). 'Same objection, Your Honor.' The court admitted it 'under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34. It may be published.' EXHIBIT-NUMBER HAZARD CREATED BY THE RECORD ITSELF: counsel first moved it as 'Baker 34', a court staff member (labelled 'Speaker 10') twice corrected him to 'Baker 35', the court then asked 'And is this Baker 34?', and the admitting ruling as transcribed again says 'Baker 34.' The identity of the admitted second chart rests on its content (the isoallele chart), not on the number spoken.

OBJECTION 3 AND RULING — 2004 DOJ Inspector General report. On redirect, defence counsel asked about a 2004 Inspector General audit of the FBI DNA laboratory ('A Review of Protocol and Practice Vulnerabilities'). State: 'Objection. The 2004 study is hardly relevant to this proceeding 22 years later.' Court: 'I'll allow this single question as she may respond, so I'm overruling the objection.' The witness answered that she is not aware of that study. INCIDENTAL CALENDAR ANCHOR: 2004 + 22 = 2026, independently corroborating that this proceeding sits in 2026.

STATE CROSS — REHABILITATION CONTENT (logged as confirmation FOR the State). BS in biology, Salisbury University; FBI laboratory contractor in the Federal Convicted Offender Program about eighteen months; biologist in the DNA casework unit about six years; forensic examiner since 2015 (counsel's '11 years' is consistent with a 2026 hearing). Laboratory accredited by ANAB, audited every four years by an outside body. Two-year training programme, oral and written boards, moot-court exercises, competency exam; she is 'not certified... qualified as an examiner'; at least eight hours a year continuing education; external-vendor proficiency testing that tests both her and the laboratory process. Every case undergoes technical AND administrative review. STRmix validated both developmentally (by the creators, in a peer-reviewed study) and internally by the FBI laboratory; in use in approximately 120 laboratories domestically and internationally. Degradation: normal, universal, and it did not affect her conclusions on either the screwdriver or item 7.

ACTIVITY-LEVEL AND TIMING LIMITS, CONFIRMED ON THE STATE'S OWN CROSS. She agreed she cannot testify what precise action left the DNA on an object and cannot testify to the exact time it was left. She listed deposition routes as direct contact, body fluids, and secondary transfer ('if I were to touch an object and then that object is given to someone else, my DNA could potentially be on that other individual'). This is the most transportable limitation in the entire stretch, and it comes from the prosecution's examination, not the defence's.

MIXTURE PROPORTIONS AND A CONDITIONING-STRIPPING EVENT. On direct (stream 05:54:24, outside the assigned range) she said of item 7: 'For one of the runs when I compared to Mr. Robinson CONDITIONING ON MR. TWIGGS, it was a 5% to 95%.' On cross, State's counsel restated that as 'I believe that the minor contributor was less than 20% and that it was actually 5% and the ratio was 5% to 95%' — dropping the conditioning clause — and then asked whether '95% is assumed from the defendant, Robinson.' The witness did NOT adopt that framing; she answered in alignment language: 'Twiggs' DNA profile aligned with the 5% contributor and Mr. Robinson's DNA profile aligned better with the 95% contributor.' The word 'conditioning'/'conditioned' occurs exactly ONCE in all of day2.txt, in her own direct answer.
findings.locator: day2.txt L9327-9347; original at char offset 217513 (stream 05:54:24), outside the assigned range

findings.finding: COUNTER-WEIGHT ON THE SAME POINT (verify in both directions). When restating the two LIKELIHOOD-RATIO sentences, State's counsel did NOT strip the conditioning — he read both propositions verbatim, including 'if Twiggs and T Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown unrelated person are contributors.' The conditioning-stripping is confined to the mixture-proportion question and does not touch the headline statistic.

INTERNAL NUMERIC INCONSISTENCY IN ONE Q&A PAIR. State's counsel put item 8's proportions as '11% from the minor and 89% from the major'; the transcribed answer reads 'Twiggs better aligned with that 11% contributor and Mr. Robinson better aligned with that 79% contributor.' The earlier direct testimony gave 11% and approximately 89%. The '79%' is therefore almost certainly a transcription error for 89% — but a file quoting L9355 verbatim would propagate a wrong number.

VERBAL-SCALE BAND DUPLICATION (recording-layer defect). At L8053 the witness is transcribed assigning the SAME descriptor to two adjacent bands: 'greater than or equal to one million, I designate that as very strong support for inclusion. The next example, 10,000 to less than one million, I would say that's very strong support for inclusion and so forth.' Two adjacent bands on a graded scale cannot both carry the top descriptor. Either the witness misspoke or Rev duplicated the phrase. RESOLVING ARTEFACT: the scale chart is page five of the admitted FBI report, which would settle it; the transcript alone cannot.
findings.locator: day2.txt L8053; chart identified at L8029-8033

findings.finding: REDIRECT — PCAST EXCHANGE. Defence read two PCAST passages (experience and judgment cannot establish the validity of a metrological method; good professional practices — societies, certification, accreditation, peer review, protocols, proficiency testing, ethics codes — cannot substitute for evidence of validity). She disagreed with both, citing extensive validation and her own exposure to validation data. She could not identify Eric Lander: 'That name does not ring a bell.' On cross she had not known the report's year ('I think it was 2016, but I'm not entirely sure'). She said 31 laboratories submitted internal validation data in response to PCAST; defence read PCAST's stated response that it was 'unpersuaded by those studies,' and she agreed PCAST had addressed them. The transcript renders 'PCAST' throughout as 'PCAS'.

RECROSS AND EXCUSAL. State's recross was a single point: field casework has no known true answer, unlike ground-truth studies, and 'our validation' is in essence a ground-truth test — she agreed. Defence had nothing further. The court asked 'May this witness be excused?', defence assented, and the court said 'Thank you, Ms. Baker. You may step down.' Neither side requested the benefit of the record.
findings.locator: day2.txt L9524-9593 (witness steps down at L9577)

findings.finding: CLOSE OF DAY 2. The court adjourned to 1:00 PM the following day: 'We do not have morning court for this proceeding and we'll start up at 1:00 PM in the afternoon.' TRANSCRIPT-INTEGRITY NOTE: the sentence terminates mid-clause — 'The court is in' — and the file runs straight into Rev site boilerplate at L9599. Day 2's transcript is truncated at the final word.

SPOKEN CLOCK REFERENCES IN THIS STRETCH (recording layer, not derived from timestamps). The court said 'we are at the 4:30 point' and later 'we are now at 4:40'; State's counsel said 'It's 5:00. I'm going to wrap up.' These are statements ON the record about time of day and are usable as such. They are NOT conversions of the recording-stream timestamps and must not be used to construct one.

'PART 13 OF 14 ENDS [07:56:04]' falls at L9039, again mid-answer, with 'developmentally and internally' duplicated. Any quotation crossing either seam will double words unless normalised.

q06_c.both_directions: CUTS FOR THE STATE: (1) The examiner's qualifications, her laboratory's ANAB accreditation and four-yearly external audits, the two-year training programme, the mandatory technical AND administrative review of every case, external proficiency testing, and STRmix's developmental (peer-reviewed) plus internal validation and use in roughly 120 laboratories all went in essentially unrebutted. (2) She testified affirmatively that degradation did not impair her conclusions on either item. (3) When State's counsel restated the two headline likelihood ratios he read BOTH propositions verbatim, conditioning clause intact — no sleight of hand at the point that matters most. (4) Her assumed-contributor account is a coherent statement of a recognised practice, not an improvisation: STRmix weights an inclusion already judged plausible rather than making the include/exclude call; elimination samples are handled differently from suspects; and the Twiggs term sits in both numerator and denominator, so it is not a simple thumb on the scale. (5) Critically, and against this project's reflex to hedge toward the defence: NOTHING in this stretch shows the Twiggs assumption inflated the Robinson number. No unconditioned alternative was computed, offered, or requested. The defence attacked the propriety of the assumption, never its numerical consequence — and a file that implies otherwise would be committing the over-hedge error this project has already had to correct three times. (6) The defence's redirect gambits largely failed on their own terms: the 2004 Inspector General question was allowed and produced only 'No, I'm not [aware]', which impeaches the witness's reading, not the science. (7) The court twice signalled that this whole line sits at or past the edge of the probable-cause standard and expressly reserved reliability for a later expert hearing. CUTS AGAINST THE STATE: (1) The headline statistics are conditional, and the condition is an assumption the examiner made by eye after her own software returned a likelihood ratio of ONE for Twiggs — 'uninformative' on her own scale and below the value of 2 she said is needed for even 'limited support'. (2) There are at least three loci (D16, D19S, TH01) where Twiggs' alleles were not observed in the item-8 data, explained by dropout or set aside as single-contributor locations. (3) Six swabs from the northeast corner of the Losee building were consumed and produced NO DNA at all, with roughly three microliters of extract remaining against ten used — effectively no retest, and nothing to compare to anyone. (4) The stairwell-railing swabs were combined, consumed, and produced more than five contributors and no conclusion. (5) She conceded she uses length-based typing only, cannot resolve isoalleles, is not qualified in sequencing, and cannot distinguish Robinson from other sequence variants at the charted loci. (6) On the State's OWN cross she confirmed she cannot say what action deposited the DNA or when. (7) She could not identify Eric Lander, did not know the PCAST year, and was unaware of the 2004 Inspector General report — which goes to her command of the reliability literature she was being questioned on, though not to the validity of the underlying science. NET, and stated narrowly: the DNA statistics offered at this hearing are conditional on an assumption the examiner reached OUTSIDE her probabilistic software, and the record in this stretch neither validates that assumption nor quantifies its effect. What would change this: the report itself (pages three and five), and any STRmix run for Robinson that does not condition on Twiggs.

findings.finding: SECOND RULING, previously unknown to the library — the defence was denied live cross-examination of Lance Twiggs at the preliminary hearing. The defence applied under Utah Code § 77-21-3 to certify an out-of-state subpoena compelling Twiggs from Texas; his counsel had declined to accept service. The State opposed and moved to quash. Held: application DENIED, motion to quash GRANTED, expressly WITHOUT PREJUDICE and renewable if the State's presentation materially differs from its proffer. Reasoning rests on Rule 14A(2) reasonableness, Rule 7B, and State v. Lopez as persuasive rather than governing. The court recorded that the State did not intend to call Twiggs live and would proceed by a video-recorded Rule 1102 interview plus electronic messages, a handwritten note and other corroboration.

THIRD ITEM bearing on the forensic record. Defence counsel Michael Burt stated on the record that the defence had arranged SEVEN forensic witnesses for the preliminary hearing — six federal examiners to fly from the East Coast plus one in-state — to meet the State's hearsay reports, which he identified as 'exhibits 30 through 34.' He asked the court to resolve their admissibility before the hearing or at latest after the State's prima facie case, to avoid the cost of flying six people. The court set it tentatively for 2026-06-26 and undertook to hear it before the prelim. This bears on Q-44 (State's Exhibits 32 and 34) and on Q-49 (whether the defence case ever reached its subject matter).

A FOURTH PROCEEDING is named and set on this record: 2026-06-26 at 8:30 a.m., for the order-to-show-cause ruling plus the electronic-media-in-the-courtroom motion, tentatively plus the forensic-experts question. transcripts.both_directions:
"CUTS FOR THE STATE. The 2026-06-22 rulings went the State's way on both contested motions: the defence's constitutional attack on reliable hearsay at a preliminary hearing was denied outright, and its attempt to compel Lance Twiggs' live testimony was denied with the State's motion to quash granted. The court's stated reasoning is conventional Utah preliminary-hearing doctrine (Timmerman, Lopez, Schmidt, Ramirez, Rule 14A(2)), not an outlier. On the 06-26 contempt matter the State also largely prevailed on remedy: the sanction the defence actually wanted — striking the death penalty — was refused as 'grossly disproportionate,' and what issued instead was procedural (jury questionnaires, possibly a larger pool). Separately, a Run 1 weakness now resolves in the State's favour: the 2026-07-28 filing of its opening brief, previously carried on a single Fox source, has a second independent outlet as of 2026-07-29. And on the transcript's own quality, the over-hedging trap is live: this document's speaker labels are broadly sound, and treating them with Day-1-grade suspicion would be a defect running against the State's witnesses and the court alike.

CUTS AGAINST THE STATE. A prosecutor on this case was found in CIVIL CONTEMPT on 2026-06-26 for violating a pretrial publicity order — reportedly by commenting on the strength of the State's evidence while correcting a ballistics report, in a case where 'no evidence of a second shooter' is itself a contested public claim. That is an adverse judicial finding against the prosecution team, and it is entirely absent from this library. The court also recorded that the State did not intend to call Twiggs live at all, proceeding instead by video-recorded Rule 1102 interview — so the man whose statements underwrite the confession, the concealed weapon, the disposed clothing and the witness-tampering count was never subject to cross-examination at the preliminary hearing, over an express defence application to compel him, and the DNA likelihoods in CR-E03 are conditioned on him. The court itself flagged the fragility of its own ruling by making the denial WITHOUT PREJUDICE and renewable. And the defence had seven forensic examiners arranged against the State's Exhibits 30-34.

CUTS AGAINST THE LIBRARY, which matters most here. The inventory was not merely incomplete — it was unaware that a whole pre-hearing motions phase existed. Three proceedings (2026-06-12, 06-22, 06-26) were missing, one of them decided the evidentiary regime the entire preliminary hearing then ran under. Run 1 reported 'seven Rev pages of this case positively identified'; the sitemap shows more Kirk-adjacent pages than that, so Run 1's enumeration was sound for court proceedings but incomplete overall. Finally, Rev's page metadata misdescribed a proceeding for a SECOND time, and this project has already been burned once by exactly that (D-51). The correct posture toward Rev's blurbs is now established twice over: they are a claimant, and the transcript is the record."
